signals.title: Adaptive lazy execution of short-circuit function arguments (continues #73776)
signals.text: This continues #73776 by @lgbo-ustc, whose branch was ~17 months behind `master` and could no longer be merged mechanically (27 conflicting files in the hottest central code). The author's commits are preserved; on top of them this reconciles the change with the current `master` and reworks the plumbing. Short-circuit evaluation decides *statically* which arguments of `and`, `or`, `if` and `multiIf` are executed lazily. Lazy execution is not free: the rows which are not needed are filtered out and the result is expanded back to the original size. When the filtered out part is small, or the argument itself is cheap, this overhead is larger than the work it saves. This adds an opt-in adaptive mode: the execution of every function is profiled (elapsed time and processed rows), and every 20000 rows the decision is revisited per action - lazy execution is turned off when the estimated cost of the full execution is lower than the measured cost of the lazy execution, and turned back on when the per-row cost of the action grows significantly. Actions whose function can throw an exception on invalid input values (for example `intDiv(1, 0)`) are never switched to eager execution, so the short-circuit protection is preserved. The mode is disabled by default and enabled with the new experimental setting `enable_adaptive_short_circuit_lazy_execution`. Changes on top of the original branch: * The flag no longer travels through `ExpressionStep`/`FilterStep` constructors, the query plan optimizations, the planner and the step serialization. It lives in `ExpressionActionsSettings` next to `enable_lazy_columns_replication`, which removes ~20 files from the change and all the ripple through `QueryPlan/Optimizations`. * `ExpressionActions::execute` and `executeOnColumns` stay `const`; the free `executeAction` became a member with three virtual hooks (`shouldExecuteLazily`, `executeFunction`, `finalizeBlockExecution`) which `AdaptiveExpressionActions` overrides. * The profile plumbing follows the current `IExecutableFunction` chain, including `executeWithoutReplicatedColumns`, which did not exist when the branch was written. * `is_no_except` is computed only when the setting is enabled, so nothing changes for the default path. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Added an experimental setting `enable_adaptive_short_circuit_lazy_execution`, which enables dynamic evaluation of whether a short-circuit function's argument should be lazily executed. The execution of the functions is profiled at runtime, and the lazy execution of an argument is disabled when it costs more than executing the argument on all the rows. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/73776 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114734&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114734](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114734+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Remove `WINDOW VIEW`
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/61069 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113493 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114097 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/75191 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/88706 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `WINDOW VIEW` feature is removed, together with the `WATCH` statement and the `windowID` function. It has been non-functional since version 24.12 (inserts into the source table were silently not delivered to window views) and was never supported by the analyzer, which is enabled by default since 24.3. The settings `allow_experimental_window_view`, `window_view_clean_interval`, `window_view_heartbeat_interval`, and `wait_for_window_view_fire_signal_timeout` are kept as obsolete no-ops. The time-window functions `tumble`, `tumbleStart`, `tumbleEnd`, `hop`, `hopStart`, and `hopEnd` are kept. If you still have window views defined, drop them before upgrading: a server that finds a window view in its metadata fails to start (`Cannot parse definition from metadata file ... (SYNTAX_ERROR)`), the same way the removal of the `Lazy` database engine behaves. Similar functionality will be reimplemented on top of streaming queries (issue [#114738](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738)). The removal, in detail: - `src/Storages/WindowView/` (`StorageWindowView`, `WindowViewSource`, `StorageBlocks`), `WatermarkTransform`, the `ParserCreateWindowViewQuery` parser, and the whole `WATCH` statement stack (`ParserWatchQuery`, `ASTWatchQuery`, `InterpreterWatchQuery`, the `IStorage::watch` virtual) — window views were the last implementor of `watch`, and the `WATCH` statement was already documented as deprecated. - The `ASTCreateQuery` watermark/lateness fields and their AST JSON serialization and validation. The `clickhouse_json` boundary fails closed rather than silently reinterpreting legacy payloads: `ASTCreateQuery::readJSON` rejects a set `is_window_view`, watermark strategy or `allowed_lateness` flag and the `watermark_function` / `lateness_function` children (otherwise such a payload deserialized as an ordinary `CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT` and was executed as an immediate-population table create), while `ASTViewTargets::readJSON` rejects the `Inner` target kind, which nothing produces any more and which formatted back to parser-impossible `INNER ENGINE ...` SQL. Both are covered by `04892_ast_json_removed_window_view_state`; the `PushingToWindowViewSink` and `ViewType::WINDOW` branches in `InsertDependenciesBuilder`; window-view special cases in `InterpreterCreateQuery`, `InterpreterInsertQuery`, `StorageFactory`, `DatabaseOrdinary`, `DatabaseReplicated`, `DDLDependencyVisitor`, `QueryFuzzer`, BuzzHouse, and the ArrowFlight table-type mapping. - The `windowID` function and the `UInt32` single-argument forms of `tumbleStart`/`tumbleEnd`/`hopStart`/`hopEnd` (they only accepted `windowID` output). The rest of the time-window function family stays, since these are ordinary functions usable in a regular `GROUP BY` and are exactly the vocabulary for the streaming-queries replacement. - The keywords `WATCH`, `EVENTS`, `ALLOWED_LATENESS`, and `STRICTLY_ASCENDING` (the `WATERMARK` keyword stays: the streaming-queries `WATERMARK FOR` clause uses it), the error code `QUERY_IS_NOT_SUPPORTED_IN_WINDOW_VIEW`, and the corresponding fuzzer dictionary and ANTLR grammar entries. - Kept for compatibility: `QueryViewsLogElement::ViewType::WINDOW` (so existing `system.query_views_log` tables keep their schema) and `ViewTarget::Inner` (so old DDL log entries still parse), following the same pattern as the `LIVE VIEW` removal. - The `allow_experimental_window_view` constraint in `tests/docker_scripts/stress_tests.lib` is kept (only the constraint, not the profile value, which would mark an obsolete setting as changed and add a `system.warnings` entry): the upgrade check runs the previous release's suite under the previous release's binary, whose window-view tests are not dropped afterwards because `--upgrade-check` implies `--fake-drop`, and the leftover metadata would then stop the new server from starting. - Tests: the four remaining window-view tests are removed. The pure time-window-function coverage of `01049_window_view_window_functions` moved to a new `04891_time_window_functions` test, which also pins the new `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` behavior of `tumbleStart(UInt32)`. - Docs: the `Window View` section of `CREATE VIEW`, the `WATCH` page (with its navigation entries and locale twins) are removed and the old-slug redirects retargeted; the window-view entries are removed from the generated settings/functions reference pages (second commit, hence the `pr-autogenerated-docs` label): the `window-view.mdx` settings page, the four settings' entries in the pages/manifest/navigation/settings explorer, and the `windowID` section of `time-window-functions.mdx`. The unrelated drift accumulated on master since the last nightly regeneration is deliberately not included; the nightly docs-autogen job will pick it up. Why now: the feature has been non-functional since Dec 2024 — commit `ceae84c87a2` removed the explicit view-dependency registration and `DDLDependencyVisitor` never extracted the source table of a `CREATE WINDOW VIEW`, so inserts into the source table were silently not pushed to window views, and direct inserts failed with `std::out_of_range` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113493). Nobody noticed for ~1.5 years. It was never ported to the analyzer (with `enable_analyzer = 1`, the default, existing window views load permanently inert), its tests were removed in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/73822 because they were inherently flaky, and it kept costing triage time (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114097 is a recent server SIGSEGV through `getSourceTableSelectQuery`). The full assessment, including the plan for reimplementing this functionality on top of streaming queries (`SELECT ... FROM t STREAM`, `WATERMARK FOR`, emit-on-watermark windowed aggregation), is in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114747&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114747](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114747+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Speed up window functions by evaluating each `MergeTree` partition independently
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108326 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114645 A window function plan sorts its input partitioned by the window `PARTITION BY` columns: every row is reshuffled across streams by `ScatterByPartitionTransform` (a hash pass over the `PARTITION BY` columns plus a repack of every column of every row through a full cross-stream `Resize`), so that whole window partitions land in single streams before the per-stream sort and `WindowTransform`. If the partition expression of the `MergeTree` table is a deterministic function of the window `PARTITION BY` columns, the reading will now emit each partition through a single port instead: every stream already carries whole window partitions, so the scatter is skipped entirely and the read, sort, and window all stay within per-partition streams. ```sql CREATE TABLE test_16 (a UInt64, b UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple() PARTITION BY sipHash64(a) % 16; INSERT INTO test_16 SELECT number % 100000, number FROM numbers_mt(30000000); OPTIMIZE TABLE test_16 FINAL; EXPLAIN PIPELINE SELECT a, sum(b) OVER (PARTITION BY a ORDER BY b) FROM test_16 SETTINGS allow_window_partitions_independently = 1, max_threads = 16; ``` ```response (Expression) ExpressionTransform × 16 (Window) Resize 16 → 16 WindowTransform × 16 (Sorting) MergeSortingTransform × 16 LimitsCheckingTransform × 16 PartialSortingTransform × 16 <- was: fed through Resize 16 → 1 + ScatterByPartitionTransform 1 → 16, reshuffling every row across streams (Expression) ExpressionTransform × 16 (ReadFromMergeTree) MergeTreeSelect(pool: ReadPoolInOrder, algorithm: InOrder) × 16 0 → 1 <- per-partition reading (16 partitions → 16 streams) ``` On `test_str_64 (a UInt64, b UInt64, s String)` with 30M rows, 100k window partitions over 64 balanced table partitions (`PARTITION BY sipHash64(a) % 64`), and a 100-byte random string in `s`, at `max_threads = 16`: | query | off | on | speedup | |--------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------|--------|---------| | `SELECT a, s, count(b) OVER (PARTITION BY a) FROM test_str_64` | 1.014s | 0.554s | 1.83× | | `SELECT a, s, sum(b) OVER (PARTITION BY a ORDER BY b) FROM test_str_64` | 1.492s | 0.956s | 1.56× | The scatter repacks every column of every row, so the win grows with the row width. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up window functions on partitioned `MergeTree` tables by reading each partition through its own stream and evaluating the windows per partition, skipping the hash scatter that ordinarily reshuffles every row across threads before the window sort. This applies when the table partition expression is a deterministic function of the window `PARTITION BY` columns and is gated by the same cost heuristic as per-partition `GROUP BY` / `DISTINCT` (enough partitions relative to `max_threads`, no dominant partition). Controlled by the new settings `allow_window_partitions_independently` (enabled by default), `force_window_partitions_independently`, and `max_number_of_partitions_for_independent_window`. --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114783&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114783](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114783+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)]

signals.title: Propagate OpenTelemetry trace context into AsyncTaskExecutor fibers
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112738 The OpenTelemetry trace context is stored in a `FiberLocal`, but the fibers created by `AsyncTaskExecutor` (`ConnectionEstablisherAsync`, `PacketReceiver`, `RemoteQueryExecutorReadContext`) started with an empty fiber-local context. Remote queries of a distributed query were parented directly to the trace context supplied by the client, bypassing the spans of the initiator, and no spans were produced for the async tasks themselves. ## Changes - `AsyncTaskExecutor` captures `OpenTelemetry::CurrentContext()` on the thread that constructs it and installs a `TracingContextHolder` inside the fiber routine. This seeds the fiber-local context from the creating query and opens one span per task execution, named after the executor (`ConnectionEstablisherAsync`, `PacketReceiver`, `RemoteQueryExecutorReadContext`). It is a no-op when tracing is not enabled. - `FiberLocal` is now a per-type singleton (obtained via `FiberLocal<T>::instance`, the constructor is private). The address of the single object keys the per-fiber data, so a fiber suspended on one thread and resumed on another resolves to the same data. ## Span hierarchy change Remote queries now descend from the initiator through the `Connection::sendQuery` CLIENT span instead of appearing as direct children of the client-supplied trace context: ``` client span └─ query (initiator) └─ Connection::sendQuery [CLIENT] └─ query (remote server) ``` The expectations of `01455_opentelemetry_distributed` are updated accordingly: only the initial query span is now a direct child of the input trace context. A new test `04869_opentelemetry_async_remote_query_spans` covers the async paths, including `use_hedged_requests=1` (asserting `ConnectionEstablisherAsync` and `PacketReceiver` spans) and fiber cancellation. This is the first part of the distributed tracing improvements discussed in the linked issue ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Propagate the OpenTelemetry trace context into the fibers used for asynchronous connection establishment and remote query execution (hedged requests, `async_socket_for_remote`, `async_query_sending_for_remote`). Spans of remote queries in a distributed query are now correctly parented under the initiator's `Connection::sendQuery` span instead of being attached directly to the client-supplied trace context, and each asynchronous task execution produces its own span.

signals.title: Prometheus HTTP API: implement /api/v1/series
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - **Experimental Feature** ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ****Prometheus HTTP API:** implement **`/api/v1/series`** for **`TimeSeries`** tables.** ### Why this matters **Prometheus clients** use **`/api/v1/series`** to discover the label sets stored for active series. This endpoint is used by **Prometheus-compatible tools** such as **Grafana** when they need to populate metric and label selectors. ClickHouse **`TimeSeries` tables** can store labels in the main **`tags` Map**, in dedicated columns configured with **`tags_to_columns`**, or in a mixture of both layouts. The endpoint needs to expose the **same logical series** regardless of how those labels are stored. ### Description This PR adds **Prometheus `/api/v1/series` support** for **`TimeSeries` tables**. The endpoint is available through both a **dedicated `/api/v1/series` handler** and the **combined `/api/v1` handler**. It supports **GET requests** and **`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` POST requests**. Supported parameters: - **`match[]`** selects series by metric name and label matchers. Repeated parameters are combined as a **union** and overlapping results are returned only once through **deduplication**. - **`start` and `end`** select series overlapping the requested **time range**. - **`limit`** limits the number of returned series and reports when the response was **truncated**. ### Changes - **Selector parsing:** parse Prometheus series selectors with equality, inequality, regular-expression, and negative regular-expression matchers. - **Storage compatibility:** support metric names, labels in the **`tags` Map**, dedicated tag columns, and mixed rows that use both storage layouts. - **Label normalization:** normalize missing labels to the **Prometheus empty-value semantics** and include the full logical label set in each response. - **PromQL compatibility:** support quoted label names and anchor regular expressions to the **complete label value**. - **Input validation:** validate selectors and timestamps before executing the query. - **Time ranges:** apply the time-range filter when trusted min/max data is available. When it is not available, keep the request valid and return the **compatible candidate superset** allowed by the Prometheus API. - **Result limits:** support zero and positive limits, exact-limit responses, truncation reporting, and invalid-value errors. - **Access control:** read the underlying series metadata through the **`TimeSeries` table-function path** after checking access to the configured **`TimeSeries` table**. Unknown routes are resolved before authorization, so they keep the normal **404 response**. - **Existing endpoints:** apply the configured **`TimeSeries` table access boundary** consistently to the existing Prometheus query endpoints. - **Query lifecycle:** run the generated query through the **normal query pipeline** and keep **query logging** and **query completion handling** intact. ### Tests Added integration coverage for: - **Matcher operators:** metric-name and label selectors with all matcher operators. - **Repeated selectors:** repeated **`match[]`** parameters, selector unions, and overlapping-result deduplication. - **Storage layouts:** Map labels, dedicated tag columns, missing labels, mixed carriers, conflicting carriers, and **`__name__`**. - **Regex and names:** quoted label names and whole-value regular-expression anchoring. - **Selector validation:** invalid and unbounded selectors, including the valid **`{host!~".*"}`** case. - **Time ranges:** two-sided, one-sided, inclusive, and invalid time ranges. - **Min/max behavior:** requests with and without trusted min/max metadata. - **Limits:** zero, exact, positive, maximum, and invalid **`limit`** values. - **HTTP methods:** GET and form POST requests. - **Authorization:** wrapper-only **`SELECT` grants**, access checks for all query endpoint families, and unknown-route handling. - **Observability:** query completion records and the existing query API limit behavior. Also ran **Python syntax checks** and **`git diff --check`**. ### Documentation **Documentation is written.** The **TimeSeries engine documentation** now covers the Prometheus handler configuration and the **`/api/v1/series` endpoint parameters**. ### Stack This is the **base PR** for the follow-up Prometheus API endpoints: - **#114868** adds **`/api/v1/labels`**. - **#114869** adds **`/api/v1/label/<name>/values`**. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114867&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114867](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114867+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Follow-ups for CREATE HANDLER: parse limits of the stored query, docs, refactoring
signals.text: Follow-ups from https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106231 (`CREATE HANDLER`). Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106231 **Requested in review of #106231:** - The two predicates over `IAST::QueryKind` that describe the `readonly` mode - whether a query of that kind is rejected under it, and whether `readonly = 2` still lets it produce side effects - moved out of `SQLDefinedHandlerFromAST` into `Interpreters/QueryKindUnderReadonly.h`; `queryKindRequiresMutatingMethod` is renamed to `isQueryKindRejectedUnderReadonly` after the property it reports. The handler code keeps the statement-level refinements and the HTTP-method fences. - `currentHandler` and `currentRequestURL` were registered with `IntroducedIn` 26.6 (the development version when they were written); they are released in 26.8. **The one unresolved review finding:** a request could still lower the parse limits of a handler's query. `HTTPHandler::processQuery` relaxed `max_parser_depth` / `max_parser_backtracks` *before* applying the settings the request supplies, and a request names settings freely - so `GET /h?max_parser_depth=1` put the caller's value back and broke a handler the server itself had accepted. The relaxation now happens after the request settings. `max_query_size` had the same hole and did not even need a hostile request: a stored query longer than its default value is creatable and reloadable (both parse without a size limit) but failed on every invocation; it is now raised to fit the query text - not disabled, because `executeQuery` also uses `max_query_size` to decide how much of the request stream to read ahead in search of the query text, where `0` would make it read a single byte. It moves to `docs/reference/statements/create/handler.mdx`, with the frontmatter and internal links converted to that tree's conventions and the page registered in `docs/reference/navigation.json`. `docs/en/operations/system-tables/handlers.md` was a leftover copy of the generated `docs/reference/system-tables/handlers.mdx` whose hand-written `SHOW HANDLERS` / secret-masking paragraph had been lost; that paragraph is restored and the legacy copy deleted. signals.title: AI functions: Make quotas per query not per block
signals.text: `AIQuotaTracker` was a stack local inside `executeImpl`, so every block and every pipeline stream started with a fresh allowance. The `ai_function_max_api_calls_per_query`, `ai_function_max_input_tokens_per_query` and `ai_function_max_output_tokens_per_query` limits therefore scaled with the data (one allowance per block per function) instead of bounding the query — any limit above the largest block's row count could never fire. The tracker is now a single instance owned by the query `Context` and shared by every AI function call in that context, with atomic counters for the concurrent pipeline threads. The API-call limit is claimed with an atomic bounded reservation, so it is an exact cap within a query-execution context even under `max_threads > 1`; the token limits are best-effort, since a call's token usage is known only after its response arrives. The limits are enforced per server / query fragment: a distributed query (across shards or parallel-replica fragments) enforces them independently on each, not summed globally. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The AI-function quota settings (`ai_function_max_api_calls_per_query`, `ai_function_max_input_tokens_per_query`, `ai_function_max_output_tokens_per_query`) were enforced per block rather than per query, letting a query exceed the configured limit in proportion to the number of blocks and threads processed. They now bound the whole query per server: the API-call limit is an exact cap (atomic reservation), and the token limits are best-effort. A distributed query enforces the limits independently on each participating server / fragment. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114885&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114885](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114885+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix AI functions embedding counters behavior on error
signals.text: `aiEmbed` and `aiSimilarity` under-report provider usage in `system.query_log` when a request fails: with the default `ai_function_throw_on_error = 1` the exception row shows `AIAPICalls = 0` and `AIInputTokens = 0`, although the provider was called and billed. Flipping only that setting records the call: | `ai_function_throw_on_error` | `AIAPICalls` | `AIRowsSkipped` | |---|---:|---:| | `1` (default) | 0 | 0 | | `0` | 1 | 1 | Same query and endpoint, with `ai_function_max_retries = 0` so exactly one attempt is made. **Cause.** `embedTexts` accumulates the counters in a local `EmbeddingResult` and returns it by value. When a failed request rethrows, `return` is never reached: the local is destroyed while unwinding and the caller's `embedding_result` is never constructed, so the caller's `ProfileEvents::increment` calls are both skipped and left with nothing to read. That defeats the intent stated at the accumulation site, which counts `api_calls` *before* issuing the request so that failed calls are still counted. **Fix.** `embedTexts` now reports `AIAPICalls` and `AIInputTokens` itself, from a `SCOPE_EXIT` guard, so the normal and throwing exits both publish them. They are plain locals rather than fields of `EmbeddingResult`, so no caller can count them twice. Callers keep their own row counters, which mean different things: texts for `aiEmbed`, pairs of texts for `aiSimilarity`. **Not covered.** Row counters are still dropped when the query throws. It delivered no rows, and preserving them would need `embedTexts` to take an out-parameter in both callers. **Tests.** Three integration tests, each verified to fail with the source reverted to `master`: one per caller for `AIAPICalls`, plus one driving the quota-exceeded throw so a batch succeeds first and `AIInputTokens` is non-zero. The failed-request tests cannot cover `AIInputTokens`, since there the first request fails and no tokens are consumed. The same defect on the text-generation path is fixed in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111830, which is what introduced a throwing path there. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111830 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `aiEmbed` and `aiSimilarity` reporting zero `AIAPICalls` in `system.query_log` when a provider request failed, and losing `AIInputTokens` already consumed by earlier successful batches. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114905&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114905](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114905+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Make a table read by a scalar subquery in a CONSTRAINT a loading dependency
signals.text: Attaching a table analyzes its constraints in `InterpreterCreateQuery::getConstraintsDescription`, and the analysis executes the scalar subqueries of a constraint expression. The tables such a subquery reads were not registered as loading dependencies, because `DDLLoadingDependencyVisitor` only looks at functions, dictionary sources and the storage definition. Nothing prevented dropping such a table, and the server did not start afterwards - attaching the dependent table threw `UNKNOWN_TABLE` and loading the metadata failed: ```sql CREATE TABLE t1 (id UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); CREATE TABLE t2 (conversation UInt64, CONSTRAINT c CHECK (SELECT id FROM t1 LIMIT 15) IN (conversation)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); DROP TABLE t1; -- accepted, and the server cannot start anymore ``` The referential dependency was recorded, since `DDLDependencyVisitor` visits `ASTTableExpression`, so `check_referential_table_dependencies = 1` rejected the `DROP`. But that setting is off by default, and it is the loading graph that the default `check_table_dependencies` check and the `DROP DATABASE` drop order (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/97057) use. A constraint declaration is now visited, and the tables of every subquery that the analysis executes are added to the loading dependencies. Subqueries which the analysis does not execute - the right argument of `IN` and the argument of `exists`, see `ExecuteScalarSubqueriesMatcher::visit` - are skipped, because what they read is needed only when the constraint is checked, not to attach the table. That keeps `02916_joinget_dependency`-style patterns working, in particular `02841_not_ready_set_constraints`, which drops the table read by an `x IN (SELECT ...)` constraint on purpose. Seen in CI as a `Cannot start clickhouse-server` stress failure, e.g. https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110231&sha=4de836223549fd5224ca017b8c1a28e344ce38e9&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_msan%29 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114918 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/87369 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A table read by a scalar subquery inside a `CONSTRAINT` is now a loading dependency of the table that declares the constraint. Previously such a table could be dropped, after which the server did not start, because attaching the dependent table executes the subquery. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114923&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114923](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114923+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix reading a tuple element through a positional Tuple structure hint
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114991 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114991 Reading a tuple element through a positional structure hint returned default values instead of the file's data. Over a Parquet file written as `t Tuple(x UInt64, y String)`: ```sql SELECT tupleElement(t, 1) FROM file('p.parquet', Parquet, 't Tuple(UInt64, String)'); -- returned 0, 0, 0 instead of 0, 1, 2 ``` `WHERE tupleElement(t, 1) = 1` matched no rows, and with `input_format_parquet_allow_missing_columns = 0` the query failed with `THERE_IS_NO_COLUMN`. Silent wrong results, on default settings. Root cause: an unnamed tuple names its elements `1`, `2`, ..., so `optimize_functions_to_subcolumns` rewrote `tupleElement(t, 1)` to the subcolumn `t.1`. The existing guards there consult the storage snapshot, which is built from the structure argument and does contain `t.1`. The Parquet reader then resolves a flattened element name by string against the file's real field names `t.x`, `t.y`, found no match, and substituted a missing column filled with defaults. The fix suppresses the rewrite when the element name is a bare ordinal and the source resolves subcolumn names against a file schema. Named hints keep their pushdown, and storages serving subcolumns from their own metadata (MergeTree and friends) are unaffected. This regressed in #113383 and is master-only: that merge is an ancestor of no release branch and is in no release tag, hence `Not for changelog`. That category also skips `Bugfix validation`, so the reddening check below is the evidence. Validated on a Debug build, with a regression arm added to `04706_tuple_subcolumn_pushdown_parquet`: - Reddening: removing only the new guard term makes the new arm fail while the pre-existing arms stay green. - Preservation: `t.x` pushdown survives for a named hint by name and by ordinal, and `t.1` still pushes down for MergeTree's unnamed tuple. - `04706`, `04707`, `04708`, `04873` pass; a `subcolumn`/`tuple_element`/`functions_to_subcolumns` sweep has no failure absent from an unmodified-master control; 50 randomized runs pass. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115000&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115000](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115000+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Read all summed columns for SELECT FINAL from SummingMergeTree
signals.text: `SELECT ... FINAL` from a `SummingMergeTree` table returned wrong results when the query read only a subset of the columns of the summation. A merge removes a row when the values in **all** of the columns of the summation are zero after summing. The FINAL read applied the same rule, but only over the columns the query happened to read. Two ways to misbehave follow from that: - A query reading a subset of the summed columns removed every group whose visible columns summed to zero, even though an unread summed column made the row survive a real merge — rows silently disappeared. The most common victim is bare `count()`, which reads a single smallest column (plus the internally added sorting key): on a table `(c0 Int8, c1 Int32, c3 UInt64) ENGINE = SummingMergeTree ORDER BY c3` with two overlapping parts where `c0` sums to zero for some keys, `SELECT count() FROM t FINAL` returned 10 instead of 15, and `SELECT c0, c3 FROM t FINAL` lost the same 5 rows. - A query reading none of the summed columns (e.g. only the sorting key) never removed anything, keeping rows that a real merge deletes. The fix always includes all columns that a merge would aggregate into the FINAL read set (and into the set protected from plan-level column pruning), so the removal decision is taken over the same set of columns as in a real merge. This makes `SELECT ... FINAL` agree with `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` followed by a plain `SELECT`. Note that queries over `SummingMergeTree FINAL` that previously read a subset of the summed columns now read all of them, which is the price of the correct result. Found by the nightly SQLancer `FinalMerge` oracle (`SELECT count() FROM t0 FINAL` returned 9947 before `OPTIMIZE TABLE t0 FINAL` and 9999 after it on the same data): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=5c9f28ed5a2c585ad46bf74d6600cdcf3aa07a9e&name_0=NightlySQLancer&name_1=SQLancer%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29&name_1=SQLancer ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong results of `SELECT ... FINAL` from `SummingMergeTree` when the query reads only a subset of the columns of the summation: the decision to remove a row whose sums are all zero is now taken over all columns of the summation, as in a real merge, instead of only the columns the query reads. Previously, rows could silently disappear from the result (for example, `SELECT count() FROM table FINAL`). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115032&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115032](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115032+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Offer the `/`-commands of the client, and name them when misspelled
signals.text: Typing `/` at the beginning of the input now shows the client's own commands (`/clear`, `/help`, `/man`) as as-you-type hints, and typing more of a name narrows the list down. `Tab` completes the command being typed, which is also how they are completed when the instant hints are disabled (`--hints 0`, `--highlight 0`, `--disable_suggestion`). Until now these commands could only be found in the documentation; now the prompt itself lists them. A mistake in the name of a command is reported as such, with the commands it may have meant, instead of being parsed as SQL and reported as a syntax error at the `/`: ``` :) /hepl Exception on client: Code: 36. DB::Exception: Unknown command `/hepl`. Maybe you meant: ['/help']. Type `/` at the beginning of the line to see all the commands. (BAD_ARGUMENTS) ``` An argument given to a command that takes none (`/clear now`) is reported the same way. Batch `clickhouse-client` still parses such input as the SQL it is, exactly like it already does for `help` and `clear`; `clickhouse-local` reports it like the interactive client. The commands come from a single list, `clientSlashCommands`, shared by the hints, the completion and the diagnostics. An offered command replaces the whole typed prefix including the `/`, which `replxx` counts as a word break character and would otherwise leave in place. The offer is off for `keeper-client` and `clickhouse-disks`: they reuse the same line reader, and a leading `/` is the beginning of a path there. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114043 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The `/`-commands of the client (`/help`, `/man`, `/clear`) are now offered by the line editor: typing `/` at the beginning of the input lists them as hints, and `Tab` completes the command being typed. A mistake in the name of a command is reported with the similar commands suggested, instead of being parsed as SQL. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115039&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115039](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115039+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Tag functional tests averaging over 60s under MSan with `no-msan`
signals.text: MSan stateless jobs are the slowest functional-test jobs in CI and sit right at the edge of the 9000 s job timeout. In a recent run the private `Stateless tests (amd_msan, distributed cache, meta in keeper, s3 storage, sequential, 2/2)` job spent 8324 s of its 9000 s budget on tests and was then killed during teardown, even though all 526 tests had passed. MSan is ~5.8× slower than release on the same tests, and the cost is concentrated in a long tail: under MSan, 8 tests take over 180 s each, and the 30 slowest account for ~48% of a sequential shard's runtime. This tags every functional test whose mean duration under MSan exceeds 60 s with `no-msan`, except two tests that would otherwise lose all sanitizer coverage. ### How the set was chosen From `play.clickhouse.com`, over the public MSan stateless checks (`Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, parallel, N/M)` and `Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, sequential, N/2)`, excluding the flaky-check and selected-tests flavors): ```sql SELECT test_name, count() AS runs, avg(test_duration_ms)/1000 AS avg_s FROM checks WHERE check_name LIKE 'Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, %' AND check_name NOT LIKE '%flaky%' AND check_name NOT LIKE '%selected%' AND test_status = 'OK' AND check_start_time >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY GROUP BY test_name HAVING runs >= 20 AND avg_s > 60 ORDER BY avg_s DESC ``` 351 tests matched. 30 of them no longer exist in `master` (reverted, split into smaller tests, or removed), leaving 321. One of those, `04062_text_index_json_all_values_ghdata`, already carried `no-msan`; two more remain under MSan to retain their only sanitizer coverage, so 318 files change here. Only `OK` runs are counted, so timeouts and failures do not inflate the averages. ### Initial expected effect The following estimates were calculated before retaining the two sanitizer-coverage tests. | Flavor | MSan test time per commit | Removed | Share | |---|---|---|---| | parallel | 129025 s | 24766 s | 19.2% | | sequential | 11236 s | 4108 s | 36.6% | ### 25 slowest of the tagged tests | Test | Mean under MSan | Runs | |---|---|---| | `03988_cached_read_big_at` | 384.6 s | 9014 | | `03008_deduplication_insert_several_blocks_replicated` | 337.2 s | 9116 | | `03008_deduplication_several_mv_into_one_table_nonreplicated` | 308.8 s | 9118 | | `03008_deduplication_insert_several_blocks_nonreplicated` | 282.6 s | 9118 | | `04039_merge_tree_snapshot_teardown_race` | 275.2 s | 9347 | | `01195_formats_diagnostic_info` | 234.6 s | 9278 | | `02475_bson_each_row_format` | 206.1 s | 9264 | | `00626_replace_partition_from_table_zookeeper` | 202.5 s | 9323 | | `01019_alter_materialized_view_atomic` | 192.5 s | 9340 | | `04062_text_index_json_all_values_ghdata` | 190.4 s | 1806 | | `01721_join_implicit_cast_long` | 182.8 s | 9339 | | `00746_sql_fuzzy` | 180.5 s | 9340 | | `03755_large_primary_key_explain` | 180.2 s | 9337 | | `02943_variant_type_with_different_local_and_global_order` | 180.2 s | 9284 | | `02448_clone_replica_lost_part` | 177.4 s | 9263 | | `02372_analyzer_join` | 176.3 s | 9345 | | `04327_cluster_functions_huge_num_streams_no_crash` | 171.8 s | 9261 | | `01721_join_implicit_cast_long_oldanalyzer` | 168.9 s | 9346 | | `01079_bad_alters_zookeeper_long` | 166.8 s | 9322 | | `01747_system_session_log_long` | 165.9 s | 9014 | | `03208_array_of_json_read_subcolumns_1` | 165 s | 9339 | | `00429_long_http_bufferization` | 160.9 s | 9277 | | `04411_deep_nested_field_to_type` | 156.8 s | 9262 | | `01383_log_broken_table` | 156.4 s | 9340 | | `03326_protobuf_schemas_race` | 155.1 s | 9279 | (318 tests are tagged in total; the full list is the diff.) ### Trade-off A large share of these are the ZooKeeper, replication, mutation and race tests — precisely where MSan is most likely to find real uninitialized-memory bugs. They continue to run under ASan, UBSan and TSan, but this is a genuine reduction in MSan coverage rather than a pure win. An alternative that keeps the coverage is duration-aware sharding of the sequential jobs: the split is currently `crc32(test filename) % total_batches`, which gave one recent shard 8248 s against its sibling's 5514 s (1.50×), so balancing alone would have reclaimed ~23 min on the shard that timed out. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115050&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115050](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115050+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Record an index's absent columns when materializing it on a wide part
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114990 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112484 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes an unreleased regression from #112484 (`master` only): `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE INDEX` produced an index that never prunes when the indexed column had been added by a metadata-only `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` and the part is wide. No stable release carries #112484, so no changelog entry and no backport are owed. ### Description Reported by @ clickgapai. #112484 merged on 2026-08-15 and is an ancestor of no release branch, so only `master` is affected. **What breaks.** `ADD COLUMN c ... DEFAULT ...` on a wide part is metadata-only, so the part holds no bytes for `c`. A following `MATERIALIZE INDEX idx` writes the index files but does not add `c` to the part's column list, and since #112484 the reader refuses an index whose columns the part does not describe. The index occupies disk and never prunes: `Granules: 16/16` on the reporter's fixture versus `1/16` before, results correct both ways. **Root cause.** `splitAndModifyMutationCommands` has two branches. The compact one turns an index's required-but-absent columns into `READ_COLUMN` commands; the wide one had no such step, so `c` never enters `updated_header` and `getColumnsForNewDataPart` erases it. The missing type is the defect, so the fix belongs on the write side. **The change.** On a wide part, `MATERIALIZE INDEX` now also reads the index's absent columns, so the part records them at the type the granules were built from. The column list belongs to the part, so it records the column only when every other index holding files there either does not read it or has its granules rebuilt by this same mutation: a carried-over granule keeps its build-time type, so recording the column now would hand the reader a matching type for a stale granule. What the mutation rebuilds is decided from its own commands, and an undecidable index counts as carried over, keeping the pre-fix behaviour. Compact parts and the reader are untouched, so every #112484 refusal holds. **Cost.** The mutation now writes column data: +247 bytes before, +806,931 after on a 200k-row wide fixture; the next merge writes it anyway. No format, serialization or default change, so no `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp` entry. <details> <summary>Validation, rejected alternative, known-unfixed shape</summary> **Rejected alternative:** recording build-time types in a new per-part file - a format change needing ~9 seams, a protocol bump and upgrade/downgrade paths. **Known-unfixed:** on a part with orphan index files (#109595) `hasSecondaryIndex` is true, so the read is suppressed and the index stays inert - the status quo, never wrong results. | arm | absent arm | control arm | |---|---|---| | pristine master | `16/16` (inert) | 1/16 | | this PR | `1/16` | 1/16 | Counts identical with and without `use_skip_indexes` in every cell; the control prunes on both. Four mutation arms cover the restriction, each red on the build missing its guard: without it, a hardlinked granule's column is rewritten at the new type and the next read attempts a 4 EiB allocation; keyed to the index named in the command rather than the column, a second index over that column has its stale granules re-enabled and the next read aborts; without the rebuilt-sibling exemption, a batched update that does rebuild the sibling still suppresses it, leaving the new index inert - covered both for a sibling reached by a named column and for one reached via a TTL target. Tests: `04869_skip_index_stale_type_absent_column` gains cases 26 (the regression), 26b (subcolumn index, absent parent recorded), 27, 28 (two indices, one absent column), 29 and 30 (rebuilt sibling). Cases 11/22/23/24 moved from `ADD COLUMN` to a column TTL expiry, since the fix makes the old route no longer leave a column absent; each gained an `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` refusal assertion, and every such assertion now pins the granule count rather than matching a substring. `04246_materialize_index_force_recalc` (the #104872 compact tripwire), `04165`, `04870` and `04871` pass unchanged; 250/250 across a 50-run randomized loop. Unrelated columns stay hardlinked (by inode), so the mutation does not escalate to a full part rewrite. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115055&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115055](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115055+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not merge patch parts across the data version of an existing part
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/98898 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113998 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `Found patch part ... that intersects mutation with version ...` (`LOGICAL_ERROR`) on tables with lightweight updates. A merge of patch parts could produce a patch whose range of data versions spans the data version of an existing part; that patch can then be neither applied nor skipped, so every later operation on the partition failed and the replication queue stalled. Such merges are no longer assigned. ### Description A patch part is applied to a part either wholly or not at all: `patchHasHigherDataVersion` asserts that the patch's data versions are either all newer or all older than the data version of the part, and throws a `LOGICAL_ERROR` otherwise. Merging patch parts unions their ranges of data versions, so the merged range must not span the data version of any part in the original partition. The merge predicate took that boundary from `getCurrentMutationVersion`, that is from the mutations it still knows about. Those records are not durable, while the data version a mutation gave to the parts is: * `ReplicatedMergeTree` removes a mutation from `mutations_by_partition` when the cleanup thread drops the finished `/mutations` znode, and immediately on `KILL MUTATION`; * `MergeTree` removes it from `current_mutations_by_version` in `clearOldMutations`. Once the record is gone, every patch on either side of the boundary maps to the same version, the pair looks mergeable, and the merge produces a patch that spans a version the parts have already crossed. From then on `DETACH`/`DROP`/`MOVE`/`REPLACE PARTITION`, applying patches and building a mutations snapshot all fail on that partition, and debug and sanitizer builds abort. The fix takes the boundary from the data versions of the parts. For `ReplicatedMergeTree` they come from `virtual_parts`, which is `current_parts` + `queue`, so a version that only a queued `MUTATE_PART` has assigned is seen before that entry is executed — the pending-mutation case, which #113998 addresses from the queue side, is covered as well. The versions are collected only when the table has patch parts, so tables without lightweight updates pay nothing. No assertion is relaxed. The refused merge is never needed: the patch on the older side of the boundary is fully applied, so `clearUnusedPatchParts` drops it, and the patches on the newer side still merge with each other. This does not repair a patch that already spans a version on disk; such a table stays stuck until the patch is removed. The test is deterministic: it keeps the applied patch with `remove_unused_patch_parts = 0`, removes the finished mutation record with `KILL MUTATION`, and forces the merge with `OPTIMIZE ... PARTITION ID '<patch partition>' FINAL`. On master it aborts with the exact message; with the fix the merge is refused, the patches stay separate and the data is correct. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=0fc2db3239a1bd6dd6581f103473834687408b7d&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_tsan%29 The same `LOGICAL_ERROR` accounts for 23 stress-test failures across 8 distinct stacks and every build flavor between 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-16, the most frequent one being a merged patch part reported from `MergeTreeData::MutationsSnapshotBase`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115064&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115064](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115064+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not pop hints on a line displayed programmatically
signals.text: When a query is displayed at once rather than typed — recalled from the history with Up/Down/Ctrl-P/Ctrl-N, found by the incremental (Ctrl-T) or fuzzy (Ctrl-R) history search, pasted, brought back from the external editor, or preloaded — the as-you-type hints no longer appear at its end. With hints visible, the next Up/Down press would navigate the hints instead of the history, so navigating the history quickly was impossible. The hints are shown again as soon as the line is edited. The suppression is armed before the navigation action because replxx repaints (and regenerates the hints) inside `history_move` itself, and the displayed text is additionally pinned afterwards because replxx may throttle that repaint and replay it after the key handler returns (its "rapid refresh" of e.g. a held-down Up key). Verified with a new pty regression test (`04909_client_hints_history_navigation`, 6 cases), including duplicate-history and unchanged-editor same-text redisplays; the existing `04402_clickhouse_client_autocomplete_inline_hints` (11 cases) and the hint-related expect tests still pass. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114043 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The command line client no longer shows the as-you-type hints on a query recalled from the history (or otherwise displayed at once, e.g. pasted), so pressing Up/Down continues to navigate the history instead of the hint list. The hints appear again as soon as the line is edited. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115065&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115065](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115065+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Support PostgreSQL regexp operators and make psql \d work over the PostgreSQL protocol
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/25757 Disclaimer: I do not like Postgres operators! I think they are ugly. It makes the language similar to Bash and Perl. They use operators instead of functions only because of some design drawbacks related to the index analysis. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Support PostgreSQL-style regular expression match operators: `~` (an alias for the `match` function), `~*` (case-insensitive match), `!~` and `!~*` (negations). The `\d`, `\dt`, `\dv` commands of `psql` now work when connected to ClickHouse over the PostgreSQL compatibility protocol, and a failed query no longer terminates the connection. --- `psql` could not run its `\d` command against ClickHouse over the PostgreSQL wire protocol: ``` alexey-milovidov=> \d ERROR: Query execution failed. DB::Exception: Exclamation mark can only occur in != operator: Syntax error: failed at position 665 (!) (line 10, col 21): !~ '^pg_toast' ... SSL connection has been closed unexpectedly The connection to the server was lost. Attempting reset: Succeeded. ``` This fixes every layer of that incompatibility: - The lexer and the expression parser now understand the PostgreSQL regular expression match operators `~`, `~*`, `!~`, `!~*`, desugaring to `match` and the new functions `matchCaseInsensitive`, `notMatch`, `notMatchCaseInsensitive` (trivial `MatchImpl` variants). The KQL dialect, which previously consumed its own `!~` operator as two error tokens, is adjusted to accept the new single token. - The PostgreSQL wire protocol handler removes the `pg_catalog.` schema qualifier from incoming queries at the token level, mapping references such as `pg_catalog.pg_class` onto the emulated per-session catalog views. - The emulated `pg_class` view now contains the actual tables of the current database (with `relname`, `relnamespace`, `relowner`, `relam`, `relkind`), `pg_namespace` contains the real databases, and a `pg_am` view is added (newer `psql` versions join it). The previous fixed rows are preserved for driver compatibility. - New compatibility functions `pgGetUserById` (alias `pg_get_userbyid`) and `pgTableIsVisible` (alias `pg_table_is_visible`) support the catalog query psql sends. - A failed query now keeps the connection alive: the server sends `ErrorResponse` and returns to the `ReadyForQuery` state, like PostgreSQL. The connection is still closed if some result bytes were already sent for the failed statement, since the output stream could be cut in the middle of a protocol message. The result: ``` psql (18.4, server 26.7.1.1) db_psql_test=> \d List of relations Schema | Name | Type | Owner --------------+-------------+-------+-------- db_psql_test | t_described | table | pguser db_psql_test | t_mt | table | pguser db_psql_test | v_described | view | pguser (3 rows) ``` Known limitation: `\d <name>` (describing a specific table) sends follow-up queries using `OPERATOR(pg_catalog.~)` syntax, `COLLATE pg_catalog.default` and `format_type`, which are not supported yet; the error is now reported without dropping the connection. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115066&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115066](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115066+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Hand the connection to the built-in web UI pages over `postMessage`
signals.text: The built-in web UI pages — `/play`, `/docs`, `/dashboard`, `/schema`, `/merges`, `/jemalloc`, `/processors-profile`, `/binary` — take their connection from their own query string, which cannot carry a password: a URL ends up in browser history, `Referer` headers, server access logs and proxy logs. Only `/webterminal` could be handed credentials by the page embedding it, in a `postMessage` message. Every page now speaks that same exchange: ``` page -> host {type: 'clickhouse-hello'} host -> page {type: 'clickhouse-credentials', url, user, password} ``` The page announces itself as soon as it can apply a connection, and the host answers. The page has to speak first because a host that opened it with `window.open` cannot observe when a cross-origin document became ready, and an embedded page would otherwise race its host's `load` handler. Having adopted a connection, each page redoes what it had already loaded with the previous one, so the handover also works when it arrives after the page started querying: `/play` re-probes the credentials, `/docs` rebuilds its cross-link name cache and re-runs the displayed search, `/dashboard` and `/processors-profile` chain their reload behind the load already in flight (two concurrent loads would otherwise duplicate charts, or let a stale failure overwrite a good listing), `/schema` and `/jemalloc` reload, and `/binary` drops its cached tiles and redraws. ## Opening `/docs` from `/play` The Documentation icon in the `/play` sidebar is the first user of the handover. A plain click opens `/docs` through `window.open` — the anchor's `rel=noopener` would sever the handle — and hands the whole connection over, so the documentation search runs against the same server as the same user without the password appearing in a URL. A middle or modifier click keeps the browser's native new-tab handling, which carries `?user=` only, since such a window has no link back to `/play`. ## Security A reply is accepted only from the one window that opened or embeds the page, and only from an exact origin: the page's own, `https://console.clickhouse.cloud`, `https://console.clickhouse-staging.com` or `https://clickhouse.com`. The list is exact rather than a domain suffix on purpose — every ClickHouse Cloud service endpoint is a `*.clickhouse.cloud` host that serves content of its owner's choosing, and a trusted host can aim a page at a server of its own through `url`, which the user may then type credentials into believing it is still their own service. `webterminal.html` gated its own exchange on such a suffix and now uses the same exact list. `url` is optional and defaults to the server the page already points at, but the credentials are replaced wholesale: a message that names only a server cannot attach credentials it did not carry to it, which is what keeps a password filled in by the browser's password manager for this page's origin from following a `url` elsewhere. Outbound, credentials are always sent with an exact target origin, never `'*'`; the readiness announcement carries no secrets, only the fact that the page exists, which its host knows already. Verified in Chromium against a mock endpoint: the `/play` → `/docs` handover, the handover into an iframe for all eight pages, rejection of a handover from an untrusted origin and from a same-origin window that is not the page's host, the wholesale credential replacement, and the exactness of the origin list for all nine pages (`https://myserviceendpoint.clickhouse.cloud`, `https://evil.clickhouse.com`, `http://console.clickhouse.cloud` and `https://console.clickhouse.cloud.evil.com` are all rejected). The committed test asserts that every served page implements both halves of the exchange and that its origin list stayed exact. The protocol is documented in `docs/concepts/features/interfaces/web-ui-embedding.mdx`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The built-in web UI pages (`/play`, `/docs`, `/dashboard`, `/schema`, `/merges`, `/jemalloc`, `/processors-profile`, `/binary`) can now be handed their connection — server URL, user and password — in a `postMessage` message by the page that opened or embedded them, instead of taking it from their own query string, where a password would be recorded in browser history, referrer headers and access logs. `/play` uses this when opening `/docs`, so the documentation search connects to the same server as the same user. A page accepts a connection only from the window that opened or embeds it, and only from an exact list of trusted origins. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115067&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115067](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115067+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add MergeTree settings `max_table_size_rows`, `max_table_size_bytes_compressed`, `max_table_size_bytes_uncompressed`
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115063 Adds three new `MergeTree`-level settings that limit the total size of a table, for multi-tenant, temporary, and demo services: - `max_table_size_rows` — the maximum total number of rows in active data parts; - `max_table_size_bytes_compressed` — the maximum total size on disk across all active and inactive data parts; - `max_table_size_bytes_uncompressed` — the same for uncompressed bytes. The limits are checked against the current table size at the beginning of `INSERT` and when new data parts are committed to the working set; on exceeding a limit, the query fails with the new `TABLE_SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` error. Inserts done by materialized views (including refreshable ones) and async insert flushes are checked as well, since they go through the same sinks and part commits. The check also triggers on committing the results of background merges and mutations, so a mutation (e.g. an `UPDATE` increasing the table size) will be repeated without finishing while the table exceeds the limit, which is intended. The check is skipped on replicated fetches and on the execution of replication log entries that add data already accepted by another replica (`ATTACH_PART`, `REPLACE_RANGE`), which permits a race condition when parallel inserts into multiple replicas overdraft the limit. Committing empty data parts is always allowed, so the data can be removed from a table that exceeds the limits, e.g. with `TRUNCATE` or `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PARTITION`. The limit on the number of rows is counted only for active data parts, while the limits on the number of bytes are counted across all active and inactive data parts, because their purpose is to limit disk usage (inactive parts are removed in the background, so the observed size can decrease over time). ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add `MergeTree` settings `max_table_size_rows`, `max_table_size_bytes_compressed`, and `max_table_size_bytes_uncompressed` that limit the total size of a table. The limits are checked at the beginning of `INSERT` and when new data parts are committed (including the results of background merges and mutations), but not on replicated fetches. This closes [#115063](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115063). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115069&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115069](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115069+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not attach a cache writer to a detached file segment
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110029 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Cache file segment is in detached state`) when reading through the filesystem cache with the experimental `use_reader_executor` setting. The regression was introduced by #110029 and is not in any release, so no backport is owed. ### Description Related: #110029 **The problem.** `BuzzHouse` aborts the server with `Cache file segment is in detached state, operation not allowed`, on two unrelated PRs, first seen 8h41m after #110029 merged. CIDB STID `4043-43b7`, [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113382&sha=97396ecebc7bcb7ee4d4921c71d1cfdd071a2895&name_0=PR&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29). **Root cause.** `FileCache::getOrSet` can hand back a synthetic `DETACHED` placeholder rather than a real segment: `getImpl` fabricates one when the covering segment is being evicted or removed, and another when the range exceeds `bypass_cache_threshold`. Such a placeholder is outside the cache metadata, holds no bytes, and the downloader role cannot be acquired on it. `DiskCacheProvider::resolve` classified it as a *writable* miss, because `segmentCommittedEnd` falls back to the write offset, which for a placeholder equals the segment start. It attached a `DiskCacheWriter`, and `ReaderExecutor::readThroughCaches` then called `claimLeadRole` on it, whose `getOrSetDownloader` hit `assertNotDetachedUnlocked`: a `LOGICAL_ERROR`, aborting the server in debug and sanitizer builds. **The change.** `resolve` now emits a writer-less miss for a detached segment, so those bytes are read from source and nothing is cached. The legacy paths already do this: `CachedOnDiskReadBufferFromFile` dispatches `State::DETACHED` to a cache bypass before acquiring any role, and `CachedOnDiskWriteBufferFromFile` skips write-through caching on `isDetached()`. `claimLeadRole` was the only one of the five non-test `getOrSetDownloader` callers reachable with a detached segment; the assertion is a correct caller contract and stays. **Reachability.** `src/IO/DiskCacheProvider.cpp` exists on no active release branch (25.8, 26.3-26.7), and #110029 is an ancestor of none of them, so no released version can reach this. `use_reader_executor` is experimental and off by default; the abort affects the `BuzzHouse` checks, which randomize it as a session setting, plus anyone opting into the experimental path. **Validation.** Deterministic, no fuzzer needed: the test arms the existing failpoint `file_cache_simulate_evicting_segment`, which makes every segment the cache reports a placeholder. Without the fix the server dies with the CI stack; with it the test passes, 50/50 randomized. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115070&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115070](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115070+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Look up the SSH key and support ssh-agent in clickhouse-client
signals.text: `--ssh-key-file` can now be specified without a value. In that case the key is looked up the same way as `ssh` does it: - the identity files configured for this host in `~/.ssh/config` and in `/etc/ssh/ssh_config`; - the default identity files, such as `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`; - the keys held by the `ssh-agent`. A key held by the `ssh-agent` is preferred, because it does not need a passphrase. It is also used when `--ssh-key-file` names a key file that the agent holds - an encrypted key that was added with `ssh-add` no longer asks for the passphrase. Signing with the agent is implemented in `SSHAgent`, a small client of the agent protocol, which produces the same `SSHSIG` signature as `SSHKey::signString` does for a local key (for RSA keys it asks the agent for `rsa-sha2-256`, because agents sign with SHA-1 by default and the server rejects that). The client reports the key it has chosen: ``` $ clickhouse-client --user abcuser --ssh-key-file Using the SSH key 'the key of abcuser' from the ssh-agent. ``` Two related changes of the existing behavior: the passphrase is now asked only if the key file is really encrypted (before, `--ssh-key-file` always asked for it), and the message about a key that cannot be imported now names the file. Tests: a new stateless test `04908_ssh_key_file_lookup` covers the default identity file, an `ed25519` key from the `ssh-agent`, and an `ssh-rsa` key from the `ssh-agent` with an empty `~/.ssh`. The existing `test_ssh_keys_authentication` integration tests pass. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `clickhouse-client` accepts `--ssh-key-file` without a value: the key is looked up the same way as `ssh` does it - the identity files configured for the host in `~/.ssh/config`, the default identity files, such as `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, and the keys held by the `ssh-agent`. Authentication with a key held by the `ssh-agent` is now supported, and it does not need a passphrase. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115072&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115072](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115072+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/libssh/pull/15

signals.title: Let the promql dialect keep tokens the SQL lexer rejects
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed PromQL queries with regex label matchers (`=~`, `!~`) being rejected under `--dialect promql`. Closes #115071. --- Under `--dialect promql`, `ParserPrometheusQuery` reads the raw query text and hands it to the PromQL grammar; it walks the SQL tokens only to find where the statement ends. But `tryParseQuery` scans those tokens for lexer errors *before* the parser runs, and `~` is not a SQL token, so the query was rejected before it ever reached the PromQL grammar: ``` $ clickhouse local --dialect promql -q 'up{instance="host1"}' Code: 471. ... The name of a TimeSeries table to use with promql dialect is not specified $ clickhouse local --dialect promql -q 'up{instance=~"host2|host3"}' Code: 62. ... Unrecognized token: Syntax error: failed at position 13 (~) ``` The equality matcher gets through to a missing-setting error; the regex matcher dies at the `~` with a **SQL** lexical error. It is not specific to `-q` — stdin and `--queries-file` fail identically. The grammar itself already has the tokens (`PromQLLexer.g4`: `RE : '=~'`, `NRE : '!~'`), and the same expression works when passed as a string to the table function, which is what makes the limitation easy to miss. `IParser` gains `consumesRawText()`, false by default and overridden by `ParserPrometheusQuery`. `tryParseQuery` skips its two lexical-error rejections for such parsers, since a token the SQL lexer does not recognise is not an error for a parser that reads the text itself. No call site changes, and any future dialect parser in the same position gets the behaviour by overriding one method. This is safe because the lexer does not stop at an unrecognised character — it consumes it and returns an `Error` token (`Lexer.cpp:546`), so statement-boundary detection still finds the terminating semicolon. Kusto solves the same problem with an entire parallel `parseKQLQuery.{h,cpp}`; PromQL needs only the boundary scan, so a virtual on `IParser` seemed proportionate. Happy to go the separate-entry-point route instead if maintainers prefer the consistency. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115073&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115073](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115073+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
