signals.title: Fix gRPC and Arrow Flight listeners for wildcard listen hosts
signals.text: `gRPC` treats `::` and `0.0.0.0` as one family-agnostic wildcard: for either of them it binds a dual-stack `::` socket, and falls back to `0.0.0.0` only on a host without IPv6 (see `add_wildcard_addrs_to_server` in `contrib/grpc`). Listing both wildcard addresses in `listen_host` therefore made ClickHouse create two listeners that bind the very same socket address, and the second one either - failed with `EADDRINUSE`, because the Arrow Flight transport disables `SO_REUSEPORT`, and the exception terminated the whole server: ``` <Error> grpc: Failed to add port to server: No address added out of total 1 resolved for '0.0.0.0:9110' (Failed to add any wildcard listeners: Error in bind for address '[::]:9110': Address already in use Error in bind for address '0.0.0.0:9110': Address already in use) <Error> Application: Code: 1002. DB::Exception: Failed init Arrow Flight Server: Unknown error: Server did not start properly. ``` - or silently shared the port with the first one, because plain gRPC keeps `SO_REUSEPORT` enabled, so each of the two independent servers ended up serving a random half of the connections, and a listener configured for `0.0.0.0` accepted IPv6 connections as well: ``` <Information> Application: Listening for gRPC protocol: [::]:9100 <Information> Application: Listening for gRPC protocol: 0.0.0.0:9100 LISTEN 0 4096 *:9100 users:(("clickhouse",pid=3851032,fd=55)) LISTEN 0 4096 *:9100 users:(("clickhouse",pid=3851032,fd=56)) ``` Only one gRPC and one Arrow Flight listener is created for a group of wildcard `listen_host` values now, which is what the transport does internally anyway. Also, `listen_try` is honored for the protocols that bind their listening socket when they are started rather than when they are created. `EADDRINUSE` from gRPC or Arrow Flight was reported from the plain `server.start()` loop, outside of the `createServer` handler that implements `listen_try`, so it was fatal even with `listen_try` (and with `listen_reuse_port`) enabled - which contradicts the documented behavior of listening to at least one of the addresses without quitting. Not addressed here: plain gRPC still keeps `SO_REUSEPORT` enabled, so a gRPC port that is already taken by a different process is silently shared instead of reported. Making that consistent with `listen_reuse_port` for both gRPC and Arrow Flight is a possible follow-up. For the record, gRPC and Arrow Flight are not available as composable protocols (the `protocols` section): the composable stack is a Poco `TCPServer` with a chain of `TCPServerConnectionFactory` layers that receive an already accepted socket, while gRPC and Arrow Flight own the listening socket, the HTTP/2 framing, TLS and their own event loop, so they can neither be a layer nor sit under `tls` / `proxy1`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix the server failing to start when `listen_host` contains both `::` and `0.0.0.0` and `arrowflight_port` is configured, and fix two gRPC listeners silently sharing one port in the same configuration. `listen_try` now also covers the gRPC and Arrow Flight protocols, which bind their listening socket when they are started. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115074&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115074](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115074+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Announce the connection endpoint once when the client asks for a password
signals.text: `clickhouse-client` printed `Connecting to ...` twice whenever it had to ask for a password: ``` $ clickhouse client --host clickhouse.new --secure --user alexey-milovidov ClickHouse client version 26.8.1.1. Connecting to clickhouse.new:9440 as user alexey-milovidov. Password for user (alexey-milovidov): Connecting to clickhouse.new:9440 as user alexey-milovidov. Connected to ClickHouse server version 26.8.1. ``` Neither `--password` nor `--ask-password` was given, so the client did not know whether the user has a password at all and connected without one. The server answered `REQUIRED_PASSWORD`, and the retry loop in `Client::main` set `ask-password` and called `connect` again, which prompted for the password and announced the very same endpoint a second time. Now an endpoint is announced only when it differs from the one announced last, and the announcement is forgotten after a successful connection, so a fallback to another port and a reconnect later in the session are still announced. Added `04909_client_password_prompt_announces_endpoint_once.expect`, which fails on the current `master` binary with `The endpoint was announced twice.` and passes with this change. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `clickhouse-client` no longer prints the `Connecting to ...` message twice when it asks for a password interactively. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115081&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115081](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115081+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Report cancellation instead of leaving an in-place set unbuilt
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114463 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107619 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'` error when a query with `partial_result_on_first_cancel = 1` was cancelled while the set of an `IN (subquery)` was still being built. ### Description Follow-up to https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114463, asked for in its review. That pull request makes a cancelled mutation report `ABORTED` instead of stopping its nested pipelines silently; the review asked whether the same silent stop is still reachable through the other two interactive-cancel callbacks. I measured both. One is, one is not. **Reachable: `partial_result_on_first_cancel`.** For the first cancel, `TCPHandler::processCancel` only sets `stop_read_return_partial_result` and deliberately does not cancel the query through the process list, so the callback returns a bare `true` (`TCPHandler.cpp:897-898`). `CompletedPipelineExecutor::execute` then cancels the nested set-build pipeline and its poll loop returns normally, so `CreatingSetsTransform::generate` never runs `Set::finishInsert`, while `FutureSetFromSubquery::build` has already moved the source plan out. A caller that evaluates its filter in the same call passes the unbuilt set to `FunctionIn`. On master (`f45871c7cfa`), one cancel during ```sql SELECT count() FROM t WHERE 1 IN (SELECT number FROM numbers(10000000) WHERE sleep(1) = 0) SETTINGS partial_result_on_first_cancel = 1, optimize_use_implicit_projections = 1, optimize_trivial_count_query = 0 ``` reports ``` Code: 49. DB::Exception: Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in' ... (LOGICAL_ERROR) ``` through `FunctionIn` (`in.cpp:116`) <- `VirtualColumnUtils::filterBlockWithExpression` (`:162`) <- `MergeTreeData::getMinMaxCountProjectionBlock` (`:10463`) <- `optimizeUseAggregateProjections` (`:630`). A debug or sanitizer build aborts on it. **Not reachable: `clickhouse-local`.** Its callback cancels the query through the process list element (`LocalConnection.cpp:191-194`), so the nested pipeline fails instead of stopping silently. The same query interrupted with `SIGINT` reports `Code: 394. DB::Exception: Query was cancelled` on master, with `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` confirming the plan is the `minmax_count` projection. That installer is untouched here. `FutureSetFromSubquery::buildSetInplace` now records whether the cancel callback fired and, if the set was left uncreated, reports `QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED` instead of returning to a caller that cannot distinguish a cancelled build from a completed one. Both conditions are required on purpose, so a set build that stops for a reason other than a cancellation keeps the behaviour it has today. Measured over the routes that stop such a pipeline early: `set_overflow_mode = 'break'`, `transfer_overflow_mode = 'break'` and `read_overflow_mode = 'break'` all still reach `CreatingSetsTransform::generate`, which finishes the set, and the query returns its result; `set_overflow_mode = 'throw'` still reports `SET_SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. For `partial_result_on_first_cancel` this means such a query now fails with `QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED` rather than with the logical error. There is no partial answer to return instead: the cancellation lands during analysis, before a row is produced, and an incomplete `IN` set would silently change the result. The mutation path keeps reporting `ABORTED` as #114463 makes it: its callback throws before this check is reached, which names the mutation the way `MergeTask::checkOperationIsNotCanceled` does and covers every nested pipeline a mutation runs, not only `buildSetInplace`. The ordered variant `buildOrderedSetInplace` needs nothing: #107924 made it build against a clone of the source plan and publish only a created set, so a silently stopped ordered build just skips index analysis. Out of scope, found while measuring this and reported here rather than fixed: a *time limit* with `break` reaches the same logical error without any cancellation, because the limit stops the set-build pipeline the same way. On master, ```sql SELECT count() FROM t WHERE 1 IN (SELECT number FROM numbers(1000)) SETTINGS optimize_use_implicit_projections = 1, optimize_trivial_count_query = 0, max_execution_time = 0.0001, timeout_overflow_mode = 'break' ``` reports `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'` too. The check added here deliberately does not cover it: `break` asks for a truncated result rather than an error, so what a partially built `IN` set should do - report the limit, or silently use the rows read so far, as `set_overflow_mode = 'break'` already does - is a semantic decision, and it is not what this pull request is about. Happy to open an issue or a follow-up for it. New test `04909_cancel_in_subquery_set_build_partial_result`. It asserts up front that the `minmax_count` projection is the plan for the predicate shape under test, so it cannot pass without exercising the synchronous filter evaluation, and both of its wait loops fail loudly rather than cancelling something else. The oracle is the reported outcome, not the survival of the server, so it is live on release builds too. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115083&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115083](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115083+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix PostgreSQL-protocol authentication for users that also have an ssh_key
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/76839 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix authentication over the PostgreSQL wire protocol for users with several authentication methods: a user that also had an `ssh_key` method (or any other method that stores no password) was rejected with `Invalid user or password` even when the correct password for its `scram_sha256_password` method was supplied, and a wrong SCRAM salt was sent to the client when the SCRAM method was not the last one (e.g. for a user with `scram_sha256_password` followed by `sha256_password`). A user with multiple authentication methods, one of which is `ssh_key`, could not authenticate over the PostgreSQL protocol at all (in either order of the methods), while the same user authenticated fine over the native, MySQL, and HTTP protocols. Reproduced on 26.7.3.19 and current master. Anyone who adds a public SSH key to their user (e.g. for the SSH endpoint) silently loses PostgreSQL access with a misleading "wrong password" error. Two defects, both fixed (each order of methods hits at least one of them): 1. `checkScramSHA256Authentication` did not check the type of the authentication method it verifies the client proof against, and `IAccessStorage::authenticateImpl` calls it for every method of the user. For methods that store no password hash (e.g. `ssh_key`), the empty hash was passed to `hmacSHA256` as the HMAC key; `EVP_MAC_init` fails for a null key, so the check threw `OPENSSL_ERROR` (`Authentication failed: Code: 454. DB::Exception: EVP_MAC_init failed`) instead of returning false, aborting the whole authentication instead of trying the next method of the user. Now it returns false for non-SCRAM methods, the same way `checkMySQLAuthentication` handles non-MySQL-compatible methods. 2. `ScrambleSHA256Auth::authenticate` in the PostgreSQL handler sent the salt of the *last* authentication method of the user instead of the salt of the SCRAM method, so the client derived a salted password that could never match the stored verifier: an empty salt when `ssh_key` was last, or an unrelated random salt when e.g. `sha256_password` was. Now it sends the salt of the first `scram_sha256_password` method. Verified before/after with `psql` against a local server; added an integration test covering both method orders, the `scram_sha256_password` + `sha256_password` combination, and wrong-password rejection. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115084&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115084](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115084+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Reload a persisted `url()` table with the storage its creation selected
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104437 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a server that refuses to start after a table was created with `CREATE TABLE ... AS url('http://host/**/', ...)` while `allow_experimental_url_wildcard_from_index_pages` was enabled. Loading such a table's metadata re-evaluated the experimental check and failed with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED`, aborting startup. ### Description Reported by @ bacek on #104437, where `Stress test (amd_tsan)` failed with `Cannot start clickhouse-server` after a fuzzer created `url('/**/', JSONEachRow, 'x int')`. No fuzzer is needed: enable the setting, create such a table, restart with the default. Root cause is one defaulted parameter. `ITableFunction::execute` declares `bool is_insert_query = false`; `CREATE ... AS url(...)` passes `true` explicitly (`InterpreterCreateQuery.cpp:2403`), while metadata replay (`DatabaseOnDisk.cpp:117`) passes nothing. `TableFunctionURL::getStorage` computes `use_web_wildcard = !is_insert_query && ...`, so the two take opposite branches for the same stored table: creation builds a plain `StorageURL` and never reaches the experimental check, replay builds `StorageObjectStorage` and does. The check is dead at creation and live only on replay, and metadata loading rethrows. The fix treats a definition arriving with stored columns as a persisted one being replayed, so it resolves to the storage creation selected. The check is not suppressed, it becomes unreachable because the correct branch is taken. Suppressing it would instead enable index-page expansion with the setting disabled and give the table a read-only storage. `ENGINE = URL` was already fixed this way in 64abbdd31d85b15 ("Gate `URL` wildcard experiment check to creation"). Behaviour change: a persisted glob `url()` table that today rebuilds as `StorageObjectStorage` after a restart now rebuilds as the `StorageURL` its creation built. Both carriers are covered by the one change and both are tested: explicit structure, and `structure = 'auto'` via `StorageTableFunctionProxy` (the surface of an earlier `test_url_wildcard_schema_inference` failure). `urlCluster` cannot persist a table. The creation-time check in `getActualTableStructure` is deliberately untouched, since a columns-less `CREATE` reaches it before `execute`. Querying `url()` directly still requires the setting. Out of scope: the check stays dead at creation, so `CREATE` with a glob still succeeds with the setting off. `ytsaurus()` has the same problem by another mechanism. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104437&sha=bee15ffc5ec3d2a9b5479bd1fbc197ac6458eebc&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_tsan%29 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115095&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115095](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115095+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: perf(promql): Fuse identical agg(X) op agg(X) into one PromQL aggregation pass
signals.text: When both sides of a math binary operator are one-argument aggregations over the same expression and grouping, scan once and compute both aggregates together instead of joining two identical grids. This is admittedly pretty niche, so let me know if this isn't worth it. signals.title: Web terminal: do not connect before the host page supplies the credentials
signals.text: A `/webterminal` page embedded in a host page - `play.html`, or the ClickHouse Cloud console - is loaded without credentials in its URL and receives them from the host page over `postMessage`, on the iframe's `load` event. It nevertheless opened a connection of its own at startup, before that message could arrive, so every embedded terminal authenticated twice: first with an empty password, which can only succeed for a passwordless user, and then, a moment later, with the credentials from the host page, after the first WebSocket had been closed and replaced. The visible symptom is `Connecting...` printed twice - `attemptConnect` announces every attempt, and whether the first line is erased before the second is printed depends on timing. Behind it are a wasted WebSocket, a guaranteed-failing authentication, and, for a passwordless user, an established session that gets torn down right away. The page now waits for the credentials instead of connecting on its own. A host page that never sends them - it does not implement the protocol, or its origin is not trusted - would leave a terminal that neither connects nor prompts, so the page says that it is waiting and Enter hands the login over to the interactive prompt; credentials arriving after that no longer hijack what the user is typing. The pages opened as a normal tab, or with a `user` URL parameter, keep connecting immediately. The wait became a state of the page's own state machine, which makes the `waitingForCredentials` and `initialAutoAuth` flags, and the `ws.onclose` branch they served, unnecessary. The new `tests/integration/test_webterminal_startup` follows the existing `test_play_reconcile_startup`: it fetches `/webterminal` from a real server and runs the page's real script in a Node `vm` with a stubbed terminal and `WebSocket`, then drives each flow and asserts which connections were opened and what was displayed. Against this branch all 34 checks pass; against `master` 23 fail, including `announces the attempt exactly once -- actual: 2`. It also pins the paths that must keep connecting immediately, the prompt after a rejected password, and that credentials from an untrusted origin, from a trusted host over plain HTTP, or from a window that is not the parent are ignored - the wait is now the only way into an embedded session, so a hole in either check would hand the terminal to a foreign page. Reported by a user of clickhouse.new, where the console drives the terminal through exactly this embedded flow. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105191 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115067 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A web terminal embedded in another page, such as the SQL console or `play.html`, receives its credentials from that page and no longer opens a connection of its own before they arrive. Previously it connected twice - once with an empty password, then again with the real credentials - and printed `Connecting...` twice. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115148&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115148](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115148+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1720` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Fix wrong count and wrong DELETE when a NULL expression sits under NOT
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112242 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112242 Requested by @ nihalzp in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112242#issuecomment-5312306258 (reported by @ zlareb1). ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results when a `WHERE` clause contained a `NULL` expression under a `NOT`, for example `SELECT count() FROM t WHERE NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL)`. Index analysis treated such a condition as provably true for the whole range, so the filter was skipped: `count()` returned rows the query rejects, and `ALTER TABLE ... DELETE` with that condition removed rows it should have kept. ### Description ```sql CREATE TABLE t (id UInt32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; INSERT INTO t SELECT number FROM numbers(40); SELECT count() FROM t WHERE NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL); -- returned 40, correct is 20 ``` Reading the rows returned 20, so `count()` and the row set disagreed on one predicate. A mutation was worse: `ALTER TABLE t DELETE WHERE NOT (id >= 38 AND NULL)` deleted all 40 rows, although the predicate is `NULL` for `id` 38 and 39, so those two had to survive. **Root cause.** `cloneDAGWithInversionPushDown` pushes `NOT` to the leaves. For `NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL)`, De Morgan turns the `and` into an `or` and pushes the inversion into both children; the all-NULL leaf is not recognized, so the tail wraps it in a literal `not()`, which `RPNBuilder` complements classically into "provably true for every row". Both steps hold only in two-valued logic: `NOT NULL` is `NULL`, which `WHERE` must reject. **The change.** Before the node dispatch, an all-NULL node absorbs the inversion instead of receiving a `not()` wrapper, the same idiom the neighbouring `materialize` and trivial-cast branches use. It still folds to "never true" downstream, correct because `NULL` is not `TRUE`, and a non-negated `x AND NULL` keeps its exact fast path. Absorbing the inversion substitutes the operand's type for the `not()` result type, so the guard is confined to `boolean_context`, the existing flag for positions where the caller discards the value. In a value position a negation would otherwise change type and drop valid rows. The all-NULL test needs both a column and a type check: `toInt64OrNull('x')` is typed `Nullable(Int64)`, while `if(id % 2, NULL, NULL)` has no constant column. <details> <summary>Validation</summary> Debug build of the base commit vs the same build with the change. | probe | base | with change | correct | |---|---|---|---| | `count() WHERE NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL)` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `toInt64OrNull('x')` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)')` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `if(id % 2, NULL, NULL)` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `materialize(NULL)` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | `numbers(100) WHERE NOT (number = 5 AND NULL) LIMIT 10` | 9 | 10 | 10 | | minmax skip index, same predicate | 40 | 20 | 20 | | `ALTER DELETE WHERE NOT (id >= 38 AND NULL)`, survivors | `[]` | `[38,39]` | `[38,39]` | | `count() WHERE id >= 20 AND NULL` | 0 | 0 | 0 | | `numbers() WHERE number > 0 AND NULL LIMIT 10` | 0 fast | 0 fast | 0 fast | | value position, `ifNull(NOT materialize(CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(Int64)')), 0)`, rows | 40 | 40 | 40 | | same with `Nullable(Float64)`, rows | 40 | 40 | 40 | The new test fails on the base build, passes with the change, and passed 50/50 randomized runs. Deleting any one of the three parts of the guard makes it fail again on exactly the arms that part covers: the column test covers `toInt64OrNull` and `CAST`, the type test covers `if(id % 2, NULL, NULL)`, the `boolean_context` test covers the two value-position arms. The unbounded `numbers()` lines pin the positive direction, which an earlier attempt at this fix turned into a hang. The projection, `KeyCondition` and minmax test families were run on both builds: the same 23 tests fail either way, all on ZooKeeper and distributed connections unavailable in this sandbox, none mentioning the exact-count projection or `KeyCondition`. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115152&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115152](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115152+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add a test for lazy materialization over a shadowed constant
signals.text: Adds a regression test for https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112209. With `query_plan_enable_optimizations = 0` the first optimization pass never runs, so the chain below the sort keeps an `ExpressionStep` whose DAG re-materializes the constant of a constant `SELECT` item while still taking a same-named input (a `COLUMN` node named `2_UInt8` next to an `INPUT` of that name). Lazy materialization lives in the second pass, which that setting does not gate, so it split such a DAG; `ActionsDAG::split` renamed the node promoted to the lazy half (`avoid_duplicate_inputs`) to `2_UInt8_0`, while the re-stacked `Sorting` step still resolved `2_UInt8` by name, and `PartialSortingTransform` failed at pipeline build with `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK`. The query was fixed indirectly by https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112326, which added `hasInputNameShadowedByComputedNode` and declines such plans upfront. That change was written for the row-policy `CAST(x, ...) AS x` shape and its test `04654_lazy_materialization_shadowed_input_name` covers only that variant, so this test pins the constant `SELECT` item with `ORDER BY ALL` as well. Verified: it throws on 26.8.1.203 (`ecb9cf7b997`) and passes from `f45cb411cbc` on. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112209 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112326 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115161&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115161](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115161+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Name the join algorithms that were tried in the "can't execute" error
signals.text: When no enabled join algorithm can run a JOIN, the planner threw: ``` Can't execute any of specified algorithms for specified strictness/kind and right storage type ``` It named neither the algorithms that were tried nor the JOIN that failed, even though both are available at the throw site. Setting `join_algorithm` to something narrower for memory reasons and then writing an `ASOF JOIN` left you with nothing to act on. It now reads: ``` None of the algorithms enabled by the 'join_algorithm' setting [grace_hash] can execute this ASOF INNER JOIN with the given right table storage type ``` Algorithm names are printed through `SettingFieldJoinAlgorithmTraits::toString` rather than `toString(JoinAlgorithm)`. The latter returns the uppercase enum spelling, `GRACE_HASH`, which the setting parser rejects, so the names in the message can now be pasted straight back into `join_algorithm`. The message deliberately does not list the algorithms that would work. `tryCreateJoin` has no capability table, the rules live implicitly across its per algorithm branches, so naming them here would add a copy of knowledge that is already in the documentation and would rot quietly the next time an algorithm gains or loses support. Also updates a comment in `02242_join_rocksdb.sql` that quoted the old wording. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): When no join algorithm enabled by the `join_algorithm` setting can execute a `JOIN`, the error message now names the algorithms that were tried and the strictness and kind of the JOIN that failed, instead of reporting only that none of them worked. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115226&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115226](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115226+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not use the trivial count optimization when the aggregate argument contains arrayJoin
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115123 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115123 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results for `SELECT count(arrayJoin(arr))` with the default `optimize_trivial_count_query = 1`. The stored row count was returned instead of the number of array elements, and on `file()` and `url()` the query returned `0`. Closes #115123. ### Description Requested by @ PedroTadim on the issue (["the fix for this seems small. Can you do it?"](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115123#issuecomment-5315767329)); reported by @ konsta-danyliuk. `applyTrivialCountIfPossible` replaces the whole table read with the stored row counter. It checks that the aggregate is `count` by type, then never inspects `count`'s argument. `arrayJoin` multiplies rows above the source read, so the aggregate observes `sum(length(arr))` rows rather than `totalRows()`, and the expansion is dropped along with the read. Measured on 3 rows / 6 elements: `count(arrayJoin(A))` returned `3` instead of `6`. The fix refuses the optimization when the argument contains `arrayJoin`, using the same `hasFunctionNode(..., "arrayJoin")` guard six sibling optimizations already use for this property. The guard sits **before** `select_query_info.optimize_trivial_count = true`: for `file()`, `url()` and object storage `totalRows()` is `nullopt`, so the function returns `false`, but the flag has already been written and those storages count in `read()`, so they returned `0`. Placing the guard after the flag write fixes MergeTree while leaving `file()` at `0`, so the test asserts the `file()` value too. The old analyzer decides trivial count separately, in `TreeRewriter`, and is affected there too. Per @ PedroTadim's review, that path is obsolete, so this PR leaves it alone: the analyzer is the only path fixed and asserted, and the test is tagged `no-old-analyzer`. Not bundled: rewriting `count(arrayJoin(A))` to `sum(A.size0)` would be faster, but that is an optimization on top of a wrong-results fix. <details><summary>Carriers and over-guard checks (measured, base vs patched)</summary> Fixture: 3 rows, `sum(length(A))` = 6. | case | base | patched | |---|---|---| | `count(arrayJoin(A))` on MergeTree | 3 | 6 | | `count(unnest(A))` (alias) | 3 | 6 | | `count(arrayJoin(A) + 1)`, `arrayJoin(arrayMap(...))` (nested) | 3 | 6 | | `count(arrayJoin(arrayJoin([A,B])))` | 3 | 11 | | `count(arrayJoin(A))` on `file()` / `url()` | **0** | 6 | | `count(arrayJoin(M))` Map / `(T)` Array(Tuple) | 3 | 5 | | `count(arrayJoin(LC))` Array(LowCardinality) | 3 | 7 | | `count(arrayJoin(A))` via `remote()` | 3 | 6 | | `count(arrayJoin(A))` ReplacingMergeTree FINAL | 6 | 6 | Object storage reads the same flag at `StorageObjectStorage.cpp:720`, so it takes the `file()`/`url()` path; with no S3 endpoint here that row is read from the code, not measured. Unchanged, and asserted so: `count()`, `count(*)`, `count(1)`, `count(n)`, `count(nullable)`, `ARRAY JOIN` as a clause, `countIf(arrayJoin(...))`, `count(DISTINCT arrayJoin(...))`, the sparsity-filter sibling, and a `count()` whose unrelated subquery contains `arrayJoin` (both visitors stop at nested query nodes). Controls: rejecting any non-empty argument list flips `count(n)` off the optimization; moving the guard below the flag write fails the `file()` arm alone. Every stateless test referencing `optimize_trivial_count` was run. The only failures need a dataset or a listener this sandbox cannot provide (`test.hits`, `127.0.0.2:9000`) and fail identically on unpatched master. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115227&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115227](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115227+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1681` (included in `26.8` and later) - Backported to: `26.7.5.3`, `26.6.4.4` <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Record the read wait-for-write span and histogram in the new Keeper dispatcher
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115017 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101757 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115017 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101757 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix the histogram metric `keeper_read_wait_for_write_time_milliseconds` and the OpenTelemetry span `keeper.read.wait_for_write` always reading zero and never being emitted when `use_new_dispatcher` is enabled, which is the default. Both are now recorded for read requests that wait for an in-flight write, as they were before the new request dispatcher. ### Description Requested by @ al13n321 on #115017: record the histogram and the span for late and intermediate reads in the commit callback. `KeeperRequestDispatcherOld` initializes the `ReadWaitForWrite` span when it parks a read and finalizes it when the write commits. The new dispatcher replaced that queue with two carriers in `InFlightBatch`, `intermediate_reads` (parked mid-batch) and `late_reads` (parked after the last request), and instrumented neither. The wait still happens; only its measurement was lost. This initializes at both park sites and finalizes both carriers in `onCommit`. `maybeFinalize` observes the histogram before checking for a span, so one pair feeds both surfaces. `dropInFlightRequests` is deliberately not finalized: those reads never saw their write complete, so timing them would mix stream-recreation timeouts into a latency metric, and `Old` does not finalize its error path either. A test arm pins it. The initialize in `LateReads::add` runs under the lock `add` already holds, before the read is visible to `onCommit`, and adds no lock, atomic or ordering edge. `onCommit` finalizes only the first group it takes per batch: the write is applied before the commit callback runs, so a read attached while that batch's reads are already draining waited for those reads, not for the write. A test arm pins this by adding a read from inside the drain. No setting, ordering or state transition changed. Validated on an embedded-keeper server: before, the histogram stays at 0 and the span is absent while sibling keeper spans are recorded; after, the count advances and the span carries the attributes `Old` emits. Two test gaps. Parking cannot be forced deterministically from a client, so the integration test keeps its assertion tolerating the span's absence rather than gaining a flaky one. No unit test reaches the `dispatchThread` initialize, which needs a started raft stream; the server run above covers it. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115252&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115252](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115252+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Remove deprecated XML way to declare a disk resource
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108286 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Removed the deprecated `read_resource` and `write_resource` disk options from `storage_configuration`. Attach a scheduler resource to a disk with `CREATE RESOURCE name (READ DISK disk, WRITE DISK disk)` instead. ### Why this is safe Declaring IO scheduler resources in XML has already been removed: #108286 deleted the XML-based `CustomResourceManager` (the `<resources>` config section), so `CREATE RESOURCE` / `CREATE WORKLOAD` (the SQL `WorkloadResourceManager`) is already the only way to define resources and workloads. The disk-level `read_resource` / `write_resource` options were the last XML remnant — they only pointed a disk at a resource *by name*, which `CREATE RESOURCE ... (READ DISK d, WRITE DISK d)` (or `READ ANY DISK` / `WRITE ANY DISK`) already expresses from the resource side. They were redundant, so this removes them together with the matching documentation. ### What to use instead ```sql CREATE RESOURCE network_read (READ DISK s3); CREATE RESOURCE network_write (WRITE DISK s3); ``` A disk that still carries `read_resource` / `write_resource` in its config is simply no longer bound to a resource by them; define the resource in SQL against that disk instead.

signals.title: Enforce allow_non_metadata_alters on the mutation path, and document what it blocks
signals.text:
Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115058 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `allow_non_metadata_alters = 0` now also rejects the `ALTER` commands that reach a `MergeTree` table as explicit mutations: `UPDATE`, `DELETE WHERE`, the five `MATERIALIZE` forms, `APPLY DELETED MASK`, `APPLY PATCHES` and `REWRITE PARTS`. Previously the check only saw the commands represented by the schema-alter path, so these rewrote parts anyway. `DELETE FROM` and `UPDATE` stay permitted, including `ON CLUSTER`. The setting description now lists what is refused, and that the check is `MergeTree`-only. ### Description The setting was only read in `MergeTreeData::checkAlterIsPossible`. The commands listed above go into a `MutationCommands` segment, which calls `checkMutationIsPossible`, whose `Settings` parameter `MergeTreeData` declared unused. The fix names it and rejects when `hasNonEmptyMutationCommands()` holds, the predicate that already decides whether the mutation runs, so guard and execution cannot drift. Plain `DELETE FROM` needed care: under the default `lightweight_delete_mode` it synthesizes `ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE _row_exists = 0`, which the storage cannot tell from the user-written form. Exempting by shape would reopen the hole, so the synthesizing interpreter grants it on a private context. `StorageWindowView::cleanup()` is the only other such call site in `src/`. A setting cannot carry that provenance across nodes: the worker re-clamps shipped settings against its own profile. So `DELETE FROM ... ON CLUSTER` now dispatches the `DELETE` itself, as `InterpreterUpdateQuery` does. Two consequences: - `DDLWorker` now leader-routes `ASTDeleteQuery`, so a replicated shard runs it once, not once per replica. This also covers a multi-shard `Replicated` database, which is reached by a plain `DELETE` rather than by `ON CLUSTER`: it replicates the `DELETE` at database level, and `ON CLUSTER` against it is rejected as a non-initial query both before and after this PR. Mid-upgrade an old and a new worker can both execute one entry, which duplicates the mutation and converges; the two closest precedents also shipped ungated. - `InterpreterDeleteQuery` now inlines SQL user-defined functions, as the interpreters it used to re-enter did. That store is not replicated by default, so an unexpanded body either failed with `UNKNOWN_FUNCTION` on the other hosts or, if defined differently there, silently deleted different rows there. Refusals happen only where the setting is 0, but the two bullets above apply at any value of it, including the default. @PedroTadim, the compatibility question is open if you prefer the docs half.
Validation, allow_non_metadata_alters = 0 on a debug build Three binaries: base, the guard without the caller exemption, and the fix. | Statement | base | guard only | fix | |---|---|---|---| | the mutation commands listed above | OK | 524 | 524 | | user-written `ALTER ... UPDATE _row_exists = 0`, local and `ON CLUSTER` | OK | 524 | 524 | | `DELETE FROM` (default mode) | OK | 524 | OK | | `DELETE FROM ... ON CLUSTER`, profile constrains the setting to 0 | OK | 524 | OK | | `DELETE FROM` (`lightweight_update` mode) | OK | OK | OK | | lightweight `UPDATE ... SET` | OK | OK | OK | | `DROP COLUMN` of an `ALIAS`, `ADD COLUMN`, `COMMENT COLUMN`, `MODIFY SETTING` | OK | OK | OK | | the alters already refused before this change | 524 | 524 | 524 | | every refused statement again under `= 1` | OK | OK | OK | 524 is `ALTER_OF_COLUMN_IS_FORBIDDEN`, the code the existing alter-path guard already throws. `DELETE FROM` is the only cell where the middle column differs from the fix, so the relaxation is exactly one statement wide. `01413_allow_non_metadata_alters` is extended with these cases and fails without the fix; each new expected-error line was justified against the base binary first, where all of them succeed. The clustered cases need a settings profile, which a stateless test cannot set, so they live in `test_allow_non_metadata_alters_on_cluster` (11 arms). Two assert a single mutation entry per shard, one for a `ReplicatedMergeTree` table reached by `ON CLUSTER`, one for a multi-shard `Replicated` database reached by a plain `DELETE`; both fail on the base binary with 2 entries. `lightweight_deletes_sync` is 2 and the DDL output mode is `THROW`, so that read happens after every host finished, with no polling or sleep. Two define a function on one host only, and differently on each host: without the inlining they fail with `UNKNOWN_FUNCTION` and with divergent surviving keys respectively.

signals.title: Remove the redundant cross-thread cancel of the Keeper leader-metrics timer
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113334 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `KeeperServer::stopLeaderMetricsPolling()` cancelled the leader-metrics timer from the main thread at shutdown, while a NuRaft asio worker re-armed the same `asio::steady_timer` from `collectLeaderMetrics()`. Both touch `deadline_timer_service::implementation_type::might_have_pending_waits` outside `leader_unavailable_metrics_mutex`, so nothing orders them. `basic_waitable_timer` is documented `Shared objects: Unsafe`, so the defect is at these two call sites, not in NuRaft or boost. TSan reports it on any amd_tsan job tearing a Keeper-enabled server down, attaching to whichever test is shutting the cluster down, hence three test names: - [amd_tsan integration 5/6](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109368&sha=51444071bc4587932301117674fde5f44a6f2f84&name_0=PR&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%205%2F6%29), `test_keeper_max_request_size` - [amd_tsan stateless flaky check](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=101841&sha=b493a5015808fdf65e1592623e56165c0bb1d44b&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20flaky%20check%29) - [amd_tsan integration 1/6](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115039&sha=a9798769f07c415c69b43a74a2547ce96291fb15&name_0=PR&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%201%2F6%29), `test_keeper_opentelemetry_tracing` I delete the cancel rather than add synchronization, because `f473bc8825cfb3b` deliberately hoisted `schedule()` out of that mutex under the subject "deadlock hazard". The cancel is also redundant: resetting the optional under the mutex is already a complete stop signal, since `collectLeaderMetrics()` re-checks it as the first statement inside its own lock before re-arming, so a late callback schedules nothing and the poll chain ends on its own. `asio_service->stop()` then joins the workers. One writer remains, no lock held across a boost call. Validated on a TSan build, since the defect is invisible in debug and release. A gdb breakpoint on `nuraft::asio_service::cancel_impl` reaches it via `stopLeaderMetricsPolling` on the main thread in 3 of 3 runs before the change and 0 of 3 after, with a positive control confirming the shutdown path ran in all six. I did not observe the TSan report itself locally, expected at three hits in 45 days. `test_keeper_max_request_size` passed 144/144 over 12 repeats; `test_keeper_back_to_back` and `test_keeper_four_word_command` passed with no `Failed to shutdown RAFT server` warning, the signal that the drain still bounds a pending expiry. Introduced by #113334 and master-only, so there is nothing to backport. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115305&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115305](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115305+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Remove `WasmEdge` in favor of `wasmtime`
signals.text: Removes the `WasmEdge` WebAssembly runtime, leaving `wasmtime` as the only engine for WebAssembly UDFs. `wasmtime` has been the default and recommended engine, and `WasmEdge` was only reachable by explicitly setting `webassembly_udf_engine` to `wasmedge`. Keeping a second implementation of `IWasmEngine` alive costs a vendored C++ submodule (plus `spdlog`, which nothing else in the tree used), a second engine backend to maintain, and CI lanes configured to switch the server over to it. What is removed: - The `contrib/wasmedge` submodule and `contrib/wasmedge-cmake`, along with `contrib/spdlog`, which existed only to build `WasmEdge`. - `src/Interpreters/WebAssembly/WasmEdgeRuntime.{h,cpp}`, the `USE_WASMEDGE` build option and its `system.build_options` row. - `IWasmEngine::requiresFuelSpecialization`, which existed only to distinguish `WasmEdge` (no fuel specialization) from `wasmtime`. The per-fuel-mode module cache is now unconditional. - The `--wasm-engine` option of `tests/config/install.sh` and the `WasmEdge` CI job option, so the affected stateless lanes are renamed: - `amd_msan, WasmEdge, {parallel,sequential}` → `amd_msan, {parallel,sequential}` - `amd_llvm_coverage, old analyzer, s3 storage, DBReplicated, WasmEdge, {parallel,sequential}` → the same name without `WasmEdge` `webassembly_udf_engine` is kept as the engine selector; `wasmtime` is now its only accepted value, and any other value is rejected with `UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_IN_CONFIG` as before. Because `WasmModuleManager` is constructed eagerly during startup (`Server::main` → `Context::setUserScriptsPath` → `Context::initWasmModuleManager`), a server whose config still says `wasmedge` will refuse to start with `Unknown WebAssembly engine 'wasmedge', available engines: 'wasmtime'` rather than fail lazily on first use. Silently aliasing `wasmedge` to `wasmtime` was rejected on purpose: it would be a fallback that hides a stale config. Verified locally on an `aarch64` build: `system.build_options` reports `USE_WASMTIME = 1` with no `USE_WASMEDGE` row; all 23 stateless WebAssembly UDF tests pass (including `04259_wasm_udf_enable_fuel`, which exercises both fuel modes and therefore the module cache path simplified here); and a server configured with `wasmedge` fails startup with the message above. No test coverage is lost. `wasmtime` is disabled under MemorySanitizer (false positives from JIT-generated code), which is why the MSan lanes ran with `WasmEdge` — but every stateless test that executes a WebAssembly module is tagged `no-msan`, so those lanes exercised no WebAssembly UDF code; the option only rewrote the server config. The two `*_ast_json_*` tests that mention `LANGUAGE WASM` only round-trip the query through `parseQueryToJSON` and never instantiate a module. On the coverage lane, those tests now run against `wasmtime` instead of `WasmEdge`. On binaries where `wasmtime` cannot be built, including MemorySanitizer, `arm_v80compat`, and `riscv64`, WebAssembly UDF support is now disabled entirely. Enabling `allow_experimental_webassembly_udf` makes the server fail during startup with `WebAssembly UDF support is disabled because ClickHouse was built without wasmtime`; it no longer exposes a module manager that can only fail later at runtime. The `wasmedge` mentions left in `docs/reference/settings/server-settings/settings/other.mdx` and in the localized `docs/<locale>/` trees are generated output and are refreshed by the docs autogeneration workflow. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Removed the `WasmEdge` engine for WebAssembly UDFs. `wasmtime`, which has always been the default, is now the only supported value of the `webassembly_udf_engine` server setting. A server configured with `<webassembly_udf_engine>wasmedge</webassembly_udf_engine>` will not start; remove that setting or set it to `wasmtime`. On binaries where `wasmtime` is unavailable, including MemorySanitizer, `arm_v80compat`, and `riscv64`, WebAssembly UDF support is unavailable and enabling it prevents server startup. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115316&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115316](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115316+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix wrong results from compiled `if`/`multiIf`/`CASE` mixing `Date`/`Date32` with `DateTime`/`DateTime64`
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115272 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115146 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results from `if`, `multiIf` and `CASE` when one branch is a `Date` or `Date32` and the result type is `DateTime` or `DateTime64`. With `compile_expressions = 1` (the default) the compiled expression copied the date's day count into the timestamp column without converting days to seconds, so `if(cond, toDate32('1900-01-01'), toDateTime64('1970-01-01', 3))` returned `1969-12-31 23:59:34.433`. Closes #115272. ### Description Reported by @ PedroTadim in [#115272](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115272), who asked me to fix it and have @Manerone review. **Root cause.** `FunctionIfBase::isCompilableImpl` already intends to refuse these expressions -- its comment reads *"It's difficult to compare Date and DateTime - cannot use JIT compilation."* -- but it tested `WhichDataType::isDate()` and `isDateTime()`, which are exact `TypeIndex` equality, so it refused only `Date`+`DateTime` and admitted `Date32`+`DateTime64`, `Date`+`DateTime64` and `Date32`+`DateTime`. Those reach `nativeCast`, which correctly finds no scale for day-count types and falls through to a plain `CreateIntCast`: `-25567` days becomes `-25567` milliseconds. The predicates were never widened when `Date32` and `DateTime64` were added. **The change** widens both predicates to `isDateOrDate32()` and `isDateTimeOrDateTime64()`, so the guard covers the whole family and the interpreted path runs. `if.cpp` and `multiIf.cpp` inherit this base, so one change covers all three. These expressions lose JIT, as the comment intended and as `Date`+`DateTime` always did. The commit message covers the rejected IR alternative. **Validation.** New test `04930_jit_compiled_if_date_to_datetime` asserts the compiled result equals the `compile_expressions = 0` result over the reported matrix: scales 0/3/6/9, both date and both datetime types, both branch orders, constant and column dates, `if`/`multiIf`/`CASE`, `Nullable(Date32)`, pre/post-1970. 12 of its 14 comparison rows fail without the fix and all pass with it (50/50 runs). The 2 exceptions are controls green both ways: `Date`+`DateTime`, already refused, and same-unit `Date32`+`Date`, which must keep compiling. Those rows are 1-vs-0 parity checks, so they would pass even if compilation stopped. Two further rows pin which shapes compile, via `ProfileEvents['CompiledFunctionExecute']`: it counts executions of an already-compiled node, so it needs no cache drop and the test stays parallel-safe. The mixed-unit row fails on an unpatched binary, so it tracks this change rather than asserting a constant. They are also why the test carries `no-fasttest, no-msan`: those builds have no embedded compiler. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115325&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115325](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115325+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Allow Map data type for asynchronous metrics
signals.text: <!--- A technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created The following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly utils/changelog/changelog.py tests/ci/cancel_and_rerun_workflow_lambda/app.py --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Asynchronous metrics can now have the `Map` data type, and the per-CPU-core and per-device metrics were converted to single key-value metrics: `OSUserTimeCPU0`, `OSUserTimeCPU1`, ... became a single `OSUserTimeCPU` metric with a map from the CPU core number to the value (and similarly for the other `OS*TimeCPU*` metrics, `CPUFrequencyMHz_*`, `Temperature*`, `EDAC*`, `Block*_*`, `Network(Receive|Send)*_*`, `Disk*_*`, `*BlobsQueueEstimate`, and `AsyncLogging*QueueSize`). `system.asynchronous_metrics` has a new `key_values Map(String, Float64)` column (the `value` column is `NaN` for such metrics), `system.asynchronous_metric_log` logs them as one row per key using a new `key` column, the Prometheus endpoint exports them with a label (e.g. `ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_BlockReadBytes{device="sda"}`), and the Graphite `MetricsTransmitter` sends them as `<prefix>.<Metric>.<key>`. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115321 Some metrics are per CPU core or per device (block device, network interface, disk, temperature sensor, EDAC memory controller, logging channel), and they were published as separate metrics with the entity name mangled into the metric name (`CPUFrequencyMHz_0`, `BlockReadBytes_sda`, `DiskTotal_default`, ...). This pollutes the metric namespace (hundreds of metrics on large machines), makes the set of metric names unstable across servers, and makes aggregation across entities awkward. Now each such family is a single key-value metric. ### Details **Data model.** `AsynchronousMetricValue` gains `key_values` (an ordered map from the entity name to the value) and `key_label` (what the key means: `cpu`, `device`, `interface`, `disk`, `sensor`, `mc`, `channel`; it is also used as the Prometheus label name). A metric is either scalar or key-value. **`system.asynchronous_metrics`.** A new column `key_values Map(String, Float64)` holds the values of a key-value metric; the `value` column is `NaN` for them (an aggregate across entities like a sum is not meaningful for every metric, e.g. `CPUFrequencyMHz` or `Temperature`, so none is invented). Example: ``` SELECT metric, key_values FROM system.asynchronous_metrics WHERE metric = 'CPUFrequencyMHz' ``` I considered making the `value` column `Dynamic` (holding either `Float64` or `Map(String, Float64)`), but it breaks the most common query patterns: `WHERE value > 0` throws `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` as soon as any row holds a Map, and `avg(value)` stops working. **`system.asynchronous_metric_log`.** A key-value metric is logged as one row per key via a new `key LowCardinality(String)` column (empty for scalar metrics). This keeps `value Float64` (and its compression), and time-series aggregation stays natural: `WHERE metric = 'BlockReadBytes' AND key = 'sda'`, or `sum(value) ... GROUP BY key`. The default `ORDER BY` of the table is now `metric, key, event_date, event_time`. On upgrade, the old table is renamed and a new one is created by the standard system-log schema-mismatch mechanism. **Prometheus.** Key-value metrics are exported as one line per key with a proper label instead of a mangled name: `ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_BlockReadBytes{device="sda"} 123` (merged with the configured constant labels; label values are escaped). **Graphite (`MetricsTransmitter`).** Key-value metrics are sent one path component deeper: `<prefix>.BlockReadBytes.sda`. **Converted metric families** ("change it where reasonable"): - `OS{User,Nice,System,Idle,IOWait,Irq,SoftIrq,Steal,Guest,GuestNice}TimeCPU<n>` → `OS*TimeCPU` keyed by the core number (the all-core sums `OSUserTime` etc. are unchanged) - `CPUFrequencyMHz_<n>` → `CPUFrequencyMHz` - `Temperature<n>` (thermal zones, numeric keys) and `Temperature_<hwmon>[_<sensor>]` (name keys) → a single `Temperature` metric - `EDAC<n>_{Correctable,Uncorrectable}` → `EDAC{Correctable,Uncorrectable}` keyed by the memory controller number - all 17 `Block*_<device>` families → `Block*` keyed by the device name - all 8 `Network{Receive,Send}*_<interface>` families → keyed by the interface name - `Disk{Total,Used,Available,Unreserved}_<disk>` and `Disk{Put,Get}ObjectThrottler{RPS,Available}_<disk>` → keyed by the disk name - `<disk>DeadBlobsQueueEstimate`, `<disk>MissingBlobsQueueEstimate` → `DeadBlobsQueueEstimate`, `MissingBlobsQueueEstimate` keyed by the disk name - `AsyncLogging<Channel>QueueSize` → `AsyncLoggingQueueSize` keyed by the channel name Left as-is (small bounded sets rather than per-device breakdowns): `PSI_*`, `NetworkTCPSockets_<STATE>`, per-protocol thread/rejected-connection metrics, `HTTPConnectionPool<Group>*`, jemalloc arena metrics. **Dashboards.** The only dashboard queries that used suffixed names are the four "Network receive/send bytes/sec" charts of the Cloud overview dashboards, which use `metric LIKE 'NetworkReceiveBytes%'` with `sum(value)` per time point. They are left unchanged deliberately: the `LIKE` pattern matches both the old suffixed rows and the new per-key rows, so the charts stay correct and continuous across the upgrade. The Web UI dashboard (`dashboard.html`) does not hardcode any metric names. **Docs.** The metric list in `docs/reference/system-tables/asynchronous_metrics.mdx` is regenerated by `utils/generate-async-metrics-docs`; the columns of both system tables are documented. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115333&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115333](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115333+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Resume a NATS JetStream subscription after a reconnect
signals.text: A `NATS` table reading from a JetStream stream can stop consuming for good after the NATS server restarts, while still looking subscribed and healthy. An asynchronous JetStream pull subscription asks for more messages only when one is delivered, and when the NATS client reconnects it re-sends the `SUB` line but not the pull request the broker was holding. A broker that goes away without answering that request - a hard kill, a network partition, or a graceful restart that lands in the milliseconds between a re-subscribe and its request being parked - leaves the table subscribed and permanently silent. That is what `test_nats_restore_failed_connection_without_losses_on_write` hits when the consumer is still behind at the moment the broker is stopped: all 100000 rows were published and acknowledged into the stream, but the ones not yet delivered are never fetched again, so the view stays short of them and the test fails with `ClickHouse lost some messages: 92807`. It fails this way on about 0.2% of runs since the NATS tests came back on 2026-07-30, and at the same rate before and after #112828 recovered the closed-subscription case on 2026-08-13 (88 of 46693 runs before, 27 of 15428 after), which is what points at the window that fix leaves open. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=c260929910ea94be9a359bb69bf5e33d7b3a40e4&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28arm_binary%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%204%2F4%29 Recovery so far keyed only on a subscription the NATS client had closed, which is what a graceful shutdown produces by answering the outstanding pull request. This reports a reconnect as well, by comparing the reconnect count the client keeps for the connection against the one taken when we subscribed, and re-subscribes through the same path. Only JetStream consumers do this: a core NATS subscription really is restored by the `SUB` line, and re-subscribing it would drop buffered messages nothing redelivers. The recovery is applied both by the background streaming task and by an in-flight direct `SELECT`, whose source retains its consumer until the query finishes. The window this closes is the residual documented in #112828, so `_restart_nats` no longer retries until a restart lands outside it, and a new test reaches that state deterministically with `SIGKILL`, which answers nothing and so leaves no closed subscription to fall back on. Verified locally with a release build, running the module through `ci.praktika`: - new test with the fix: passed twice (65 s, 146 s); - new test with `src/Storages/NATS` reverted to `master` and everything else unchanged: `AssertionError: consumption did not resume, view holds 10 of 20 keys` - the messages published after the restart never arrive; - the five existing restart tests plus `test_nats_restore_failed_connection_without_losses_on_write`, all six passed with the fix. signals.title: Support the short ATTACH syntax for views
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115259 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114747 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `ATTACH VIEW <name>` and `ATTACH MATERIALIZED VIEW <name>` now re-attach a previously detached view from its stored metadata, like `ATTACH TABLE` and `ATTACH DICTIONARY` already did. Previously only `DETACH VIEW` was accepted and the matching `ATTACH` was a syntax error. The definition is read on the node that runs the query, so these spellings are not supported for `ON CLUSTER` queries or in `Replicated` databases; use `ATTACH TABLE` there. Closes #115259. ### Description Requested by @ PedroTadim ([ack](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115259#issuecomment-5327133729)). `VIEW` was the only object kind where `DETACH X <name>` had no matching `ATTACH X <name>`: `ParserCreateTableQuery` has a short-attach shortcut (`ParserCreateQuery.cpp:858`) but `ParserCreateViewQuery` required the body. Added the same shortcut, keeping the view flags for routing. Five interpreter changes follow, each proved on a build carrying only the earlier ones: `createTable` synthesized an empty `sql_security` for any AST whose `supportSQLSecurity()` is true, which the new branch sets, so `has_dropped_clauses` threw `BAD_ARGUMENTS` about a clause nobody wrote; now suppressed for this shape. Three are access checks, because `getRequiredAccess()` authorizes from the typed keyword before metadata is read and `CREATE TABLE` implies `CREATE VIEW`. A `CREATE VIEW`-only user could attach a detached ordinary table, re-attach a stored `DEFINER` view without `SET DEFINER`, and re-attach a `MATERIALIZED VIEW ... TO dst` without the `dst` grant (all measured). So a view-spelled ATTACH whose stored metadata is not a view is rejected, and the loaded `SQL SECURITY` clause and targets are authorized. View spelling only; an `IF NOT EXISTS` no-op needs no such grant. The fifth keeps the view spellings local. `ON CLUSTER` and `Replicated` databases enqueue before the metadata load and the worker has no user, hence full access, so none of those checks can run: measured there, a `CREATE VIEW`-only user re-attached both carriers and read privileged data, where no spelling previously gave a route. `ATTACH TABLE` still works. The check sits in `execute()`, since `distributed_ddl_entry_format_version` below 3 dispatches before `createTable`; authorizing before enqueueing is #111561's question. `ATTACH WINDOW VIEW` keeps its parser gap while #114747 removes `WINDOW VIEW`; since `isView()` covers that kind, a stored Window View is rejected rather than taken. Validation: eight new stateless tests plus a converted arm of `01600_detach_permanently`, each verified to fail without its change; these and four existing tests pass. <details> <summary>Sibling and edge-case matrix</summary> | statement | before | after | |---|---|---| | `ATTACH VIEW v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | re-attaches | | `ATTACH MATERIALIZED VIEW mv` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | re-attaches | | `ATTACH VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | re-attaches, idempotent | | `ATTACH VIEW v ON CLUSTER c` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | `INCORRECT_QUERY`, use `ATTACH TABLE` | | `ATTACH VIEW db.v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | re-attaches | | `ATTACH VIEW v UUID '...'` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | `BAD_ARGUMENTS`, as `ATTACH TABLE t UUID '...'` | | `ATTACH TEMPORARY VIEW v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` (parser) | `SYNTAX_ERROR` (interpreter), as `ATTACH TEMPORARY TABLE` | | `ATTACH VIEW <a table>` | n/a | `INCORRECT_QUERY`, "it is a Table" | | `ATTACH VIEW v` with stored `DEFINER`/`NONE`, caller lacking the grant | n/a | `ACCESS_DENIED` | | `ATTACH WINDOW VIEW wv` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | unchanged, see #114747 | | `ATTACH VIEW <a stored WINDOW VIEW>` | n/a | `INCORRECT_QUERY`, use `ATTACH TABLE` | | `ATTACH OR REPLACE VIEW v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | unchanged | | `ATTACH SQL SECURITY INVOKER VIEW v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | unchanged | | `ATTACH DEFINER = u VIEW v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | unchanged | | `DETACH MATERIALIZED VIEW mv` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | unchanged, out of scope | | `ATTACH VIEW v` in a `Replicated` database | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | `INCORRECT_QUERY`, use `ATTACH TABLE` | | `ATTACH TABLE <a detached view>` | works | works | | `ATTACH TABLE`/`DICTIONARY`/`DATABASE`, incl. `ON CLUSTER` | works | works | </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow signals.title: Keep one output port per shard when a JOIN side reads nothing
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115057 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109393 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Join is supported only for pipelines with one output port`) for a `full_sorting_merge` JOIN with `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges` enabled when one of the two sides is pruned to no parts at all - by the primary key, by column statistics, or because the table is empty. ### Description A JOIN sharded by primary-key ranges pairs the shards of its two sides positionally, so both sides have to produce exactly one output port per layer. `optimizeJoinByShards` builds the layers from the parts of all the sources at once and hands every source the same number of them, and `ReadFromMergeTree::readByLayers` keeps the port of an empty layer occupied by substituting a `NullSource` for it. That invariant did not hold for a source that reads nothing at all: `ReadFromMergeTree::initializePipeline` replaced the whole side with a single `NullSource` before it ever reached the layers. A side pruned to zero parts therefore arrived at the JOIN with one port while the other side kept its layers, the stream counts disagreed, `JoinStep` stopped using sharding, and the `YShaped` pipeline it went to instead accepts only a single port per side: ``` Logical error: 'Join is supported only for pipelines with one output port, got 1 and 2' ``` The fix emits one `NullSource` per layer, so the number of ports stays what the plan says it is. The layers are only ever set by `optimizeJoinByShards` (gated by `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges`, off by default) and are ignored for a read coordinated across parallel replicas, so for every other query the pipeline is unchanged. The comment at the `JoinStep` fallback claimed that the regular pipeline handles diverging stream counts. That is true for `joinPipelinesRightLeft` (hash) but not for the merge-join path, and it is what made the missing invariant look intentional, so it is corrected as well. This replaces the approach in #109393, which merged the diverging streams back together inside `joinPipelinesYShaped`; @vdimir asked there for the invariant to be fixed at its source instead, which is what this pull request does. The throw in `joinPipelinesYShaped` is left in place. Reproducer (the second query is the shape from the CI report - the sharded side keeps its layers while the other side is pruned away): ```sql CREATE TABLE t_l (k UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k SETTINGS index_granularity = 128; CREATE TABLE t_r (k UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k SETTINGS index_granularity = 128; INSERT INTO t_l SELECT number FROM numbers(1000); INSERT INTO t_r SELECT number FROM numbers(1000); SET query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges = 1, join_algorithm = 'full_sorting_merge', max_threads = 4; SELECT count() FROM t_l AS l JOIN (SELECT * FROM t_r WHERE k > 1000000) AS r ON l.k = r.k; SELECT count() FROM (SELECT * FROM t_l WHERE k > 1000000) AS l LEFT JOIN t_r AS r ON l.k = r.k; ``` ### How the CI report maps onto this The failing test in the report is `03447_analyzer_correlated_subqueries_tpc_h` (TPC-H Q2), run by the settings randomizer with `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges = 1` and `join_algorithm = 'full_sorting_merge'`. Replaying that query with the report's own settings, `EXPLAIN PLAN indexes=1` shows the sharded join with one side gone: ``` Join (JOIN YShaped) part ⋈ partsupp Join conditions: p_partkey = ps_partkey Sharding: [(p_partkey = ps_partkey)] ├── ReadFromMergeTree (part) Parts: 0 | Granules: 0 <- pruned by the statistics on p_size └── ReadFromMergeTree (partsupp) Parts: 1 | Granules: 1 ``` `part` is pruned to `Parts: 0` and collapses to a single port; `partsupp` keeps one port per layer. CI report this starts from: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=172d9bf947f5081ddd3288073fe0cf6be664b924&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_debug%29 The stack is one of the most frequent stress and AST-fuzzer failures at the moment: 57 hits of this exact `STID 4488-4e11` since 2026-05-27 (5 of them on master), plus 21 more of the two sibling stacks `4488-4590` and `4488-4a91`. ### Verification - The reproducer above, the one from #115057, and the new test `05019_join_shard_by_pk_ranges_pruned_side` all abort on a master binary (`got 4 and 1`) and pass with the fix. - The new test also compares the sharded result against `join_algorithm = 'hash'` with `count()` plus a `cityHash64` checksum for the `LEFT`/`RIGHT` cases, where every row of the surviving side reaches the output. This covers the semantics of the padded pipeline, not only the disappearance of the exception. - TPC-H Q2 from `03447_analyzer_correlated_subqueries_tpc_h` with the report's full settings passes. - All 1061 local stateless tests matching `join`, and the primary-key-sharding tests (`03357`, `03668`, `03774`, `04065`, `04251`, `04517`, `04655`, `04812`), pass. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115352&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115352](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115352+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1724` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->
