signal.title: Mongo queries: keep whole documents in a JSON column
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/68493 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/58394 Adds two ways to run MongoDB queries against ClickHouse: - a **wire protocol endpoint** (`mongo_port`), so MongoDB drivers and tools such as `pymongo` and `mongosh` can connect to ClickHouse as if it were a MongoDB server; - a **query dialect** (`SET dialect = 'mongo'`), so MongoDB shell syntax can be sent over the usual ClickHouse interfaces. This continues @scanhex12's https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/68493 - it holds all of its commits - and changes how a collection is stored, which is what the review of that pull request asked for (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/68493#discussion_r3771132310): a collection the endpoint creates keeps whole documents in one `JSON` column rather than a column inferred per field of the first document. ```sql CREATE TABLE db.users (`_id` String, `json` JSON) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY `_id` ``` The document goes into the `JSON` column, whose paths are its fields, and its object id into the `_id` column, which is the primary key. A document may then hold a field that no document before it had, may leave out a field another one has, and `$exists` answers what it means. A table that was created in ClickHouse keeps its own columns, and a field of a query names the column of the same name there, so an application can also be pointed at a table that already holds the data. A read of the documents as they are stored selects them next to the types of their paths, so a date reads back as a BSON date and an integer as an `int32`/`int64` of its width. The integration tests of `test_mongo_protocol` say what each shape answers now - a collection of documents where that is what is tested, a table created in ClickHouse where the test is about a column - and 75/75 of them pass. **This is a draft** because a few things of a document collection are an explicit error rather than an answer: an `update` of it, an index over a path, the `mongo` dialect over it, the element-wise match of an array by equality or `$in`, `$unwind` of a path, and the accumulators that read a number. They are the next commits; every one of them is listed in `docs/en/interfaces/mongo.md` and pinned by a test in the meantime. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a MongoDB-compatible wire protocol endpoint (the `mongo_port` server setting) and a MongoDB query dialect (`SET dialect = 'mongo'`) for basic collection operations. signal.title: Fix gRPC and Arrow Flight listeners for wildcard listen hosts
signal.text: `gRPC` treats `::` and `0.0.0.0` as one family-agnostic wildcard: for either of them it binds a dual-stack `::` socket, and falls back to `0.0.0.0` only on a host without IPv6 (see `add_wildcard_addrs_to_server` in `contrib/grpc`). Listing both wildcard addresses in `listen_host` therefore made ClickHouse create two listeners that bind the very same socket address, and the second one either - failed with `EADDRINUSE`, because the Arrow Flight transport disables `SO_REUSEPORT`, and the exception terminated the whole server: ``` <Error> grpc: Failed to add port to server: No address added out of total 1 resolved for '0.0.0.0:9110' (Failed to add any wildcard listeners: Error in bind for address '[::]:9110': Address already in use Error in bind for address '0.0.0.0:9110': Address already in use) <Error> Application: Code: 1002. DB::Exception: Failed init Arrow Flight Server: Unknown error: Server did not start properly. ``` - or silently shared the port with the first one, because plain gRPC keeps `SO_REUSEPORT` enabled, so each of the two independent servers ended up serving a random half of the connections, and a listener configured for `0.0.0.0` accepted IPv6 connections as well: ``` <Information> Application: Listening for gRPC protocol: [::]:9100 <Information> Application: Listening for gRPC protocol: 0.0.0.0:9100 LISTEN 0 4096 *:9100 users:(("clickhouse",pid=3851032,fd=55)) LISTEN 0 4096 *:9100 users:(("clickhouse",pid=3851032,fd=56)) ``` Only one gRPC and one Arrow Flight listener is created for a group of wildcard `listen_host` values now, which is what the transport does internally anyway. Also, `listen_try` is honored for the protocols that bind their listening socket when they are started rather than when they are created. `EADDRINUSE` from gRPC or Arrow Flight was reported from the plain `server.start()` loop, outside of the `createServer` handler that implements `listen_try`, so it was fatal even with `listen_try` (and with `listen_reuse_port`) enabled - which contradicts the documented behavior of listening to at least one of the addresses without quitting. Not addressed here: plain gRPC still keeps `SO_REUSEPORT` enabled, so a gRPC port that is already taken by a different process is silently shared instead of reported. Making that consistent with `listen_reuse_port` for both gRPC and Arrow Flight is a possible follow-up. For the record, gRPC and Arrow Flight are not available as composable protocols (the `protocols` section): the composable stack is a Poco `TCPServer` with a chain of `TCPServerConnectionFactory` layers that receive an already accepted socket, while gRPC and Arrow Flight own the listening socket, the HTTP/2 framing, TLS and their own event loop, so they can neither be a layer nor sit under `tls` / `proxy1`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix the server failing to start when `listen_host` contains both `::` and `0.0.0.0` and `arrowflight_port` is configured, and fix two gRPC listeners silently sharing one port in the same configuration. `listen_try` now also covers the gRPC and Arrow Flight protocols, which bind their listening socket when they are started. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115074&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115074](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115074+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Automatic LowCardinality serialization based on uniq statistics
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/85145 --> This PR adds automatic `LowCardinality` serialization for `MergeTree`, analogous to the existing automatic `Sparse` serialization. A `String` or `FixedString` column whose declared type is **not** `LowCardinality` can now be stored on disk in dictionary-encoded form when it has a `uniq` statistic with a low cardinality estimate. The encoding is transparent: the column keeps its declared data type, flows through the query pipeline as a (non-native) `ColumnLowCardinality`, and is materialized to a full column at the boundaries that require it. **Motivation:** save disk space and read I/O for low-cardinality string columns without requiring users to declare the column type as `LowCardinality(...)`. **How it works** - A new per-part serialization kind `LOW_CARDINALITY` (shown as `LowCardinality` in `system.parts_columns.serialization_kind`). - The decision is made at write time from the **existing** `uniq` statistic — there are **no changes to statistics serialization**. In `MergeTreeDataWriter`, a `String`/`FixedString` column whose `uniq` estimate does not exceed the new `MergeTree` setting `max_uniq_number_for_low_cardinality` (default `0` = disabled), and which was not already chosen for `Sparse`, is stored with `SerializationLowCardinality`. The column must therefore declare `STATISTICS(uniq)` and have `materialize_statistics_on_insert` enabled. - A new `is_native` flag on `ColumnLowCardinality` makes `getDataType` report the nested type, so the "column class matches data type" invariant holds while such a column flows through the pipeline. It is materialized to a full column in `removeSpecialRepresentations` (aggregation, joins, squashing, blocks), in the merge-input step of `IMergingAlgorithm`, in the sorting and sparse-removing transforms, and in `IFunction`. The `optimize_functions_to_subcolumns` pass skips columns stored as non-native `LowCardinality`, since the dictionary encoding does not expose the data type's regular subcolumns. - The kind is independent of sparse serialization: `SerializationInfo` entries for eligible columns are created in the writer, in merges, in mutations and in the per-table serialization hints even when `ratio_of_defaults_for_sparse_serialization = 1` disables `Sparse` entirely. **Notes** - Opt-in: disabled by default and requires an explicit `uniq` statistic, so existing tables are unaffected. Requires `allow_experimental_statistics`. - Reading a subcolumn of an encoded column (for example `s.size`) is not supported and reports `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`: the subcolumn's streams do not exist in a dictionary-encoded part. Making it read the full column and extract the subcolumn in memory needs a dedicated serialization and is left for a separate change. - Extracts and reimplements the automatic `LowCardinality` part of the draft #85145 against current `master`, without the statistics-serialization refactoring. That refactoring is still unmerged (#85145 and #109128 are open drafts). Validated locally with a server built from this branch: kind selection for `Wide` and `Compact` parts, `String` and `FixedString`, query correctness, functions, `GROUP BY`/`ORDER BY`/`DISTINCT`/`LIMIT BY`/window functions, joins, `IN` subqueries, `INSERT SELECT`, `UNION ALL`, `OPTIMIZE FINAL` (LowCardinality preserved through merges), mutations, `ALTER RENAME`/`MODIFY COLUMN`, `DETACH`/`ATTACH`, `PREWHERE`, input/output formats with and without `allow_special_serialization_kinds_in_output_formats`, and tables with mixed `Default` and `LowCardinality` active parts. The three tests also pass with `ratio_of_defaults_for_sparse_serialization` forced to `0.0` and `1.0`, with `enable_block_offset_column`/`enable_block_number_column`, with compact parts, and over repeated fully randomized runs. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added automatic `LowCardinality` serialization: a `String`/`FixedString` column that has a `uniq` statistic and low cardinality can be stored in dictionary-encoded form on disk while keeping its declared data type. Controlled by the new `MergeTree` setting `max_uniq_number_for_low_cardinality` (disabled by default). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107436&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/107436](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F107436+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Allow Map data type for asynchronous metrics
signal.text: <!--- A technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created The following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly utils/changelog/changelog.py tests/ci/cancel_and_rerun_workflow_lambda/app.py --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Asynchronous metrics can now have the `Map` data type, and the per-CPU-core and per-device metrics were converted to single key-value metrics: `OSUserTimeCPU0`, `OSUserTimeCPU1`, ... became a single `OSUserTimeCPU` metric with a map from the CPU core number to the value (and similarly for the other `OS*TimeCPU*` metrics, `CPUFrequencyMHz_*`, `Temperature*`, `EDAC*`, `Block*_*`, `Network(Receive|Send)*_*`, `Disk*_*`, `*BlobsQueueEstimate`, and `AsyncLogging*QueueSize`). `system.asynchronous_metrics` has a new `key_values Map(String, Float64)` column (the `value` column is `NaN` for such metrics), `system.asynchronous_metric_log` logs them as one row per key using a new `key` column, the Prometheus endpoint exports them with a label (e.g. `ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_BlockReadBytes{device="sda"}`), and the Graphite `MetricsTransmitter` sends them as `<prefix>.<Metric>.<key>`. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115321 Some metrics are per CPU core or per device (block device, network interface, disk, temperature sensor, EDAC memory controller, logging channel), and they were published as separate metrics with the entity name mangled into the metric name (`CPUFrequencyMHz_0`, `BlockReadBytes_sda`, `DiskTotal_default`, ...). This pollutes the metric namespace (hundreds of metrics on large machines), makes the set of metric names unstable across servers, and makes aggregation across entities awkward. Now each such family is a single key-value metric. ### Details **Data model.** `AsynchronousMetricValue` gains `key_values` (an ordered map from the entity name to the value) and `key_label` (what the key means: `cpu`, `device`, `interface`, `disk`, `sensor`, `mc`, `channel`; it is also used as the Prometheus label name). A metric is either scalar or key-value. **`system.asynchronous_metrics`.** A new column `key_values Map(String, Float64)` holds the values of a key-value metric; the `value` column is `NaN` for them (an aggregate across entities like a sum is not meaningful for every metric, e.g. `CPUFrequencyMHz` or `Temperature`, so none is invented). Example: ``` SELECT metric, key_values FROM system.asynchronous_metrics WHERE metric = 'CPUFrequencyMHz' ``` I considered making the `value` column `Dynamic` (holding either `Float64` or `Map(String, Float64)`), but it breaks the most common query patterns: `WHERE value > 0` throws `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` as soon as any row holds a Map, and `avg(value)` stops working. **`system.asynchronous_metric_log`.** A key-value metric is logged as one row per key via a new `key LowCardinality(String)` column (empty for scalar metrics). This keeps `value Float64` (and its compression), and time-series aggregation stays natural: `WHERE metric = 'BlockReadBytes' AND key = 'sda'`, or `sum(value) ... GROUP BY key`. The default `ORDER BY` of the table is now `metric, key, event_date, event_time`. On upgrade, the old table is renamed and a new one is created by the standard system-log schema-mismatch mechanism. **Prometheus.** Key-value metrics are exported as one line per key with a proper label instead of a mangled name: `ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_BlockReadBytes{device="sda"} 123` (merged with the configured constant labels; label values are escaped). **Graphite (`MetricsTransmitter`).** Key-value metrics are sent one path component deeper: `<prefix>.BlockReadBytes.sda`. **Converted metric families** ("change it where reasonable"): - `OS{User,Nice,System,Idle,IOWait,Irq,SoftIrq,Steal,Guest,GuestNice}TimeCPU<n>` → `OS*TimeCPU` keyed by the core number (the all-core sums `OSUserTime` etc. are unchanged) - `CPUFrequencyMHz_<n>` → `CPUFrequencyMHz` - `Temperature<n>` (thermal zones, numeric keys) and `Temperature_<hwmon>[_<sensor>]` (name keys) → a single `Temperature` metric - `EDAC<n>_{Correctable,Uncorrectable}` → `EDAC{Correctable,Uncorrectable}` keyed by the memory controller number - all 17 `Block*_<device>` families → `Block*` keyed by the device name - all 8 `Network{Receive,Send}*_<interface>` families → keyed by the interface name - `Disk{Total,Used,Available,Unreserved}_<disk>` and `Disk{Put,Get}ObjectThrottler{RPS,Available}_<disk>` → keyed by the disk name - `<disk>DeadBlobsQueueEstimate`, `<disk>MissingBlobsQueueEstimate` → `DeadBlobsQueueEstimate`, `MissingBlobsQueueEstimate` keyed by the disk name - `AsyncLogging<Channel>QueueSize` → `AsyncLoggingQueueSize` keyed by the channel name Left as-is (small bounded sets rather than per-device breakdowns): `PSI_*`, `NetworkTCPSockets_<STATE>`, per-protocol thread/rejected-connection metrics, `HTTPConnectionPool<Group>*`, jemalloc arena metrics. **Dashboards.** The only dashboard queries that used suffixed names are the four "Network receive/send bytes/sec" charts of the Cloud overview dashboards, which use `metric LIKE 'NetworkReceiveBytes%'` with `sum(value)` per time point. They are left unchanged deliberately: the `LIKE` pattern matches both the old suffixed rows and the new per-key rows, so the charts stay correct and continuous across the upgrade. The Web UI dashboard (`dashboard.html`) does not hardcode any metric names. **Docs.** The metric list in `docs/reference/system-tables/asynchronous_metrics.mdx` is regenerated by `utils/generate-async-metrics-docs`; the columns of both system tables are documented. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115333&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115333](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115333+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix SLRU cache admitting no new entries once max_count entries were used twice
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed caches configured by a maximum number of entries (`SLRU` policy) silently stopping to admit new entries once that many entries had been accessed at least twice. Affected caches include the Iceberg and Paimon metadata file caches, the Parquet metadata cache, the text index caches, the vector similarity index cache, the compiled expression cache and the ObjectStorageQueue file status cache. ### Description Found by reading `SLRUCachePolicy`'s eviction arithmetic; there is no public issue for it. The case below rests only on the source and on the added test, which fails on unpatched master. `SLRUCachePolicy` bounds its protected queue by bytes (`max_protected_size`) but has no count equivalent, so the protected arm of `removeOverflow` compares the protected queue's size against `max_count`, the *total* entry limit. The probationary arm runs last on every `set()` and already enforces `cells.size() <= max_count`, which makes that comparison unsatisfiable: the protected queue is never shrunk under count pressure. Once `max_count` entries have each been accessed twice (a second `set`, or any `get`, promotes an entry), the protected queue holds all of them. The next insertion overflows, and the only eviction candidate in the probationary queue is the entry just inserted. Lowering `max_entries` at runtime reaches the same state at once, because `setMaxCount` demotes the protected queue to exactly `max_count` entries. The fix bounds protected count the way protected bytes already is: `max_protected_count = min(trunc(max_count * size_ratio), max_count - 1)`, so the probationary queue always keeps one slot, and recomputes it in `setMaxCount`. `SLRUFileCachePriority` ratio-splits both `max_size_` and `max_elements_` the same way. `cells.size() <= max_count` is unchanged, so `max_entries` keeps its meaning and no setting is added. Eviction behaviour does change for the affected caches: a protected entry can now be demoted to probationary under count pressure, where previously only byte pressure could. That is what makes these caches admit new entries at all. Splitting the count bound by `size_ratio` mirrors the byte side rather than following from a measurement. The existing suite exercised the count limit only with distinct keys, where entries stay probationary and the protected queue stays empty, so the defect was unreachable. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115517&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115517](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115517+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Implement PromQL range functions present_over_time, absent_over_time, quantile_over_time and predict_linear
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/57545 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): PromQL: implemented range functions `present_over_time()`, `absent_over_time()`, `quantile_over_time()` and `predict_linear()`. ### Description Implements four PromQL functions over range vectors that were previously rejected with a not-implemented error: - `present_over_time(v range-vector)` — for each grid point, `1` if its staleness window contains at least one sample, otherwise the series is dropped. - `absent_over_time(v range-vector)` — an empty vector if the range vector has any samples, otherwise a 1-element synthetic series with value `1` and the labels inferred from the selector's equality matchers (matching Prometheus `absent_over_time` / `absent` semantics). - `quantile_over_time(phi scalar, v range-vector)` — the φ-quantile of the sample values in each grid point's window, computed with the R-7 (inclusive) method (`quantileExactInclusive`). φ outside `[0, 1]` yields ±Inf and NaN φ yields NaN, as in Prometheus. - `predict_linear(v range-vector, t scalar)` — simple linear regression over the in-window samples, extrapolated `t` seconds past the evaluation time. **Implementation** - Two new grid aggregate functions: - `timeSeriesPresentToGrid` — `1` if a window has any sample, else `NULL`. - `timeSeriesQuantileToGrid` — R-7 inclusive quantile over a window (non-invertible summary that collects window values and sorts them in `getResult`). Both are registered inline in `AggregateFunctionTimeseriesHelpers.cpp`. `predict_linear` reuses the existing `timeSeriesPredictLinearToGrid` aggregate (the `is_predict` variant of the linear-regression aggregate). - `present_over_time` is wired through `applyFunctionOverRange`'s `impl_map`. `quantile_over_time` and `predict_linear` have dedicated translators because they take an extra scalar argument. - `absent_over_time` builds a per-series presence grid via `present_over_time`, then at runtime counts present series per grid point (`countForEach`) and inverts the result, so it works whether or not the metric exists (a selector on a missing metric is a runtime subquery, not a compile-time-empty one). Output labels are derived from the selector's matchers, like `absent()`. No parser changes were needed — the grammar already accepts these function names and `getFunctionResultType` already returns the correct result types. **Testing**: new parser cases in `gtest_PromQLParser.cpp` for `present_over_time` and `absent_over_time` (`quantile_over_time` / `predict_linear` were already covered); new stateless test `04551_promql_phase3_range_functions.sh` exercising all four functions (present/absent, quantile at φ = 0 / 0.5 / 1, predict_linear at offsets 0 and 60) against a multi-series TimeSeries table, with values verified against Prometheus semantics. **Update: time-varying `predict_offset` / `phi`** `predict_linear`'s `t` and `quantile_over_time`'s `phi` now also accept a per-grid-point-varying PromQL scalar (e.g. `time()` in a range query), not just a constant or single-row scalar. This is handled by two new, self-contained aggregate functions, `timeSeriesPredictLinearVaryingToGrid` / `timeSeriesQuantileVaryingToGrid`, which take the varying value as a 3rd `Array(Float64)` argument instead of a fixed aggregate parameter (ClickHouse aggregate parameters are bound once per instance and can't vary per row). They're isolated from `AggregateFunctionTimeseriesBase` (shared by ~10 other `timeSeries*ToGrid` functions) to avoid regression risk to those. Since these are public SQL aggregate functions, not just an internal translator detail, they validate that the 3rd-argument array is identical across every row/merged state and throw `BAD_ARGUMENTS` otherwise, rather than silently using whichever array was seen first. **Scope note**: the varying value is normalized to `Array(Float64)` in the translator so it works for `Float32`-valued `TimeSeries` tables too, not just `Float64`. However, the PromQL scalar's *own* grid representation (`fromFunctionTime.cpp`'s `SCALAR_GRID` output for `time()`) is cast to `Array(scalar_data_type)`, which is the *table's value type* — for a `Float32`-valued table, that means `time()`'s own raw values (Unix timestamps, ~1.7e9) already lose precision (~128-unit rounding at that magnitude) before my code ever sees them. This is a pre-existing property of `scalar_data_type` being shared between value-precision and timestamp-scalar-precision, not something this change introduces, but this change is what makes it reachable for `predict_offset`/`phi`. It only matters when the varying value is derived from a large absolute number (like raw `time()`) on a `Float32` table; typical `phi` (`[0, 1]`) or `predict_offset` (seconds-scale) formulas aren't affected. Fixing the root cause would mean changing `fromFunctionTime.cpp`'s shared `SCALAR_GRID` representation, which has ~15 other callers — out of scope here. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112842&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112842](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112842+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Preserve execution limits and resources in derived QueryPlans
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107619 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107924 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Preserve execution limits and resource lifetimes when deriving `QueryPlan` instances for internal query execution. ### Description The non-destructive in-place set-build fix from https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107924 is already on `master`; this follow-up fixes the remaining `QueryPlan` propagation and lifetime invariants. `QueryPlan::clone` and `QueryPlan::extractSubplan` previously copied or moved only the node tree. The HTTP `make_distributed_plan` set-build behavior described in the remaining review thread is intentionally out of scope: it is a pre-existing `QueryPlan::convertToDistributed` boundary unrelated to this follow-up, and the native protocol re-applies concurrency control after pipeline construction. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109722&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/109722](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F109722+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix std::out_of_range when a space-filling curve is not a key column
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `std::out_of_range: map::at: key not found` when a `MergeTree` key expression contains a `mortonEncode` or `hilbertEncode` call that is not itself a key column, for example `ORDER BY mortonEncode(hilbertEncode(x, y), x, y)` or `PARTITION BY mortonEncode(x, y) % 4`. ### Description `KeyCondition::getAllSpaceFillingCurves` walks every action of the key-expression DAG and looks up each curve node in `key_columns` with `at()`. `key_columns` holds only top-level key columns, so a curve nested inside another expression is an intermediate node whose `result_name` is absent, and the lookup throws out of `KeyCondition`'s constructor. Such a table accepts `CREATE` and `INSERT`, then rejects almost every read. On released `26.7.4.14` with `ORDER BY mortonEncode(hilbertEncode(x, y), x, y)`, `SELECT *`, `SELECT count() WHERE x = 5` and `SELECT sum(y)` all fail with `Code: 1001` and `ALTER TABLE ... DELETE` with `Code: 341`; only a bare `count()` works. Debug and sanitizer builds abort instead. It reproduces on `25.8.30.12` (LTS), `26.6.3.28` and `26.7.4.14`, so it is not new. A curve is only ever consumed through `key_column_pos` as a key column index, so one that is not a key column cannot participate in curve-aware key analysis at all. Rather than catch the failed lookup, the fix restricts the enumeration to curve nodes that are key columns, using the `key_columns.find` form already used at the five other lookups here. Line 1386 was the file's only unconditional `at()` on `key_columns`. Three construction sites reach that line and are all fixed: the primary/sorting key, the partition key, and minmax/set skip indexes. Nothing that worked before changes: for `ORDER BY mortonEncode(x, y)`, and for a nested curve that is also a key column, `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` is byte-identical before and after, so curve pruning is preserved. signal.title: Log a query_views_log row for a view that failed before it was fully built
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104444 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a missing `system.query_views_log` row for a materialized view that fails while its dependencies are being collected with `materialized_views_ignore_errors` enabled. In debug and sanitizer builds this also aborts the server with `std::out_of_range` instead of logging the view. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104444 `InsertDependenciesBuilder::logQueryView` guards three maps before building the log element, but the element builder read five: it also did `select_queries.at(view_id)` and `select_contexts.at(view_id)`, neither of which the guard covered. `observePath` fills `select_contexts` last, so a view throwing while its select context is created keeps all three guarded maps populated and that one absent. The `catch (...)` in `collectAllDependencies` (reached only with `materialized_views_ignore_errors = 1`) then calls `logQueryView` on exactly that half-built view, the guard passes, and `.at()` throws `std::out_of_range`. The local `catch (...)` logs through `tryLogCurrentException`, so a debug or sanitizer build turns that into `abortOnFailedAssertion` and the server aborts. A release build only logs it, and the visible defect there is a missing `system.query_views_log` row. The fix builds the element from what is available. The select query is stored before the select context, so on this path the query is present and only the context is missing; a helper formats the stored query with `init_context`, which supplies the `log_queries_cut_to_length` cut-off `getCleanQueryAst` reads from it and which `logQueryView` already uses for every other logging setting. An empty `view_query` is reserved for a genuinely absent AST. Extending the guard instead would drop the whole row, removing the `ExceptionBeforeStart` record precisely when a view failed. The other three `logQueryView` call sites read the same field and are covered by the same change. They run only for views that reached chain construction, so were never separately affected. Found by `Stress test (amd_debug)` on an unrelated PR, STID `2508-3f5e`: [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110073&sha=5d28dfdf72dde6d0df0944be7fcdaa50fa0c6944&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_debug%29). Validated with a deterministic reproducer, added as a regression test: renaming a view's definer leaves the stored `DEFINER` name unresolvable, throwing from the statement that assigns the select context. Pristine master aborts with the CI stack; with the fix the server stays up and logs one `ExceptionBeforeStart` row keeping the view's query. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1728` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Report cancellation instead of leaving an in-place set unbuilt
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114463 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107619 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'` error when a query with `partial_result_on_first_cancel = 1` was cancelled while the set of an `IN (subquery)` was still being built. ### Description Follow-up to https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114463, asked for in its review. That pull request makes a cancelled mutation report `ABORTED` instead of stopping its nested pipelines silently; the review asked whether the same silent stop is still reachable through the other two interactive-cancel callbacks. I measured both. One is, one is not. **Reachable: `partial_result_on_first_cancel`.** For the first cancel, `TCPHandler::processCancel` only sets `stop_read_return_partial_result` and deliberately does not cancel the query through the process list, so the callback returns a bare `true` (`TCPHandler.cpp:897-898`). `CompletedPipelineExecutor::execute` then cancels the nested set-build pipeline and its poll loop returns normally, so `CreatingSetsTransform::generate` never runs `Set::finishInsert`, while `FutureSetFromSubquery::build` has already moved the source plan out. A caller that evaluates its filter in the same call passes the unbuilt set to `FunctionIn`. On master (`f45871c7cfa`), one cancel during ```sql SELECT count() FROM t WHERE 1 IN (SELECT number FROM numbers(10000000) WHERE sleep(1) = 0) SETTINGS partial_result_on_first_cancel = 1, optimize_use_implicit_projections = 1, optimize_trivial_count_query = 0 ``` reports ``` Code: 49. DB::Exception: Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in' ... (LOGICAL_ERROR) ``` through `FunctionIn` (`in.cpp:116`) <- `VirtualColumnUtils::filterBlockWithExpression` (`:162`) <- `MergeTreeData::getMinMaxCountProjectionBlock` (`:10463`) <- `optimizeUseAggregateProjections` (`:630`). A debug or sanitizer build aborts on it. **Not reachable: `clickhouse-local`.** Its callback cancels the query through the process list element (`LocalConnection.cpp:191-194`), so the nested pipeline fails instead of stopping silently. The same query interrupted with `SIGINT` reports `Code: 394. DB::Exception: Query was cancelled` on master, with `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` confirming the plan is the `minmax_count` projection. That installer is untouched here. `FutureSetFromSubquery::buildSetInplace` now records whether the cancel callback fired and, if the set was left uncreated, reports `QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED` instead of returning to a caller that cannot distinguish a cancelled build from a completed one. Both conditions are required on purpose, so a set build that stops for a reason other than a cancellation keeps the behaviour it has today. Measured over the routes that stop such a pipeline early: `set_overflow_mode = 'break'`, `transfer_overflow_mode = 'break'` and `read_overflow_mode = 'break'` all still reach `CreatingSetsTransform::generate`, which finishes the set, and the query returns its result; `set_overflow_mode = 'throw'` still reports `SET_SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. For `partial_result_on_first_cancel` this means such a query now fails with `QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED` rather than with the logical error. There is no partial answer to return instead: the cancellation lands during analysis, before a row is produced, and an incomplete `IN` set would silently change the result. The mutation path keeps reporting `ABORTED` as #114463 makes it: its callback throws before this check is reached, which names the mutation the way `MergeTask::checkOperationIsNotCanceled` does and covers every nested pipeline a mutation runs, not only `buildSetInplace`. The ordered variant `buildOrderedSetInplace` needs nothing: #107924 made it build against a clone of the source plan and publish only a created set, so a silently stopped ordered build just skips index analysis. Out of scope, found while measuring this and reported here rather than fixed: a *time limit* with `break` reaches the same logical error without any cancellation, because the limit stops the set-build pipeline the same way. On master, ```sql SELECT count() FROM t WHERE 1 IN (SELECT number FROM numbers(1000)) SETTINGS optimize_use_implicit_projections = 1, optimize_trivial_count_query = 0, max_execution_time = 0.0001, timeout_overflow_mode = 'break' ``` reports `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'` too. The check added here deliberately does not cover it: `break` asks for a truncated result rather than an error, so what a partially built `IN` set should do - report the limit, or silently use the rows read so far, as `set_overflow_mode = 'break'` already does - is a semantic decision, and it is not what this pull request is about. Happy to open an issue or a follow-up for it. New test `04909_cancel_in_subquery_set_build_partial_result`. It asserts up front that the `minmax_count` projection is the plan for the predicate shape under test, so it cannot pass without exercising the synchronous filter evaluation, and both of its wait loops fail loudly rather than cancelling something else. The oracle is the reported outcome, not the survival of the server, so it is live on release builds too. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115083&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115083](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115083+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Disable the sampling query profiler under Memory Sanitizer
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/100242 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106591 Every `MemorySanitizer` report produced in CI since 2026-05-28 is truncated to a single line: ``` ==117==WARNING: MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value MemorySanitizer: nested bug in the same thread, aborting. ``` No stack trace, no `SUMMARY`, no origin — so no MSan failure can be located. In the CI database, `msan` checks recorded 1009 reports with a usable stack in 2026-04 and 0 in 2026-07, while `asan`, `tsan` and `ubsan` reports are unaffected and still carry full stacks. The regression window matches #100242 (merged 2026-05-28), which enabled the sampling query profiler for sanitizer builds. Printing an MSan report takes the sanitizer runtime seconds, because it symbolizes every frame through an `llvm-symbolizer` subprocess, and it holds `ScopedErrorReportLock` for the whole time. A profiler signal delivered to that thread meanwhile runs instrumented code in the handler and trips a second MSan check; compiler-rt treats a same-thread re-entry into the report lock as unrecoverable, writes `nested bug in the same thread, aborting.` with `CatastrophicErrorWrite` and calls `internal__exit`, so the report that was already being written to `MSAN_OPTIONS=log_path` stops after its header line. Reproduced with the `arm_msan` binary built from master `3885f7b7bbf1`, running the same query against the same server three times and forcing a sanitizer report with `max_allocation_size_mb=32 allocator_may_return_null=0`: | configuration | result | | --- | --- | | profiler on (default `global_profiler_real_time_period_ns`) | `nested bug in the same thread, aborting.`, 1-line report | | `<trace_log remove="1"/>` (no profiler at all) | full 31-line report with stack | | `trace_log` on, `global_profiler_*_period_ns = 0`, per-query profiler off | full 31-line report with stack | So it is the profiler timer signals, not the trace collector. This turns `QUERY_PROFILER_SUPPORTED` off under MSan, next to the existing TSan-on-macOS exclusion. The trace collector stays enabled: the memory profiler, `trace_profile_events` and `SYSTEM INSTRUMENT` all feed it from ordinary code rather than from a signal handler. Other sanitizers keep the profiler, because their checks fire only on genuinely invalid accesses, which the handler does not perform. `00974_query_profiler` and `01569_query_profiler_big_query_id` assert that samples reach `system.trace_log`, so they get `no-msan` back. The other profiler and `trace_log` tests either already carry `no-msan`, exercise the memory profiler / `trace_profile_events` / `SYSTEM INSTRUMENT` (unaffected), or make no assertion on sample counts. This does not fix the uninitialized read that the `BuzzHouse (amd_msan)` run below hit — that one is unidentifiable as reported. It makes the next occurrence diagnosable. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=3885f7b7bbf1b8791021e1c97ca2e4eea132de04&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28amd_msan%29 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113107&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113107](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113107+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix PostgreSQL-protocol authentication for users that also have an ssh_key
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/76839 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix authentication over the PostgreSQL wire protocol for users with several authentication methods: a user that also had an `ssh_key` method (or any other method that stores no password) was rejected with `Invalid user or password` even when the correct password for its `scram_sha256_password` method was supplied, and a wrong SCRAM salt was sent to the client when the SCRAM method was not the last one (e.g. for a user with `scram_sha256_password` followed by `sha256_password`). A user with multiple authentication methods, one of which is `ssh_key`, could not authenticate over the PostgreSQL protocol at all (in either order of the methods), while the same user authenticated fine over the native, MySQL, and HTTP protocols. Reproduced on 26.7.3.19 and current master. Anyone who adds a public SSH key to their user (e.g. for the SSH endpoint) silently loses PostgreSQL access with a misleading "wrong password" error. Two defects, both fixed (each order of methods hits at least one of them): 1. `checkScramSHA256Authentication` did not check the type of the authentication method it verifies the client proof against, and `IAccessStorage::authenticateImpl` calls it for every method of the user. For methods that store no password hash (e.g. `ssh_key`), the empty hash was passed to `hmacSHA256` as the HMAC key; `EVP_MAC_init` fails for a null key, so the check threw `OPENSSL_ERROR` (`Authentication failed: Code: 454. DB::Exception: EVP_MAC_init failed`) instead of returning false, aborting the whole authentication instead of trying the next method of the user. Now it returns false for non-SCRAM methods, the same way `checkMySQLAuthentication` handles non-MySQL-compatible methods. 2. `ScrambleSHA256Auth::authenticate` in the PostgreSQL handler sent the salt of the *last* authentication method of the user instead of the salt of the SCRAM method, so the client derived a salted password that could never match the stored verifier: an empty salt when `ssh_key` was last, or an unrelated random salt when e.g. `sha256_password` was. Now it sends the salt of the first `scram_sha256_password` method. Verified before/after with `psql` against a local server; added an integration test covering both method orders, the `scram_sha256_password` + `sha256_password` combination, and wrong-password rejection. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115084&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115084](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115084+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Wait for the worker cleanup before force-killing the test workers
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113393 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description No related open issue; found while investigating `Stress test (*)` jobs failing with only ` script exit code: 1`. `do_run_tests` stops a run by SIGTERMing each worker and waiting `join(timeout=10)` before SIGKILLing it. That worker's SIGTERM path reaches `kill_process_group`, which on a sanitizer build sleeps **60** seconds, so every worker got 10 seconds for a 60 second cleanup and died inside that sleep. Two consequences. The sanitizer report is truncated, which is what the grace in `1a76ce9b81ce3fc` exists to collect. And `p.kill()` reaches only the worker, not the test's process group, whose PGID file is already unlinked, so the test's `bash` and `clickhouse-client` survive. When the stress harness's random query killer terminates that leaked client, the orphaned `bash` writes `Terminated` into the log file descriptor it inherited, after the parent moved on. If that lands while the job packages the logs, `tar` reports `file changed as we read it` and exits 1, and the job dies *before* the hung check. The wait is now derived from the delays that cleanup sleeps for, so the two cannot drift apart again, and `ddc6bcfbd68a761`'s escalation is unchanged: SIGTERM, bounded wait, SIGKILL, bounded wait. The sanitizer grace is one monotonic deadline shared by all workers, since they clean up concurrently, but no single wait drops below the previous 10 seconds. It is a ceiling, not a sleep, so a prompt worker is not delayed. Worst case is the grace plus 10 seconds a worker. Bounded to those sleeps, so not a guarantee: the stacktrace collection after them is not counted, uninterruptible sleep outlives any budget, and under `spawn` (`aarch` check names) there is no cleanup. A unit test pinning the budget to that delay was removed on review request, so the mechanism now rests on the CI runs that exercise the stop path. <details> <summary>Affected runs, validation, and interaction with #113393</summary> All four are sanitizer lanes over three weeks, `base_ref=master`. In each the worker log stops after the `SANITIZED`-gated print, never reaching the `Killing process group` after the sleep, and the archived log is 11 bytes short. Release and debug lanes, which skip that sleep, show none. - [`57ffb33`, PR 111575, `arm_asan_ubsan`](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111575&sha=57ffb330ff3e3da66a99a2c8dfa6f4a49ffddc27&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29) - [`5639d68`, PR 107736, `arm_tsan`](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107736&sha=5639d68fe32623687d7dba60a6f72a58ffd1603b&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_tsan%29) - [`542bb86`, PR 112951, `arm_msan`](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112951&sha=542bb86022afb31800274d59fcd836d8c7dfc159&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_msan%29) - [`6e15957`, PR 114695, `amd_asan_ubsan`](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114695&sha=6e159579fc017f42673653cf0db45fc03ac9090d&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_asan_ubsan%29) Before the test was removed, eleven mutations each reddened it distinctly (flat 10 seconds, no `kill()` escalation, an unbounded wait, a sleep instead of a ceiling, a per-worker budget, either delay dropped from the sum, the floor removed, a wall-clock deadline, the call site reverted). End to end with real processes, the pre-change shape leaks the worker's `bash` and writes those 11 bytes 3/3; this change eliminates it 3/3. #113393 (mine, open) extracts this same sequence into `quiesce_workers_and_reap()` and keeps `p.join(timeout=10)` verbatim, relocating this defect without fixing it. They are complementary (that one reaps orphaned groups, this one stops creating them) but conflict textually. I can rebase onto it or fold this in there. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115403&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115403](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115403+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

At a minimum, the following information should be added (but add more as needed). - Motivation: Why is this function, table engine, etc. useful to ClickHouse users? - Parameters: If the feature being added takes arguments, options or is influenced by settings, please list them below with a brief explanation. - Example use: A query or command. --> - Motivation: SQL standard has SIMILAR TO predicate that combines SQL LIKE wildcards (%, _) with regular expression metacharacters `|, *, +, ?, [...], {m,n}, (...)`. Note that excluded are `^, $, .`. It is supported by PostgreSQL and others. See the [PostgreSQL documentation on pattern matching](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-matching.html#FUNCTIONS-SIMILARTO-REGEXP) for reference. I also added: negation and substring pattern shortcut. Syntax highlighting is also hooked in to highlight the metacharacters. - Parameters: None. - Example use: ```sql SELECT similarTo('ClickHouse', 'Cl_ck[hH]ouse'); -- Returns: 1 SELECT 'ClickHouse' NOT SIMILAR TO 'Cl%ck[0-9]ouse'; -- Returns: 1 ``` - Corner cases - Character class inside bracket expression. - Bracket expressions don't nest. So `[[:a]]` is invalid, but up to RE2 to process. Addresses https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/99608. <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Adds new SQL operator/function surface area and a new pattern-to-regexp translator, which can affect query parsing and string filtering semantics; risk is moderate due to edge cases in escaping/bracket handling and regex compilation paths. > > **Overview** > Adds SQL-standard `SIMILAR TO` pattern matching (and `NOT SIMILAR TO`) implemented via new `similarToPatternToRegexp()` conversion and new `similarTo`/`notSimilarTo` functions wired into `MatchImpl`/`Regexps::createRegexp`. > > Extends the parser to recognize and pretty-print `SIMILAR TO` / `NOT SIMILAR TO`, updates CNF NOT-pushing inversions, and adds syntax-highlighting support for SIMILAR TO metacharacters. > > Updates call sites to the new `Regexps::createRegexp<like, similar_to, ...>` template signature and expands query fuzzer swap sets plus a new stateless test suite covering SIMILAR TO behavior and corner cases. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit e17d9fd7d3d079c5528a281d7a9af6781ecff4dd. signal.title: Do not treat an existing object as proof that a multipart upload completed
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114348 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113994 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed silent data loss when writing to a fixed S3 key that already holds an object, for example `INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3(...)` with `s3_truncate_on_insert = 1`. If the multipart upload was aborted between create and complete, for example by an `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` lifecycle rule, `CompleteMultipartUpload` correctly returned `NoSuchUpload`, but the error was rewritten to success whenever any object existed at the key, so the INSERT was acknowledged while none of its rows were stored and the previous object kept being served. The error is now only absorbed when the object at the key is the one the upload would have produced. Closes #114348. ### Description Requested by @ zlareb1 in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114348#issuecomment-5255487765. `Client::CompleteMultipartUpload` absorbs `NoSuchUpload` if a `HeadObject` finds any object at the key. That check is from #56475, whose premise is a completion that succeeded and whose response was lost - i.e. the completion was replayed *and* the object is this upload's. Key existence tests neither, so a genuinely aborted upload against a key holding an unrelated object also passes, and the INSERT is acknowledged with none of its rows stored. `NO_SUCH_UPLOAD` is unretryable and excluded from `isTransientCompleteMultipartUploadError`, so this rewrite is the only thing between the abort and a silent success. MergeTree over S3 is unaffected: it writes random unique keys. The rewrite now requires the object to carry the ETag implied by the request's own part list, `md5(concat(binary md5 of each part))-<N>`. No extra request, no new state, and both callers (`WriteBufferFromS3`, `copyS3File`) are fixed at once. It fails closed: when the ETag does not match or is not derivable - SSE-KMS, a non-default checksum algorithm, S3 Express, a provider that computes it differently - the original error is returned, so a replay that used to be absorbed now errors. A failed INSERT is recoverable; a silently discarded one is not. A matching ETag proves the payload, not the create-time attributes: a completion may also carry `If-Match` / `If-None-Match`, and `CreateMultipartUpload` may carry metadata or a storage class, which this layer cannot observe. That residual is pre-existing, strictly less reachable here, and unset on the in-tree S3 multipart paths. #113994 addresses it in `WriteBufferFromS3`, which knows the writer identity. A new integration test fails on master (INSERT acknowledged, old object survives) and passes here, with a no-fault control. Two unit tests keep #56475 honest: a matching object is absorbed, a foreign one errors. cc @ scanhex12 @ kssenii @ CheSema <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114375&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114375](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114375+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Sync `BackupImpl` lock-file handling and the Cloud-only resume state
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-private/pull/69709 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-private/pull/69709 This is the public side of the private pull request above, and most of it is that sync. The shared files both touch -- `BackupImpl.h`, `BackupImpl.cpp`, `BackupFactory.h` -- are identical here and there, down to the blank lines, so `Check public build` can overlay the private ones unchanged and later syncs have nothing to reconcile in them. What stays private is where continuing an interrupted backup is implemented, because nothing outside ClickHouse Cloud resumes one. The part that changes this build is the lock-file handling. `open` removes a lock it created when the verification that follows throws. Otherwise the lock outlives the failed attempt and fences the destination against every later one, which cannot match it either: a retry picks a fresh backup UUID, so the orphaned lock belongs to nobody, and every later `BACKUP` to that destination fails until someone deletes the file by hand. `removeLockFile` now reports whether the destination still holds the lock. `checkLockFile(false)` is false both for a foreign lock and for one it could not read, so a caller could not tell "not ours" from "unknown" while the lock was still there; `tryRemoveAllFiles` reports that as a failure rather than claiming the destination is clean. `createLockFile` asks for the lock with `writeFileIfNotExists` and, when that fails, compares what is there against what it would have written: its own contents mean a concurrent backup, a completed `.backup` means the backup already exists, and a lock that has since disappeared rethrows the original failure rather than guessing. `writeFileIfNotExists` is only exclusive where the storage can be -- `S3` and `Azure` implement it, every other writer falls back to an ordinary write -- so on those other destinations it is the comparison, not the create, that detects a concurrent backup. The rest is behind `CLICKHOUSE_CLOUD` and compiles to nothing here: `CreateParams` carries the resume parameters, `open` hands them to a `BackupResumer` this build does not have, and the places that read them are the ownership check before anything becomes visible, the timestamp a continuation republishes, the lock a continuation is allowed to find, and the manifest it does not write again. `BackupImpl` keeps one member for the last of those, `metadata_already_published`; the parameters themselves stay out, along with everything that acts on them. So this build behaves as it did: it writes its own timestamp and always publishes metadata. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `BACKUP` no longer leaves a lock file behind in its destination when the attempt that created it fails before writing anything. No later backup could match such a lock, so every retry to the same destination failed until the file was deleted by hand. Backups to `S3` and `Azure` destinations now also create the lock exclusively, and a lock that belongs to another backup is reported as a concurrent backup rather than as whatever error the storage returned. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115387&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115387](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115387+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Modularize the adaptive aggregation, weigh its thaw by staged bytes, and add the freeze-bytes and bucket-top-K settings
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111459 Restructuring of the adaptive aggregation, plus one behavioral improvement the new structure enabled and two new settings. ### Refactoring (no behavior change) - **The block-to-staged-chunk conversion is a separate component**: `StagedChunkBuilder` in `AdaptiveAggregationStaging.{h,cpp}` owns the recorded misses, the counting sort into bucket slices, the count dedup, and the seal coalescing, and emits through an `IStagedChunkSink`. The builder knows nothing about the aggregator, so a future consumer of bucket-grouped records (e.g. a grace-style join) can reuse the representation without pulling in the aggregation machinery. - **Staged chunks travel as pipeline data instead of side-channel state**: each producing `AggregatingTransform` emits sealed chunks through its output port, and a new `AdaptiveAggregationMergeTransform` (its own processor files) absorbs them as the backlogs' only writer, uses the closed producer ports as the finish barrier, and assembles the merge. The flow is now visible in `EXPLAIN PIPELINE` and pinned by a test. - **The drain side mirrors the build side**: `StagedChunkDrainer` (merge-time and pressure-time consumption, bucket retirement) consumes chunks through a `StagedSliceApplier` — a narrow inline contract (create states, apply instructions to a contiguous slice) that is the drain's entire dependency on the aggregator. - **The adaptation decisions are rule objects that own their state and constants**: `LearningState::decide` (freeze / give-up), `FrozenState::recordProbeSample` (probe bypass), `ThawSampler` (the global thaw). `Aggregator::executeOnBlock` shrinks to phase hooks; adding an adaptation no longer grows the kernels. - **One entity per file**: `AdaptiveAggregationSession.{h,cpp}`, `AdaptiveAggregationProducer.h`, `AdaptiveAggregationDrain.{h,cpp}`, the processor files, and an updated architecture comment describing the pipeline topology. ### Behavioral change: the thaw verdict is weighted by bytes The thaw previously fired on the staged stream's repeat factor alone (> 12). That misses streams that repeat keys only a few times but drag wide payloads with every staged record. The verdict is now *wasted staged bytes per distinct key*: `(repeat factor − 1) × bytes per record > 300` — a key's first record is the price of storing-it-once; every repeat is bytes the baseline would have absorbed as an in-place update. Near-unique streams measure ~0 by construction and cannot fire; light count records tolerate high repeats; heavy-column streams stand down early in proportion to the damage. Renamed the verdict vocabulary accordingly (`adaptive_staging_wasteful`, `WastefulStagedStream`). Measured on `hits` (100M) (off → on, 16/64 threads): - `SELECT URL, min(Title) GROUP BY URL` (90-byte string key): 0.83×/0.73× → **0.99×/1.01×** - `SELECT UserID, min(URL) GROUP BY UserID` (heavy argument, +121% peak RSS before): 0.83×/0.59× → **0.97×/1.00×**, peak RSS 14.5 → 6.3 GB (matching the ordinary path) ### New settings - **`adaptive_aggregator_freeze_threshold_bytes`** (default 4 MiB): the byte twin of the key-count freeze threshold — a thread's local table freezes at whichever bound is reached first. Measured as the local table's own allocated bytes (hash-table buffer plus arenas), checked between blocks like the baseline's conversion thresholds; deliberately not the query-wide tracked memory, which would freeze all the locals off each other's growth. At the default it is a guardrail: calibration on the heaviest shapes shows ordinary tables keep freezing by key count (e.g. `WatchID, min(URL)`: 14 of 16 locals unchanged, two freeze earlier by bytes, at 15582 and 8192 keys), and a full ClickBench `GROUP BY` sweep of default vs `0` is noise (geomeans 1.001 / 1.007 at 16 / 64 threads). - **`query_plan_aggregation_bucket_top_k`** (default true): a dedicated toggle for the bucket top-K conversion. The contract is worded generally (`ORDER BY` over the aggregation's outputs with `LIMIT n`, gated on provable exactness) so the planned generalization beyond the lone `count()` and a single sort column extends the rule, not the setting. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The adaptive `GROUP BY` aggregation (`enable_adaptive_aggregator`) now measures whether deferring rare keys pays off and returns to the ordinary algorithm when their keys or aggregate arguments are too wide to copy profitably, so aggregations over heavy string columns (e.g. `min(URL)` per user) run at the ordinary algorithm's speed and memory. Adds `adaptive_aggregator_freeze_threshold_bytes` to bound each thread's frozen table in bytes (whichever of it and the key-count threshold is reached first freezes the table), and `query_plan_aggregation_bucket_top_k` to toggle the top-N aggregation optimization. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115480&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115480](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115480+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Convert the JOIN keys to the type of the values that they have in common
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/21794 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/21794 There is no type that is able to hold all the values of both `UInt64` and `Int64`, so a JOIN on such keys was rejected: ``` SELECT * FROM (SELECT number FROM numbers(10)) AS a INNER JOIN (SELECT number FROM numbers(10)) AS b ON a.number = b.number - 1 Code: 386. DB::Exception: There is no supertype for types UInt64, Int64 ... ``` But a JOIN does not need the least supertype. It is enough to convert both keys to the type of the values that they have in common - the most subtype, which is `UInt64` for this pair, holding the values from `0` to `9223372036854775807`. A value outside of this range is not equal to any value from the other side, so `accurateCastOrNull` converts it to NULL, and it does not match anything. This is applied to the equality conditions in the `ON` section, and to the `USING` section of an `INNER JOIN` or a `SEMI JOIN`, where the result contains only the matched values. It is not applied to: - the kinds of JOIN with `USING` that can emit unmatched rows (`LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `FULL`, `ANTI`), where the key is also a column of the result and can hold the unmatched values; - null-safe comparisons (`IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`), where NULL matches NULL, so the values converted to NULL would match each other; - the ASOF inequality (the last column in the `USING` list), which needs the order of the values, not only their equality; - a `Join` table engine whose stored key is not itself the common type, because its hash table is prebuilt over the original key values and cannot be converted - the opposite direction, where only the probe key has to be converted, is supported. A runtime filter is not built for such a JOIN, because a `NOT IN` filter over a set with NULLs would drop the rows that have to be preserved. Only the queries that were failing before are affected - the type inference is unchanged whenever the least supertype exists. It is implemented in the analyzer, which is enabled by default; with `enable_analyzer = 0` the old `TableJoin::inferJoinKeyCommonType` path still rejects such a JOIN, exactly as before. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Allow a JOIN on keys that have no common supertype, such as `UInt64` and `Int64`. Previously such a query was rejected with `There is no supertype for types UInt64, Int64`. Now the keys are converted to the type of the values that they have in common, and a value outside of this range does not match anything. This requires the analyzer (`enable_analyzer = 1`, the default). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112951&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112951](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112951+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add `secondary_indices_materialized` column to `system.parts`
signal.text: ### Changelog category: - New Feature ### Changelog entry [Users can now validate which secondary indices are fully materialized in a data part via the new “secondary_indices_materialized” column in the “system.parts” table.] ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) # secondary_indices_materialized Within the “/src/Storages/System/StorageSystemParts.cpp” code file, added a new column named “secondary_indices_materialized” to the “system.parts” system table to resolve issue #88576. This column provides an array of strings containing the specific names of all materialized secondary indices for each data part which was previously not possible if a given part had multiple secondary indices. The new column definition and its associated array output calculation are both placed in the correct order with respect to the existing column definition and calculation pairs. **Syntax** {"secondary_indices_materialized", std::make_shared<DataTypeArray>(std::make_shared<DataTypeString>()), "The array of materialized secondary index names"}, ... if (columns_mask[src_index++]) { Array materialized_indices; auto secondary_indices_descriptions = part->storage.getInMemoryMetadataPtr()->secondary_indices; for (const auto & index_description : secondary_indices_descriptions) { if (part->hasSecondaryIndex(index_description.name)) materialized_indices.push_back(index_description.name); } columns[res_index++]->insert(materialized_indices); } **Arguments** Not applicable (no function added) **Implementation Details** The “secondary_indices_materialized” column is first defined; If run by a user query, the code retrieves all secondary index definitions for all existing parts from the overall metadata table using “part->storage.getInMemoryMetadataPtr()->secondary_indices”, then iterates through each of these secondary index definitions and validates if it is actually materialized in the current part, with “part->hasSecondaryIndex(index_description.name)”. This way, index names are only added to the resulting array if they exist for the specified part, before the result array is inserted into the output column. **Returned value** - Returns {columns[res_index++]->insert(materialized_indices);}. [Array](../data-types/float.md) **Example** Query: \```sql SELECT 'name, secondary_indices_materialized FROM system.parts WHERE database = ‘ex_database' AND table = ‘ex_table’; \``` Response: \```response ┌──────name─────────────secondary_indices_materialized───────────┐ │ [part_number] │ [‘indexStr1’, ‘indexStr2’, ‘…’] └─────────────────────────────────────────────── ┘ \``` --- **Additional fix (2026-07-27)** While adding the regression test for the `escape_index_filenames` semantics of the new column, CI (under the randomized MergeTree setting `auto_statistics_types`) exposed an unrelated pre-existing bug, fixed here as well: In the settings-alter branch of `StorageMergeTree::alter` and `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::alter`, `changeSettings` is the sole writer of the setting-derived fields `StorageInMemoryMetadata::escape_index_filenames` and `IndexDescription::escape_filenames`. When the table carries an explicit `auto_statistics_types` setting, the subsequent `setInMemoryMetadata` call that re-commits the implicit statistics writes back a metadata copy that was taken *before* `changeSettings` (`commands.apply` never sets those fields), so `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY SETTING escape_index_filenames = ...` did not take effect until the server was restarted. The committed escape fields are now carried into that copy, exactly as the `areNonReplicatedAlterCommands` branch of `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::alter` already does for the comment commit. New test: `04650_alter_escape_index_filenames_with_auto_statistics`. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/88576 --- **Additional fixes (2026-08-04 / 2026-08-12 / 2026-08-20)** - A mixed `ALTER` that includes `MODIFY SETTING escape_index_filenames` (for example together with `MODIFY COMMENT`, or with a replicated command) republished a metadata copy taken before `changeSettings` and so reverted the index filename policy in memory until a server restart, in both `StorageMergeTree::alter` and `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::alter`. The policy is now re-applied from the committed `escape_index_filenames` setting through `MergeTreeData::applyEscapeIndexFilenamesFromSettings`. Test: `04700_alter_escape_index_filenames_mixed_alter`. - The column no longer counts index files the part does not own. An index file left in the part directory but missing from `checksums.txt` is an orphan of the released bug #109595 and the index still has to be rebuilt, while a packed substream (a member of `skp_idx.packed`, which has no per-file entry of its own) does count. Test: `04870_system_parts_secondary_indices_orphan_index_file`. - The column now follows the read path exactly: it asks `IMergeTreeIndex::getDeserializedFormat`, the same call `MergeTreeIndexReader` makes, and requires the part to own every substream of the layout it returns. A multistream index such as `text` is therefore not reported as materialized when a sibling stream is missing, and an index the reader refuses for another reason (an invalidated system column, or granules serialized under a column type the metadata no longer declares) is reported as absent too. Test: `05023_system_parts_secondary_indices_text_index`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=89350&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/89350](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F89350+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Use bloom filter skip index for arrayJoin(col) IN (set) and arrayJoin(col) = const
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109516 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109844 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A `bloom_filter` skip index on an `Array` column is now used for `arrayJoin(column) IN (set)`, `arrayJoin(column) GLOBAL IN (set)` and `arrayJoin(column) = const`, the same way it was already used for `hasAny(column, set)` and `has(column, const)`. Previously these `arrayJoin ...` forms fell back to a full scan. ### Description `MergeTreeIndexConditionBloomFilter` only accepted the argument of `IN` / `=` as an indexed column directly or one of a few wrappers (`tuple`, map subcolumns, JSON paths). `arrayJoin(tags)` matched none, so the atom became `FUNCTION_UNKNOWN` and nothing was pruned, while `hasAny(tags, ...)` / `has(tags, ...)` already pruned. This PR recognizes `arrayJoin(indexed_array_column)` on the left side and maps: - `arrayJoin(arr) IN (set)` (and `GLOBAL IN`) to the same granule test as `hasAny(arr, set_elements)` (`traverseTreeIn`); - `arrayJoin(arr) = const` to the same granule test as `has(arr, const)` (`traverseTreeEquals`). `arrayJoin` only multiplies rows, so a granule matches only if one of its array elements belongs to the set / equals the constant, which is what the bloom filter evaluates for `hasAny` / `has`. `NOT IN` / `!=` are intentionally not handled: a granule containing a set element / the constant can still yield rows whose value is outside the set / differs. Both derivations hash the constant after converting it towards the indexed element type, and SQL comparison coerces more widely than that conversion does. Where the two disagree the index was probed with bytes the predicate never compares, or the conversion threw during index analysis. Both are now gated on a proven-matching hash domain: an identical element and constant type, or integer against integer. Everything else is declined, leaving a full scan and keeping a conversion error reachable at execution rather than turning it into pruned granules. Integer widening and a `LowCardinality` wrapper stay admitted, so the pruning this PR adds is unchanged. Verified with `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` that the `arrayJoin ...` forms prune like `hasAny` / `has`, that `NOT IN` / `!=` do not prune, and that results are identical with the skip index on and off for every declined domain and for the `LEFT ARRAY JOIN` case. Test: `04365_bloom_filter_arrayJoin_in`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109536&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/109536](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F109536+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
