signal.title: Bind the parallel replicas shard scope to the cluster that produced it
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/81738 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results and a `LOGICAL_ERROR` when a query reads with parallel replicas inside a distributed sub-query whose `cluster_for_parallel_replicas` numbers its shards differently from the cluster the query is distributed over, for example a `VIEW` carrying its own `SETTINGS cluster_for_parallel_replicas`, or a read through `clusterAllReplicas` of that same cluster. The shard number shipped by the initiator was applied to the other numbering and selected the wrong shard. Parallel replicas are now declined for such a read. ### Description `prepareClusterForParallelReplicas` indexes the `_shard_num` scalar into `cluster_for_parallel_replicas` as if both described the same cluster. They are independent: `_shard_num` is shipped over the wire by a distributed query's initiator, while `cluster_for_parallel_replicas` is a per-query setting any nested `SETTINGS` clause can change, including inside a `view(...)`. - Above the other cluster's shard count, the read throws `LOGICAL_ERROR: Shard number is greater than shard count`, aborting debug and sanitizer builds. - In range, no check fires and the read silently returns **the wrong shard's data**: `10000090` where `90` is correct. `21ef1f1d1c9ba39` removed a `_cluster_for_parallel_replicas` scalar, reasoning that the setting alone identifies the cluster; a view with its own `SETTINGS` falsifies that. This restores the provenance as a second column of the `_shard_num` block, so overwriting the number replaces it atomically. A scope is honoured only when its provenance identifies the same shard *numbering*, not merely the same cluster name: `clusterAllReplicas` derives a renumbered cluster that keeps the name. Otherwise parallel replicas are declined at every admission site, giving the same results as `enable_parallel_replicas = 0`. No assertion is weakened: with admission gated, the `LOGICAL_ERROR` becomes correct rather than misapplied. Absent provenance means "trust the shard number", so mixed-version clusters keep today's behaviour. Each consequence reproduces on unpatched master and passes here. Added a stateless test, an integration test for the wrong-shard read, and gtests for wire cases SQL cannot build. Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/101325 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113589&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113589](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113589+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115272 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115146 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results from `if`, `multiIf` and `CASE` when one branch is a `Date` or `Date32` and the result type is `DateTime` or `DateTime64`. With `compile_expressions = 1` (the default) the compiled expression copied the date's day count into the timestamp column without converting days to seconds, so `if(cond, toDate32('1900-01-01'), toDateTime64('1970-01-01', 3))` returned `1969-12-31 23:59:34.433`. Closes #115272. ### Description Reported by @ PedroTadim in [#115272](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115272), who asked me to fix it and have @Manerone review. **Root cause.** `FunctionIfBase::isCompilableImpl` already intends to refuse these expressions -- its comment reads *"It's difficult to compare Date and DateTime - cannot use JIT compilation."* -- but it tested `WhichDataType::isDate()` and `isDateTime()`, which are exact `TypeIndex` equality, so it refused only `Date`+`DateTime` and admitted `Date32`+`DateTime64`, `Date`+`DateTime64` and `Date32`+`DateTime`. Those reach `nativeCast`, which correctly finds no scale for day-count types and falls through to a plain `CreateIntCast`: `-25567` days becomes `-25567` milliseconds. The predicates were never widened when `Date32` and `DateTime64` were added. **The change** widens both predicates to `isDateOrDate32()` and `isDateTimeOrDateTime64()`, so the guard covers the whole family and the interpreted path runs. `if.cpp` and `multiIf.cpp` inherit this base, so one change covers all three. These expressions lose JIT, as the comment intended and as `Date`+`DateTime` always did. The commit message covers the rejected IR alternative. **Validation.** New test `04930_jit_compiled_if_date_to_datetime` asserts the compiled result equals the `compile_expressions = 0` result over the reported matrix: scales 0/3/6/9, both date and both datetime types, both branch orders, constant and column dates, `if`/`multiIf`/`CASE`, `Nullable(Date32)`, pre/post-1970. 12 of its 14 comparison rows fail without the fix and all pass with it (50/50 runs). The 2 exceptions are controls green both ways: `Date`+`DateTime`, already refused, and same-unit `Date32`+`Date`, which must keep compiling. Those rows are 1-vs-0 parity checks, so they would pass even if compilation stopped. Two further rows pin which shapes compile, via `ProfileEvents['CompiledFunctionExecute']`: it counts executions of an already-compiled node, so it needs no cache drop and the test stays parallel-safe. The mixed-unit row fails on an unpatched binary, so it tracks this change rather than asserting a constant. They are also why the test carries `no-fasttest, no-msan`: those builds have no embedded compiler. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115325&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115325](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115325+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Push equi-key filter into the left input of RIGHT JOIN for cross-type USING keys
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103038 For `RIGHT JOIN` with a `WHERE` predicate on a `USING` column whose two sides have different types, the predicate was not used as a primary-key index condition on the left input, so the left `MergeTree` read every granule. `buildEquialentSetsForJoinStepLogical` only returns equi-key pairs whose two sides have equal types, because those pairs feed a Union-Find equivalence class. Plain column-name substitution does not need that. It does need two other things: the replacement must carry the type the replaced name has in the `JOIN` output, because that is what the filter's nodes were typed against, and it must evaluate to the value that output column holds, because the filter's semantics are defined on that value. A cross-type equi-key gives both once the replacement is cast the way the `JOIN` casts that key. The two sides are compared in their least supertype, so `CAST(<opposite side>, supertype)` is exactly what is behind the `JOIN` output column. Requiring the `JOIN` output type to be that supertype keeps the cast widening - a narrowing one would change what the predicate returns - and still rejects a column the `JOIN` altered for an unrelated reason, such as `join_use_nulls` widening it to `Nullable`. The cast node is only materialized once a pushed-down filter actually references it. Reproducer from the issue: ```sql CREATE TABLE mt (k UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k AS SELECT number FROM numbers(10000000); SELECT k FROM mt AS l RIGHT JOIN (SELECT 1 AS k) AS r USING (k) WHERE k = 1; ``` Measured on 10M rows, before and after on the same data: | | rows read | bytes read | time | |--- |--- |--- |--- | | before | 10,000,001 | 76.29 MiB | 0.050 s | | after | 8,193 | 64.00 KiB | 0.021 s | Granules read on the left `MergeTree` for `RIGHT JOIN ... USING (k) WHERE k = 1`, 1M rows, by key type pair. The first two rows are what an earlier revision already delivered; the last three are what this revision adds: | left | right | `USING` type | before | after | |--- |--- |--- |--- |--- | | `UInt64` | `UInt8` | `UInt64` (== left) | 122/122 | 1/122 | | `Int64` | `UInt32` | `Int64` (== left) | 122/122 | 1/122 | | `Int32` | `Int64` | `Int64` (== right) | 122/122 | 1/122 | | `Int32` | `UInt32` | `Int64` (wider than both) | 122/122 | 1/122 | | `UInt32` | `Int32` | `Int64` (wider than both) | 122/122 | 1/122 | The pushed-down condition is the `JOIN`'s own cast, so the index still applies: `Condition: (_CAST(k, 'Int64') in [1, 1])`. ### Scope This does not close https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103038. The issue asks for `RIGHT` **and** `FULL JOIN`, and covers both planners; this pull request only fixes `RIGHT JOIN` under `enable_analyzer = 1`. `FULL JOIN` is not fixed, for the reasons below, and the test keeps its cases as result-only regression guards. The legacy `JoinStep` path (`enable_analyzer = 0`) is not fixed either. There, a `USING` key is renamed to `<table>.<key>` in the right input header while the `JOIN` output keeps the bare name, so `equivalent_columns_to_push_down` holds a name the filter never references and nothing is pushed - the type check this pull request relaxes is not what blocks it. Making it work would additionally require the `JOIN`-output type guard that path lacks entirely, which is the guard https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/98167 had to add for `join_use_nulls`. That is out of scope here. The substitution is also not registered in the opposite direction when it would need a narrowing cast, for example a predicate on the wider of the two keys: the narrower side cannot reproduce the value the `JOIN` output carries, so the predicate stays above the `JOIN`. An earlier revision of this pull request also enabled the push-down for `FULL JOIN` and generalised `RIGHT` / `LEFT JOIN` from `Semi` strictness to any strictness. Both were unsound and have been reverted. The reasoning behind them was that the top-level `WHERE` stays above the `JOIN` and removes any row that slips through the duplicated per-side filter. It does not: `tryPushDownOverJoinStep` replaces the `FilterStep` with an `ExpressionStep` once every conjunction has been pushed, and conjunctions routed through `equivalent_columns_to_push_down` are pushed to both sides and never land in `rejected_conjunctions`, which is exactly what triggers the removal. Keeping the post-join filter would not have been sufficient either. Pushing an equivalence-derived predicate to the opposite input changes which rows match, and an outer `JOIN` then emits a defaulted unmatched row whose columns differ from the original, so a predicate evaluated on that default both admits rows belonging to neither input and discards rows that should survive: ```sql -- returned 3 rows instead of 1 SELECT * FROM t1 AS lhs FULL JOIN t2 AS rhs ON lhs.id = rhs.id WHERE lhs.id != 0 AND rhs.id != 0; -- lost the unmatched (5, 0) row SELECT lhs.id, rhs.id FROM s1 AS lhs FULL JOIN s2 AS rhs ON lhs.id = rhs.id WHERE rhs.id != 5; -- returned a jt.x = 5 row, against a filled join where the right-side push is disabled SELECT lt.x, jt.x FROM lt RIGHT JOIN jt ON lt.x = jt.x WHERE jt.x = 1; ``` `SEMI` emits only matched rows, which is why the original restriction was there. `FULL JOIN`, both `Semi` restrictions and both equivalence branches are now identical to `master`, and the `03036_join_filter_push_down_equivalent_sets` reference no longer needs the rewrite an earlier revision gave it. The test covers the granule pruning for `RIGHT JOIN` across the key-type pairs above and keeps the wrong-result cases as regression guards. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Push a `WHERE` condition on a `USING` column through a `RIGHT JOIN` so the left `MergeTree` input can use it as a primary-key index condition, also when the two join keys have different types. Applies when `enable_analyzer = 1`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=103478&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/103478](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F103478+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Compare stored table definition expressions by AST instead of formatted text
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/92340 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110840 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108590 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed cross-version metadata compatibility for tables whose keys and other definition expressions were written with redundant parentheses (`PARTITION BY (a)`, `ORDER BY (b, c)`, `DEFAULT (a + 1)`, `TTL (d + INTERVAL 10 YEAR)`, `INDEX ix (b * c)`, `CONSTRAINT c CHECK (a > 0)`, `PROJECTION p (SELECT (b) ...)`) or with an explicit single-element `tuple(a)`. #92340 started preserving these parentheses in stored metadata, so `ATTACH`/`REPLACE`/`MOVE PARTITION FROM` between two such tables failed with `Tables have different ...` even on a single server version, and a replica reading metadata written by another version failed with `METADATA_MISMATCH`. Stored table definition expressions are now compared by their ASTs (`getTreeHash`), not by their formatted text. ### Description #92340 started to preserve redundant parentheses in the stored definition ASTs. Older versions stored the canonical form without them, so the metadata serialized by the two versions differs, and every comparison (`ReplicatedMergeTree` replica join, `ATTACH`/`REPLACE`/`MOVE PARTITION FROM`) rejected definitions that are actually equal. Two sub-cases with different affected ranges: - Redundant parentheses (`PARTITION BY (a)` vs `PARTITION BY a`). This is the #92340 regression: measured on released binaries, 25.8, 26.3 and 26.4 accept `ATTACH PARTITION FROM` between the two forms while 26.5, 26.6 and 26.7 reject it, matching the branches that contain `b38a892dfbfab6`. It does **not** require an upgrade or a mixed-version cluster: both tables created by the same 26.7 binary already fail, because the comparison is between two in-memory ASTs of which only one carries the `parenthesized` flag. - An explicit single-element `tuple(a)` vs `a`. This one fails on every version tried, 25.8 included, so it is a long-standing bug rather than a #92340 regression. It is fixed here as well because `extractKeyExpressionList` unwraps the optional `tuple(...)`. Following https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110833#issuecomment-5040213065, this replaces the earlier text-canonicalization approach entirely: - Expressions are compared by their ASTs using `getTreeHash`, not as text or reformatted text. Comparing formatted text is wrong because the text depends on the formatting logic, which can change for unrelated (e.g. aesthetic) reasons, while the stored form may have been written by any past server version. - The comparison method is reusable: `sameAST` in `src/Parsers/IAST.h` (aliases significant, `nullptr`-tolerant overload for optional expressions). - It is applied at every place where serialized, stored expressions are compared to check whether the table was altered or changed unexpectedly: - `ReplicatedMergeTreeTableMetadata::checkImmutableFieldsEquals` / `checkEquals` / `checkAndFindDiff` (replica join, `ALTER` application). The stored strings are parsed purely syntactically (without resolving against any column set), so the fields of an `ALTER` log entry that adds a column and changes a key in one go compare safely; the `columns`/`context` parameters are gone. Keys additionally go through `extractKeyExpressionList`, so `a`, `(a)` and `tuple(a)` are the same single-column key while `a DESC` stays different. - `MergeTreeData::checkStructureAndGetMergeTreeData` (the `ATTACH`/`REPLACE`/`MOVE PARTITION FROM` structure gate): sorting/partition/primary keys and the secondary-index/projection definition sets. - `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::checkTableStructureAttempt`: the columns comparison (`ColumnsDescription`/`ColumnDescription`/`ColumnDefault` equality now compares the default/codec/TTL expressions as ASTs). The column-by-column comparison also has to ignore in-memory-only state that is never serialized (implicit statistics and the auxiliary `data_type` of `ColumnStatisticsDescription`, hence the new `hasSameExplicitStatistics`), otherwise every replicated `CREATE` would report `INCOMPATIBLE_COLUMNS` against the columns it had just written to ZooKeeper. - `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::alter`: detection of which metadata fields an `ALTER` actually changed. The changed fields are also written back to Keeper through the same backward-compatible serializers the `ReplicatedMergeTreeTableMetadata` constructor uses (`formatDefinition` / `formatDefinitionList`), so an `ALTER` never publishes a parenthesized definition that an older replica would reject. - `AlterCommand::isTTLAlter` (whether restating a TTL schedules a `MATERIALIZE TTL` mutation) and the `MODIFY ORDER BY` no-op detection in `AlterCommands::prepare`. - `ProjectionDescription::operator==`. - For `getTreeHash` to be a faithful identity of a definition, AST nodes that keep semantic state outside of `children` now hash that state (`updateTreeHashImpl` overrides): `ASTTTLElement` (mode, destination, `GROUP BY` keys/assignments, recompression codec), `ASTIndexDeclaration` (name, granularity), `ASTConstraintDeclaration` (name, `CHECK`/`ASSUME`), `ASTProjectionDeclaration` (name), `ASTProjectionSelectQuery` (which clause each child belongs to, previously `SELECT a GROUP BY b` and `SELECT a ORDER BY b` hashed equally), `ASTWindowDefinition` (frame type and boundary kinds). - Since a member that is not a child and is not hashed silently makes two different definitions compare equal, `getTreeHash` documents the requirement, and the classes whose member set is the whole point of the override (`ASTTTLElement`, `ASTIndexDeclaration`, `ASTConstraintDeclaration`, `ASTProjectionDeclaration`, `ASTWindowDefinition`, `ASTSetQuery`, `ASTWithElement`, `ASTWindowListElement`) carry a `sizeof` `static_assert`, so adding a member there fails to compile until it is considered. `ASTSelectQuery`, `ASTProjectionSelectQuery` and `ASTOrderByElement` instead iterate the clause/child-role enumerators, so a newly added one is hashed with no code change. The remaining overrides are not asserted: `ASTColumnsApplyTransformer` (which reaches the `parameters` and `lambda` subtrees) and `ASTSelectWithUnionQuery` hash more than one member, `ASTWithAlias` and `ASTSelectIntersectExceptQuery` one each. Measured: the `static_assert` fires for a new `String`, `UInt64` or pointer member; a lone `bool` can still fit in tail padding, which the comment covers. The negative tests found five ways the comparison was too permissive, each of which master rejects. They are fixed here and each is covered by a test that fails if the fix is reverted: - `ColumnDescription::operator==` used `IDataType::equals`, which ignores the `SimpleAggregateFunction` wrapper (as `MergeTreeData::sortingKeyChanged` already documents), so a replica declaring a plain `UInt64` joined a table whose column is `SimpleAggregateFunction(sum, UInt64)`. It compares `getName` now. - `hasSameExplicitStatistics` kept only the `StatisticsType`, so `STATISTICS(tdigest(1))` and `STATISTICS(tdigest(2))` compared equal although the parameters are a part of the stored definition and survive `SHOW CREATE`. The declaration ASTs are compared as well. - `parameters` and `lambda` of `ASTColumnsApplyTransformer` are not children and were hashed with `updateTreeHashImpl`, which stops at the node itself, so a projection using `APPLY quantile(0.5)` and one using `APPLY quantile(0.9)` hashed equally. `stripArtificialParens` could not reach them either. Both now descend. - The alias was hashed without a length prefix, so `fooIdentifier_bar` and `bar AS Identifier_foo` produced the same byte stream and two projections with different output columns compared equal. - `ASTWindowDefinition` keeps its frame type and boundary kinds outside `children` and did not hash them, so a projection aggregating over `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` compared equal to one over `ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND CURRENT ROW`. The frame offsets are children and were already covered. One latent bug became reachable and is fixed too: `ASTTTLElement::clone` left `recompression_codec` shared with the source, and `formatDefinition` clones the metadata AST specifically in order to canonicalize it, so `stripArtificialParens` would have written into the live metadata snapshot of a `RECOMPRESS` TTL. No parser or formatter changes and no on-disk/`SHOW CREATE` changes: what the user wrote is preserved; only comparisons became insensitive to formatting. Genuinely different definitions still differ (`a` vs `b`, `a` vs `a DESC`, different index granularity, `CHECK` vs `ASSUME`, different TTL destination). The comparison of whole `CREATE` queries during `RESTORE` (`compareRestoredTableDef`) still compares text: it is a whole-query comparison rather than an expression comparison, and its failure direction is safe (refuses the restore). Tested with a real previous-version server (`clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.4`): `tests/integration/test_backward_compatibility/test_parenthesized_keys.py` exercises a new replica joining an old table and vice versa, an old replica applying parenthesized `ALTER` log entries written by the new version plus restarts of both replicas, and upgrade + `ATTACH PARTITION FROM`. Unit test `src/Storages/MergeTree/tests/gtest_replicated_metadata_compare.cpp` locks the comparison semantics including the negative cases. Stateless tests: `03471_replace_partition_tuple_key_normalization`, `04604_parenthesized_partition_key_attach_from`, `04612_parenthesized_index_projection_attach_from`, `04622_modify_ttl_parenthesized_no_mutation`, `04646_projection_ttl_parenthesized_zk_metadata`, `04648_alter_parenthesized_zk_metadata`, `04650_replica_column_definition_mismatch_rejected`, `04693_projection_apply_function_name_case` (the function name of a projection's `COLUMNS(...) APPLY` transformer is canonicalized for the comparison only, so `APPLY SUM` and `APPLY sum` compare equal while the stored definition keeps the as-written spelling that older replicas compare byte-for-byte). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110833&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110833](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110833+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR on runtime filter lookup before build finished
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` exception "Trying to lookup values in runtime filter before building it was finished" during JOINs with `enable_join_runtime_filters` enabled when the join stops reading the build side early (for example `join_overflow_mode = 'break'` with a finite `max_rows_in_join` / `max_bytes_in_join`, or an empty/short-circuited right side). ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer (STID 2210-585c) and reproducible on master. A JOIN runtime filter is built on the right (build) side by N parallel `BuildRuntimeFilterTransform` streams. The filter becomes visible to `RuntimeFilterLookup::find(name)` after the FIRST stream's `finish()`, but `IRuntimeFilter::inserts_are_finished` only becomes true after the LAST stream merges its partial filter (`filters_to_merge` reaches 0). The probe (left) side applies the filter via `FunctionApplyFilter` -> `IRuntimeFilter::find()`. Normally the join's pull discipline guarantees the build side is fully consumed before the probe side runs. But when the join stops reading the build side early, `FillingRightJoinSideTransform` closes its input and the build-phase finish counter reaches `isLast()` before all N `BuildRuntimeFilterTransform` streams have called `finish()`. The probe side then calls `find()` on a filter whose `inserts_are_finished` is still false, and `IRuntimeFilter::find()` raised a `LOGICAL_ERROR`, crashing debug/sanitizer builds. The runtime filter is a best-effort optimization: correctness always comes from the JOIN itself, never from this pre-filter (`FunctionApplyFilter` already returns const-true when the filter is absent). The fix makes `find()` pass all rows through (return const-true) when the build side is not finished yet, instead of throwing. This is safe for both "contains" and "not-contains" filter polarities, since the JOIN drops the non-matching rows. `finishInsert()` is also reordered to finalize the underlying set/bloom filter before publishing `inserts_are_finished = true`, so a concurrent `find()` can never observe a half-built filter. Adds a functional test (`04337_runtime_filter_lookup_before_finished`) that drives a real JOIN pipeline with `join_overflow_mode = 'break'` and a tiny `max_bytes_in_join` over a multi-part build table, so the probe side reaches `find()` while the runtime filter is still unfinished. The query is repeated so the probabilistic race is hit with high probability; without the fix at least one repetition aborts the server, and with the fix the test passes. Report (AST fuzzer, amd_debug, targeted): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=103322&sha=eeec76f833a27b148d130ef8f504ac362f26caef&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107108&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/107108](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F107108+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Name the join algorithms that were tried in the "can't execute" error
signal.text: When no enabled join algorithm can run a JOIN, the planner threw: ``` Can't execute any of specified algorithms for specified strictness/kind and right storage type ``` It named neither the algorithms that were tried nor the JOIN that failed, even though both are available at the throw site. Setting `join_algorithm` to something narrower for memory reasons and then writing an `ASOF JOIN` left you with nothing to act on. It now reads: ``` None of the algorithms enabled by the 'join_algorithm' setting [grace_hash] can execute this ASOF INNER JOIN with the given right table storage type ``` Algorithm names are printed through `SettingFieldJoinAlgorithmTraits::toString` rather than `toString(JoinAlgorithm)`. The latter returns the uppercase enum spelling, `GRACE_HASH`, which the setting parser rejects, so the names in the message can now be pasted straight back into `join_algorithm`. The message deliberately does not list the algorithms that would work. `tryCreateJoin` has no capability table, the rules live implicitly across its per algorithm branches, so naming them here would add a copy of knowledge that is already in the documentation and would rot quietly the next time an algorithm gains or loses support. Also updates a comment in `02242_join_rocksdb.sql` that quoted the old wording. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): When no join algorithm enabled by the `join_algorithm` setting can execute a `JOIN`, the error message now names the algorithms that were tried and the strictness and kind of the JOIN that failed, instead of reporting only that none of them worked. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115226&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115226](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115226+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add `sorted_merge` and `parallel_sorted_merge` join algorithms
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109005 Implements the two algorithms planned in [this discussion](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109005#discussion_r3694159098): `full_sorting_merge` and `parallel_full_sorting_merge` are always supported, so anything listed after them in `join_algorithm` is unreachable — listing them is an unconditional choice, not a preference. The new `sorted_merge` and `parallel_sorted_merge` algorithms execute the same merge join, but are **available only when both join inputs can be efficiently read in the order of the join keys** (e.g. MergeTree tables whose primary key starts with the join keys), so the pre-join sorts become cheap `FinishSorting` or disappear. When the tables' order cannot be exploited, the selection falls through to the next algorithm in the list. That makes them meaningful as a high-priority preference: `join_algorithm = 'sorted_merge,parallel_hash'` uses the streaming, low-memory merge join exactly when it is certainly beneficial, and a hash join otherwise. `sorted_merge` runs a single in-order merge join. `parallel_sorted_merge` additionally shards the join by ranges of the tables' common primary-key prefix into independent per-shard merge joins running in parallel — the same source-side sharding `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges` applies, enabled for this join by the algorithm itself; the in-order reads stay intact (no scatter, no re-sort). When the sharding cannot apply (e.g. an `ASOF` join), it degrades to a single `sorted_merge`. Implementation notes: - Eligibility is decided during plan physicalization, where the input subplans are visible: `JoinStepLogical::inputsCanBeReadInJoinKeyOrder` finds the `ReadFromMergeTree` below each input (mirroring `findReadingStep` of `optimizeReadInOrder`, without descending through nested joins) and probes the actual read-in-order matcher (`wouldReadInOrderBeUseful`, the same side-effect-free probe `topKThroughJoin` uses) with the join-key sort description. The predicted decision degrades gracefully in both directions: a false positive runs like `full_sorting_merge` (with a full sort), a false negative falls through to the next algorithm. - The same memoized predicate makes `tryAddJoinRuntimeFilter` keep its hands off an eligible join listed before the first hash-family algorithm. Without this, planting a runtime filter erases the merge algorithms from the list (a merge join reads both sides concurrently and cannot use a runtime filter), silently overriding the priority order — the defining feature of these algorithms. For non-eligible joins the runtime filter (and the erasure) stays, because those algorithms are not selectable anyway. When `applyParallelReplicas` later breaks the eligibility (a join input becomes a distributed read), the filter pass is re-run for exactly the joins it had skipped, so the `hash` fall-through gets its runtime filter back. - `FullSortingMergeJoin` now carries the selected algorithm (`getSelectedAlgorithm`) instead of an `is_parallel` flag; the hash-scatter rewrite (`optimizeParallelFullSortingMergeJoin`) stays exclusive to `parallel_full_sorting_merge`, and `optimizeJoinByShards` runs in a restricted mode (only `parallel_sorted_merge`-selected joins, with a cheap pre-scan bail-out) when `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges` is off. When the sharded stream counts diverge at pipeline-building time (e.g. a data-dependent `PREWHERE` prunes one side to a single empty stream), `JoinStep` merges each side's per-shard sorted streams back into one sorted stream and runs the single-stream merge join instead of failing (the same approach as #109393, applied at the sharding fallback). - The `CreateSetAndFilterOnTheFlyStep` pair (`max_rows_in_set_to_optimize_join`) is not added for sorted-merge joins: it sits between the read and the sort and would defeat the in-order read the algorithm was selected for. - The old analyzer has no query plan at selection time, so there the algorithms are never selected and the list falls through (documented). With only `sorted_merge` listed and no exploitable order, the query fails with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, like other unsupported single-algorithm configurations. - The known lower-priority-fallback side effects of listing merge algorithms (stricter `USING` key-type inference, `topKThroughJoin` deferral) extend to the new values and are documented in the `join_algorithm` setting description. Tests: `04669_sorted_merge_join_selection` pins the selection gating via `EXPLAIN PIPELINE` (selected on a primary-key join with no re-sort, falls through on non-key joins / disabled read-in-order / old analyzer, priority order respected, error when listed alone without exploitable order) and correctness against `hash` for `INNER`/`LEFT`/`RIGHT`/`FULL`/`ANY`/`join_use_nulls`. `04670_parallel_sorted_merge_join` pins the primary-key-range sharding (`Sharding:` marker with `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges = 0`, no `ScatterByPartitionTransform`, no `MergeSortingTransform`), the `ASOF` degradation, and correctness. `04824_sorted_merge_join_parallel_replicas_fallthrough` and `04894_sorted_merge_join_parallel_replicas_runtime_filter` pin the parallel-replicas edge (fall-through to `hash` with the runtime filter restored), `04895_parallel_sorted_merge_join_shard_stream_divergence` pins the diverged-shard degradation, `04896_sorted_merge_join_null_safe_equals` pins the ineligibility of a nullable null-safe (`<=>`) join (whose keys are compared wrapped into `tuple(...)`, so they cannot be read in table order), and `04760`/`04850` pin the `join_use_nulls` and `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges` contracts. The PR #109005 regression tests and the join runtime filter tests pass unchanged. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added new `join_algorithm` values `sorted_merge` and `parallel_sorted_merge`: merge-join algorithms that are available only when both join inputs can be efficiently read in the order of the join keys (so the join benefits from the tables' order instead of sorting), and otherwise fall through to the next algorithm in the list. `parallel_sorted_merge` additionally shards the join by primary-key ranges into independent per-shard merge joins running in parallel. Listing them first, e.g. `join_algorithm = 'sorted_merge,parallel_hash'`, uses the streaming low-memory merge join exactly when it is certainly beneficial. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112973&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112973](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112973+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: AI functions: Make quotas per query not per block
signal.text: `AIQuotaTracker` was a stack local inside `executeImpl`, so every block and every pipeline stream started with a fresh allowance. The `ai_function_max_api_calls_per_query`, `ai_function_max_input_tokens_per_query` and `ai_function_max_output_tokens_per_query` limits therefore scaled with the data (one allowance per block per function) instead of bounding the query — any limit above the largest block's row count could never fire. The tracker is now a single instance owned by the query `Context` and shared by every AI function call in that context, with atomic counters for the concurrent pipeline threads. The API-call limit is claimed with an atomic bounded reservation, so it is an exact cap within a query-execution context even under `max_threads > 1`; the token limits are best-effort, since a call's token usage is known only after its response arrives. The limits are enforced per server / query fragment: a distributed query (across shards or parallel-replica fragments) enforces them independently on each, not summed globally. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The AI-function quota settings (`ai_function_max_api_calls_per_query`, `ai_function_max_input_tokens_per_query`, `ai_function_max_output_tokens_per_query`) were enforced per block rather than per query, letting a query exceed the configured limit in proportion to the number of blocks and threads processed. They now bound the whole query per server: the API-call limit is an exact cap (atomic reservation), and the token limits are best-effort. A distributed query enforces the limits independently on each participating server / fragment. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114885&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114885](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114885+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix a logical error when materialized views share one target table
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104448 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `Block structure mismatch` logical error on `INSERT` into a table that several materialized views write to, when the target table's metadata is changed concurrently. Each view's sink is now built from the same metadata snapshot as the header feeding it. ### Description A table reached through N materialized views is visited N times while insert dependencies are collected, because `DependencyPath::popBack` removes the node from `visited`. `observePath` re-read the target's metadata every visit and published it into the builder-wide `metadata_snapshots` unconditionally, so the **last** visit won, while `output_headers` is keyed per view and keeps the snapshot of the visit that observed it. `createSinkImpl` pairs the two: `RemovingSparseTransform` from `output_headers.at(view_id)`, the sink from `metadata_snapshots.at(inner_table_id)`. If the target's metadata is replaced between two visits, an earlier view's sink is built against a snapshot its header did not come from, and `Chain::addSink` -> `connect` throws: ``` Logical error: 'Block structure mismatch in function connect between RemovingSparseTransform and MemorySink stream: different number of columns: k UInt32 UInt32(size = 0), v UInt32 UInt32(size = 0), w UInt32 UInt32(size = 0) k UInt32 UInt32(size = 0), v UInt32 UInt32(size = 0)' ``` The share lock `observePath` takes is a drop lock, so it does not prevent this: `ALTER` takes `alter_lock`, and `StorageObjectStorage`'s schema refresh calls `setInMemoryMetadata` with no lock at all. The fix stores the storage handle, its snapshot and its share lock only on the first observation, then adopts that snapshot and re-derives the materialized-view pointer from the stored handle, so a node's published artifacts all describe one storage as seen once. A view is itself re-visitable, and that pointer picks the branch and supplies `getTargetTableId`. It sits after the stale-dependency validation, which keeps its fresh read, and before `output_headers` is filled. Where both reads would return the same value the adopted handle *is* that value, so behaviour is unchanged. Reproduced on `Memory` and `MergeTree` targets by racing `INSERT` against `ALTER ADD/DROP COLUMN`: pristine master aborted 4 of 4 runs, the fix survived 4 of 4. A gtest pins the invariant; two mutation arms confirm both halves load-bearing.

signal.title: Support safe type conversions in correlated subquery equivalence substitution
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113407 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/101863 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Correlated subqueries with an equality on columns that differ only in nullability (e.g. `Int64` vs `Nullable(Int64)` under `data_type_default_nullable = 1`, as in TPC-DS Q35), or on native-number columns having a least common type (e.g. `Int32` vs `Int64`), are now decorrelated via equivalent-expression substitution instead of falling back to a CROSS JOIN with a post-join filter, avoiding severe memory growth on such queries. Closes #113407. --- ## Motivation The equivalent-expression substitution in `PlannerCorrelatedSubqueries` recorded an equivalence only when both sides of the correlated `equals` had exactly the same type. A correlated `EXISTS` whose join condition compares `Int64` with `Nullable(Int64)` therefore decorrelated through the CROSS JOIN fallback; at TPC-DS SF100 (Q35 with `data_type_default_nullable = 1`) the cross-joined intermediate grew without bound (35+ GiB and climbing before being killed, versus 1.72 s / 1.70 GiB with aligned column types). ## Approach The exact-type guard was load-bearing: correlated columns are `PLACEHOLDER` nodes typed with the outer column's type, and every decorrelated DAG declares that type for its inputs, so a substituted column of a different runtime type is a logical error during execution. The substitution therefore cannot simply alias a column of another type, nor cast to the common supertype — it must produce exactly the placeholder's type. Equivalence classes now track `(column name, type)` pairs. The recording guard admits, besides equal types, two verified-safe families: - nullability-only differences (any base type) — the equality predicate rejects `NULL`s; - native-number pairs with a least supertype — for them `equals` is mathematically exact (`9007199254740993 :: Int64 = 9007199254740992.0 :: Float64` is `0`), the supertype exists only when every type embeds losslessly, and `accurateCastOrNull` is exactness-checking, so value equivalence is transitive across a class. At substitution the chosen equivalent column is converted to exactly the correlated type: `toNullable` / lossless `CAST` when widening, `assumeNotNull` / `accurateCastOrNull` when narrowing. For the narrowing conversions a `FilterStep` is inserted below the renaming that drops rows whose value is `NULL` or does not convert exactly — such rows can never satisfy the recorded equality (a top-level AND-conjunct of an ancestor filter), and dropping them before `assumeNotNull` is required so that its arbitrary result for non-converting values cannot leak into aggregation keys (the aggregation decorrelation appends correlated identifiers as group keys). Pairs whose comparison semantics are not consistent with `CAST` keep the previous CROSS JOIN fallback: `Decimal` vs `Float` (comparison converts to `Float` and is inexact), `String` vs `FixedString` (comparison ignores padding), and supertype-less numeric pairs such as `Int64` vs `UInt64` or `Int64` vs `Float64`. ## Verification - The issue's reproducer plans with zero `cross` nodes and returns the same result as the fallback. - New stateless test `05023_correlated_subquery_equivalence_type_conversion` (12 cases: both nullability directions, widening/narrowing/sideways/float numerics with adversarial boundary values, scalar-subquery aggregation with an outer `0` vs inner `NULL`, guarded fallbacks) passed 6/6 runs under harness setting randomization. - A cross-check over 16 type pairs compared `EXISTS` / `NOT EXISTS` / scalar `count()` results between substitution and the CROSS JOIN fallback on value pools with boundary values (`2^31±1`, `2^32±1`, `2^53`, `2^53+1`, non-integer floats) and `NULL`s — identical everywhere, and plan probes confirmed the substitution fires exactly for the admitted pairs. - The existing `correlated` stateless subset passes (3 environment-only failures in the local scratch setup: MinIO, test cluster, writable access storage). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115493&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115493](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115493+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description When a praktika job dies in a step that is not the node named by `result_name_for_cidb`, CIDB gets one row whose entire `test_context_raw` is `Failures: N/M`, and zero test rows. The step's `info` (the server-log tail naming the cause) reaches no row at all, so no test-name-keyed and no signature-keyed query can see the failure, including anti-join scans requiring `test_name != ''`. 30d on public CIDB: 22 master jobs across 39 distinct checks. One of them, `Stateless tests (amd_debug, distributed plan, s3 storage, parallel)` at `b03544a19bc` ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=b03544a19bc3e7046b8ac5eb6467bf444f295038&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_debug%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20parallel%29)): its failing `Start ClickHouse Server` node carries 301 lines, and CIDB got 13 bytes. Cause: `json_data_generator` emits the job row with `test_context_raw = result.info`, plus one row per child of the single node `_get_sub_result_with_test_cases` matches by exact name. A failing sibling of that node is visited by neither loop, and `result.info` is then the count-only fallback `Result._add_job_summary_to_info` writes while `info` is empty. This appends `"<name>: <info>"` for each failing direct child that reaches no other row, after the existing text, so the old value stays a strict prefix. Child rows are unchanged, since a `test_name='Install ClickHouse'` row would enter per-test statistics and flaky-rate aggregations. A child whose `info` is already in the job's own text is skipped: `fast_test.py` copies the `Tests` node's info onto the root without clearing it, and `Result.create_from(with_info_from_results=True)` already lifts child info in this same shape. Not addressed: `Keeper Stress` names a `result_name_for_cidb` no child carries, so its cases reach no row. Different root cause, different files; this change does not recover them. Validation: new `ci/tests/test_cidb_job_row_carries_step_failure.py`, 16 cases including 5 byte-identity negative controls and 2 duplication guards. Each of the three predicate clauses was mutation-tested and fails only its own arms. Replaying the fixed generator over the `b03544a19bc` report JSON still yields exactly one row, now naming the step. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115526&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115526](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115526+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix data race in shared format init exception rethrow
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a data race (and rare crash) when a parsing/analysis error is reported while reading a file/object storage table. A parse error raised during lazy `KeyCondition` initialization was shared as a single exception object across reader threads, and two threads could concurrently append `(in file/uri ...)` to its message, racing on the exception message string. ### Description The race is in the lazy, `std::call_once`-guarded init of the shared format filter, not in `ParallelParsingInputFormat` (that class has a single reader thread per its header and the `IProcessor` no-parallel-work rule). `FormatFilterInfo::initKeyConditionOnce` builds a `KeyCondition` under `call_once`; if that throws (e.g. `convertFieldToType` failing to parse a `DateTime64` literal, `readDateTimeTextFallback`), the exception is stored in `init_exception` and rethrown to every later reader via `std::rethrow_exception(init_exception)`. `std::rethrow_exception` hands out the SAME managed `DB::Exception` object. Up the stack, `IInputFormat::generate()` mutates it in place in its catch block via `e.addMessage(...)` -> `Poco::Exception::extendedMessage()`, which appends to the exception's `_msg` `std::string`. Two `StorageObjectStorageSource::generate()` readers therefore race on `_msg` (TSan report STID 2427-2c05, allocation stack in `FormatFilterInfo::initKeyConditionOnce`; the same class was seen as a segfault). Fix both `call_once` init sites (`FormatFilterInfo::initKeyConditionOnce` and the symmetric `FormatParserSharedResources::initOnce`): keep the stored `init_exception` an immutable template that is only ever read, and hand each caller - the first thrower and every later rethrower - a private copy via `copyMutableException()`. Both reads of the stored `exception_ptr` happen inside `call_once`, so the copies are race-free. `Common/Exception.h` documents that returning a reference to a mutable `DB::Exception` is unsafe for exactly this reason; @ azat applied the same helper to the Parquet reader in f6025e3. The earlier `ParallelParsingInputFormat` change is reverted - it was not the racing path. CI report (STID 2427-2c05, Stress test (amd_tsan)): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108469&sha=aef76155cf7a0af8fe890077cbea2598f0a521d9&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_tsan%29

signal.title: Fix geoToH3 accepting float types it cannot execute
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/101813 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/101813 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `geoToH3` declared that it accepts any float type but only executes `Float64`, so a `Float32` or `BFloat16` coordinate was rejected late with a message naming the wrong argument position and the wrong type. Such arguments are now rejected during analysis with the correct position and type. Closes #101813. ### Description `geoToH3` validated its coordinates with `isFloat` (`Float32 | Float64 | BFloat16`) while `executeImpl` binds them with `checkAndGetColumn<ColumnFloat64>`. A `Float32` argument therefore passed analysis and failed in a runtime check whose argument index is hardcoded for the legacy `geotoh3_argument_order = 'lon_lat'`. Under the default `lat_lon` both the reported position and type were wrong, and because the type was read off that hardcoded index the message named the other, valid argument: ``` SELECT geoToH3(toFloat32(55.71), toFloat64(37.79), toUInt8(15)); -- was (44): Illegal type Float64 of argument 2 of function geoToH3. Must be Float64. -- now (43): ... as 1st argument 'latitude' ... Expected: Float64, got: Float32 ``` I narrowed both coordinate descriptors to exact `Float64` in both order branches, restoring the check this function had before 5340c88271a4f4f. `validateFunctionArguments` is already order-aware, so position, argument name and both types are now correct in all four slots; `lon_lat` reported the right position before and still does. No query that runs today stops running, since no `Float32` or `BFloat16` call to `geoToH3` succeeds, so no `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp` entry applies. Rejection does move into analysis, so a stored `MATERIALIZED geoToH3(f32, f64, 15)` is now refused during DDL validation rather than at insert time. Such a column could never be computed, so this surfaces an already-broken definition earlier. The two runtime index expressions are corrected as defence in depth; narrowing makes them unreachable, so I claim no test coverage for that half. `s2CapUnion` has the same mismatch but a fixed argument order, so its indices are correct. The new shell test asserts position, argument name and both types for each coordinate slot under both setting values, plus `BFloat16` and a `Float64` case that must still succeed. A `serverError` annotation would check only the code, which passes unfixed. Verified red without the change and green with it over 50 randomized runs. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115503&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115503](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115503+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115503&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115503](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115503+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR in normal projection optimization with correlated subqueries
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103695 (same `Invalid number of columns in chunk pushed to OutputPort` error family) ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` raised when a normal projection was used to read the input of a correlated subquery (decorrelated into a join) and all parts were served from the projection. Depending on the settings it was reported as `Invalid number of columns in chunk pushed to OutputPort` or as `Block structure mismatch in joined block stream`. It is an exception in release builds and aborts the server in debug and sanitizer builds. ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer, reproduces on current master and is unrelated to the pull requests it was seen on: [amd_msan](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=100332&sha=766a499fbbfcfb5b1cbd865a4f435f75c7b5ee28&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_msan%29) (STID 2270-3452), [amd_tsan](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=92472&sha=0d58afae81ce01111323d3f73a59d6d032d199f7&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_tsan%29) (STID 0993-3a3c), and `Stress test (arm_debug)`. Root cause: `optimizeUseNormalProjections` reads the projection over `required_columns = reading->getAllColumnNames()`. Columns of that set which the rebuilt `query.dag` does not consume survive as pass-throughs, because `ActionsDAG::updateHeader` appends every un-consumed input, and widen the rewritten read's output header. The all-parts-from-projection branch spliced that widened node in without the `blocksHaveEqualStructure` check the Union branch already had, so a downstream step got more columns than its declared header. Change: emit the replaced header's columns by name, dropping the surplus pass-throughs so the projection stays usable, and hoist the equal-structure check to cover both replacement branches. It stays below the narrowing as a fail-closed net for what narrowing cannot repair (a missing column, or a type difference), skipping the projection and keeping the regular read. Since `filterPartsByProjection` mutates the parent analysis result in place, it now runs only after that check passes, so a skipped projection no longer drops parts; `has_parent_parts` moves ahead of it and is computed non-destructively. Validation: the load-bearing regression test is `03324_union_block_structure_mismatch`. Reverting only this change makes its first statement fail with `PROJECTION_NOT_USED`; that statement previously carried `-- { serverError PROJECTION_NOT_USED }`, so the projection is now used where it was refused before. `04410` and `04907` pin the plan shape via `EXPLAIN`: every read served by the projection, none declined, no base-table arm. The `04410` carriers abort on the commit the fuzzer reports came from, but not at the current merge-base, where an earlier pass prevents the widening; they are kept as plan-shape pins, not as the proof. The failing-test set across the projection, prewhere, part_offset and correlated suites is unchanged. <details><summary>Both carriers: error signatures</summary> Carrier 1, virtual columns (`_part_offset` in the projection), output port assert: ``` Invalid number of columns in chunk pushed to OutputPort. Expected 2, found 4 src/Processors/Port.h:425 src/Processors/Transforms/JoiningTransform.cpp:101 DB::JoiningTransform::prepare() ``` Carrier 2, real columns. The inner decorrelation join's right side carries exactly one column by design, so the leaked columns trip its structure check instead of the output port one: ``` Block structure mismatch in joined block stream: different number of columns: __table3.timestamp UInt64 UInt64(size = 0) __table3.timestamp UInt64 UInt64(size = 2), payload String String(size = 2), id UUID Sparse(size = 2, UUID(size = 1), UInt64(size = 0)) src/Core/Block.cpp:863 DB::assertBlocksHaveEqualStructureAllowReplicated src/Interpreters/ConstantJoin.cpp:230 DB::ConstantJoin::addBlockToJoin src/Processors/Transforms/JoiningTransform.cpp:373 DB::FillingRightJoinSideTransform::work() ``` `correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer = 0` selects the `ConstantJoin` assert; adding `correlated_subqueries_default_join_kind = 'left'` selects the output port one. Runnable reproducers for both are the statements in the new test file. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111401&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111401](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111401+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Resolve the default time zone from an absolute `TZ` path outside `TZDIR`
signal.text: If `TZ` contains an absolute path or is not set and the requested file is not inside the `TZDIR` directory, try to resolve the time zone id as the longest suffix recognized by the embedded time zone database. If the parent dir of the found suffix is `right`, the file is rejected as we assume that it contains leap seconds and such files are not supported. `glibc` ignores `TZDIR` when `TZ` is an absolute path, so this behavior is more aligned with `glibc` than failing to resolve at all. If we fail to resolve the time zone id, the reported error message now also contains the time zone database directory that was used. The embedded database is used as the oracle rather than `TZDIR` to avoid dependency on `TZDIR` if `TZ` contains an absolute path. It also doesn't need filesystem access and yields ids that `DateLUTImpl` is able to load. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/86495 ### Out of scope A `TZ` value that cannot be resolved still throws while initializing the `DateLUT` singleton, which terminates the process at startup. Matching `glibc` more closely would mean degrading to UTC with a clear warning for the operator; that is a separate behavioural change. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The default time zone is now also determined when the `TZ` environment variable holds an absolute path to a time zone file located outside the time zone database directory (`TZDIR`). The time zone id is now recovered from the longest suffix of the path that names a time zone in the embedded time zone database. Files under a `right/` directory are rejected explicitly, since they are assumed to be encoded with leap seconds, which are not supported. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115483&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115483](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115483+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Stop resolving the UTC time zone in `TimezoneMixin`
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112496 --> While profiling `clickhouse local --query "SELECT 1"` it turned out that almost all of the run happens before the query: the query itself took 1ms of a 45ms run. This is one of the sources of that startup work, split out of #112496. `TimezoneMixin` resolved the UTC time zone in its constructor, in addition to the named or default one. Building a `DateLUTImpl` walks ~146k days through cctz, about 70M instructions, and `DataTypeDateTime` / `DataTypeDateTime64` get constructed just to name a column type — for example when building the schemas of the system tables — without ever touching UTC. Only the serializations need UTC, for ISO output and for the `best_effort` parsers, so `SerializationDateTime`, `SerializationDateTime64` and the `DateTime` / `DateTime64` nodes of `JSONExtractTree` declare their own `utc_time_zone` member instead. The cost is then paid once per formatter rather than once per named type. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Naming a `DateTime` or `DateTime64` type no longer builds a UTC time zone lookup table that nothing reads, which makes constructing these types — and therefore starting up `clickhouse local` and `clickhouse client` — faster. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115488&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115488](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115488+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Rename `allow_experimental_adaptive_codec_selection` to `enable_adaptive_codec_selection`
signal.text: Renames the MergeTree setting `allow_experimental_adaptive_codec_selection` to `enable_adaptive_codec_selection`. The `allow_experimental_` prefix is the pre-tier way of gating a feature. The `EXPERIMENTAL` tier in the declaration already carries that information and is exposed as `tier` in `system.merge_tree_settings`, so the prefix duplicates it in the one place that is expensive to change later: the name. When the feature graduates, a prefixed name has to be renamed and the old spelling carried as an alias forever. That is why the tree already holds `allow_experimental_analyzer` -> `enable_analyzer`, `allow_experimental_nullable_tuple_type` -> `enable_nullable_tuple_type` and `allow_experimental_database_iceberg` -> `allow_database_iceberg`. With the tier doing the gating, graduation becomes a one-word change. `enable_` matches the neighbouring MergeTree booleans (`enable_block_number_column`, `enable_block_offset_column`, `enable_mixed_granularity_parts`). **Why this can be a plain rename.** The setting was added in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111834 and has not shipped in any release: its `SettingsChangesHistory` entry sits in the unreleased `26.8` block, which this PR updates in place. So there is no alias, no `MAKE_OBSOLETE` and no compatibility entry, and nothing for `compatibility` to revert. The tier stays `EXPERIMENTAL` and the default stays `false`; only the name changes. The autogenerated settings reference pages (`docs/reference/settings/merge-tree-settings/allow-experimental.mdx`, the manifest, the settings explorer and the legacy-route map) still spell the old name. They are generated from a binary's introspection tables by the nightly docs job (`ci/jobs/docs_autogen_nightly.py`), so they are deliberately not hand-edited here and the setting will move to its new group page on the next run. Hand-written prose in `docs/reference/statements/create/table.mdx` is updated. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111834 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113479&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113479](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113479+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: allow_non_metadata_alters=0 does not block many mutation-triggering ALTERs and its documentation is unclear
signal.text: ### Company or project name EnterpriseDB ### Describe what's wrong The setting `allow_non_metadata_alters=0` is documented as a safety switch to prevent `ALTER` statements that rewrite table data. In practice it only blocks a subset of mutation-causing `ALTER` commands. Several statements that trigger mutations (background part rewrites) still succeed with the setting turned off, and the docs do not say which ones. The following statements are **not** blocked, even though they schedule mutations and rewrite parts: - `ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE ... WHERE ...` - `ALTER TABLE ... DELETE WHERE ...` - `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE INDEX ...` - `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE PROJECTION ...` - `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE COLUMN ...` - `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE TTL` - `ALTER TABLE ... APPLY DELETED MASK` - `ALTER TABLE ... APPLY PATCHES` - `ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN c` when `c` is an `ALIAS` (metadata-only, so arguably correct, but not documented) The setting **does** block column-payload changes (on `MergeTree` engines) e.g.: - `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN c <new_type>` when the type change rewrites data - `ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN c` where `c` is a physical column (including `MATERIALIZED`) [The docs](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/allow#allow_non_metadata_alters) are very minimal: > > `allow_non_metadata_alters` > Allow to execute alters which affects not only tables metadata, but also data on disk There's no mention here of key terms like "DDL" or "mutation" that might be searched for so it's hard to find. And the description isn't specific about what it actually permits vs blocks. In reality, it only restricts a subset of mutation-causing operations, and only on `MergeTree` tables, but a user would never be able to tell that from the documentation Sidenotes: * Non-`MergeTree` engines (`Memory`, `Log`, `TinyLog`, `StripeLog`, ...) ignore the check entirely, but that's pretty reasonable as they don't really have meaningful async mutations. It's still a bit confusing as the docs don't say anything about how this does or does not affect non-mergetree tables. * Lightweight `DELETE FROM ... WHERE ...` and Lightweight `UPDATE ... SET ... WHERE ...` are also permitted when this setting is 0 to block alters; arguably these are not "mutations" or "alters" so this is fairly reasonable, but would be good to call out explicitly. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes ### How to reproduce ```sql DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ana_gaps; CREATE TABLE ana_gaps ( key UInt64, v_str String, v_num UInt16, v_dt DateTime, v_d Date, v_mat UInt64 MATERIALIZED key * 2, v_ali UInt64 ALIAS key * 3 ) ENGINE = MergeTree() PARTITION BY tuple() ORDER BY key SETTINGS enable_block_number_column = 1, enable_block_offset_column = 1; INSERT INTO ana_gaps (key, v_str, v_num, v_dt, v_d) VALUES (1, 'a', 1, '2020-01-01 00:00:00', '2020-01-01'); SET allow_non_metadata_alters = 0; SELECT '-- positive: DROP COLUMN (physical)'; ALTER TABLE ana_gaps DROP COLUMN v_str; -- { serverError ALTER_OF_COLUMN_IS_FORBIDDEN } SELECT '-- gap: ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE (explicit heavy mutation)'; ALTER TABLE ana_gaps UPDATE v_num = 42 WHERE key = 1; SELECT 'mutations:', count() FROM system.mutations WHERE database = currentDatabase() AND table = 'ana_gaps'; SELECT '-- gap: ALTER TABLE ... DELETE (explicit heavy mutation)'; ALTER TABLE ana_gaps DELETE WHERE key = 999; SELECT 'mutations:', count() FROM system.mutations WHERE database = currentDatabase() AND table = 'ana_gaps'; SELECT '-- gap: MATERIALIZE COLUMN (default backfill)'; SET allow_non_metadata_alters = 1; ALTER TABLE ana_gaps ADD COLUMN v_backfill UInt64 DEFAULT key + 100; SET allow_non_metadata_alters = 0; SELECT 'mutations:', count() FROM system.mutations WHERE database = currentDatabase() AND table = 'ana_gaps'; ALTER TABLE ana_gaps MATERIALIZE COLUMN v_backfill; SELECT 'mutations:', count() FROM system.mutations WHERE database = currentDatabase() AND table = 'ana_gaps'; ``` Result of execution - the explicit mutations and the `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE COLUMN` all triggered mutations and were unexpectedly permitted to run: ``` -- positive: DROP COLUMN (physical) -- gap: ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE (explicit heavy mutation) mutations: 1 -- gap: ALTER TABLE ... DELETE (explicit heavy mutation) mutations: 2 -- gap: MATERIALIZE COLUMN (default backfill) mutations: 2 mutations: 3 ``` For details and a more complete list of statements that bypass this check, see the test case lightweight CI run I did at https://github.com/ringerc/ClickHouse-patches/pull/3 to validate these, particularly the test sql for the gaps and the test script for the engine matching: * [04869_allow_non_metadata_alters_gaps.sql ](https://github.com/ringerc/ClickHouse-patches/blob/test-allow-non-metadata-alters-gaps/tests/queries/0_stateless/04869_allow_non_metadata_alters_gaps.sql) and [04869_allow_non_metadata_alters_gaps.reference](https://github.com/ringerc/ClickHouse-patches/blob/test-allow-non-metadata-alters-gaps/tests/queries/0_stateless/04869_allow_non_metadata_alters_gaps.reference) * [04870_allow_non_metadata_alters_engines.sh](https://github.com/ringerc/ClickHouse-patches/blob/test-allow-non-metadata-alters-gaps/tests/queries/0_stateless/04870_allow_non_metadata_alters_engines.sh) and [04870_allow_non_metadata_alters_engines.reference](https://github.com/ringerc/ClickHouse-patches/blob/test-allow-non-metadata-alters-gaps/tests/queries/0_stateless/04870_allow_non_metadata_alters_engines.reference) ### Expected behavior Expected `ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE`, `ALTER TABLE ... DELETE`, `ALTER TABLE ana_gaps MATERIALIZE COLUMN` etc to be blocked by `allow_non_metadata_alters` ### Error message and/or stacktrace N/A ### Related issues and pull requests _No response_ ### Additional context The [changelog for the setting's initial introduction read](https://clickhouse.com/docs/resources/changelogs/oss/2020#new-feature-5) > Add setting allow_non_metadata_alters which restricts to execute ALTER queries which modify data on disk. Disabled be default. Closes [#11547](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/11547). [#12635](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/12635) ([alesapin](https://github.com/alesapin)). Related issues * https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/11547 * https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/12635 Related experiment in migration-blocking DDL: * https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114594

signal.title: Fix vacuous assertion in 04102_hash_join_stress_test step 14
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Step 14 of `04102_hash_join_stress_test` pinned `max_joined_block_rows = 100`, a setting that does not exist: the declared name is `max_joined_block_size_rows`. The clause sat inside a subquery, where an unknown setting name is discarded silently, so the step never applied truncation and stayed green because its assertion is inert. PR 115397, which tightens nested-`SETTINGS` validation, turns that into a hard failure. A rename alone leaves the step inert, so three things change: - the setting name; - the oracle. `count()` cannot observe truncation, which changes block geometry and not cardinality: 5000 rows either way. It is now `blockSize()`-based, the idiom of `02962` and `03633`, with `count()` kept; `min_joined_block_size_rows/bytes = 0` stops a squash from re-merging the truncated blocks; - the `SETTINGS` placement, moved outside the subquery, where an unknown name raises `UNKNOWN_SETTING`. Two arms: plain equality reaches the post-hoc block split, and a residual predicate routes through `joinRightColumnsWithAdditionalFilter` and its early break (the predicate is always true on this fixture, so cardinality is unchanged). Block sizes cannot observe that break, since the post-hoc split caps every block either way, so a third assertion checks the join row counters, where only a re-probed remainder is counted twice; the sides are summed because the planner may swap them. Those counters are local to the initiator, so both statements pin `enable_parallel_replicas = 0`. The multi-map disjunction break stays uncovered. Each arm reddens when truncation is removed. With only the early break deleted, the counter assertion reddens for every `query_plan_join_swap_table` value and every parallel-replica arm, while the block-size one stays `Ok`. Runs pass with randomization on and off, six concurrent copies, and 25 settings arms. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115397&sha=3f9b9c92090140528a0eb86b3bb0e059efb8f842&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28arm_binary%2C%20parallel%29 No related open issue. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115513&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115513](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115513+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
