signal.title: Transform JOIN hash table payload to row major
signal.text: Resolves [#97883](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/97883) Introduce an alternative layout for hash table payload in hash joins, where fixed and contiguous columns under a certain size are transformed into one row-major block of data. Before the change: ``` col1 Int32 col2 String col3 UInt8 col4 Float64 ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌────────────┐ │ .... │ │ .... │ │ .... │ │ .... │ │ .... │ │ .... │ │ .... │ │ .... │ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └────────────┘ └──────────────┴──────────────┴───────────────┘ row N → col1[N], col2[N], col3[N], col4[N] ``` After the change: ``` ROW STORE (col1 + col3 + col4, contiguous per row) col2 String (columnar) ┌──────────┬──────────┬────────────┐ ┌──────────┐ │ col1 │ col3 │ col4 │ ← row N (record) │ .... │ ← col2[N] ├──────────┼──────────┼────────────┤ ├──────────┤ │ col1 │ col3 │ col4 │ │ .... │ └──────────┴──────────┴────────────┘ └──────────┘ ``` ### Rational: The row-major format allows the output construction to be a tight loop over each column, basically one pointer load and data copy: ``` for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) { const char * row_store_ptr = row_store_ptrs[i]; col->insertData(row_store_ptr + value_offset, value_size); } ``` In comparison the columnar version has to do more work: load columns[j], row_numbers[j], replicated_columns access, insertFrom ... For the following query `SELECT * FROM rs_probe_200m l JOIN rs_right_10m r ON (l.k % toUInt64(10000000 / 0.9)) = r.k FORMAT Null` from `04054_hash_join_with_row_store.sql` the perf counters for `LazyOutput::buildOutput` in `AddedColumns` look as follows: ``` ┌─variant────────────────────────────┬─query_id─────────────────────────────┬─runtime_ms─┬───────instr─┬──────cycles─┬──────cmiss─┬──brmiss─┬───ipc─┬─cmiss_per_kinstr─┬─brmiss_per_kinstr─┐ │ row-major-enabled-multi-threaded │ 9d2d6886-2ad7-430f-af2c-6c7cd32f3808 │ 1621 │ 11393048228 │ 31974507197 │ 1470246364 │ 5892574 │ 0.356 │ 129.05 │ 0.517 │ │ row-major-enabled-multi-threaded │ 56b33013-8bec-4d7a-a415-2a06beb14bf6 │ 1633 │ 11547943445 │ 31874206968 │ 1484117664 │ 6265932 │ 0.362 │ 128.52 │ 0.543 │ │ row-major-enabled-multi-threaded │ 65583fa7-9ce0-4426-95eb-977251d38f75 │ 1708 │ 11338601601 │ 31825721703 │ 1468670383 │ 5921051 │ 0.356 │ 129.53 │ 0.522 │ │ row-major-disabled-multi-threaded │ 5ff1b154-3c3f-40c6-bae9-f6cf0feafe81 │ 2548 │ 15453833738 │ 58322156979 │ 2636461094 │ 9533242 │ 0.265 │ 170.6 │ 0.617 │ │ row-major-disabled-multi-threaded │ 6e92c1d4-8432-4a79-a6cc-85e38232116d │ 2580 │ 15400954730 │ 58683032344 │ 2623136775 │ 9455570 │ 0.262 │ 170.32 │ 0.614 │ │ row-major-disabled-multi-threaded │ 133f384f-c09a-4e12-9e69-85b61272a360 │ 2686 │ 15419169622 │ 59548322941 │ 2647601264 │ 9746405 │ 0.259 │ 171.71 │ 0.632 │ │ row-major-enabled-single-threaded │ 20039e91-b5dc-4b4a-8e22-f4451f6067be │ 30610 │ 9046504977 │ 16964398066 │ 995568814 │ 3235355 │ 0.533 │ 110.05 │ 0.358 │ │ row-major-disabled-single-threaded │ a3f9a822-dae6-45c1-9a4e-63e87a3592e8 │ 56821 │ 15279361788 │ 27940919919 │ 1167368997 │ 4694553 │ 0.547 │ 76.4 │ 0.307 │ └────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────┴────────────┴─────────────┴─────────────┴────────────┴─────────┴───────┴──────────────────┴───────────────────┘ ``` ### Changes: - A `RowDataStore` that takes a set of columns and lays them in row major format. It exposes access to individual rows and the layout of each row (offset and size of fields in a row). - New `IColumn` interfaces that handle building the output columns from the row store, used manly by `AddedColumns.cpp`. - Two new settings to control the row-major transformation: - min_columns_for_hash_join_row_store: the minimum number of columns that must be suitable to the transformation to apply. - min_rows_ratio_for_hash_join_row_store: Minimum estimated ratio of join output rows to build-side rows to enable transforming hash join payload to row-major. Used in the planner to decide when to enable the optimization. - A runtime feedback loop that tracks the number of hash table matches from a join and feeds it to the next execution of the join instead of relying on the estimated join output: - The match count is only published when the probe phase fully completes. - Only joins that went through the join reorder optimizer get a cache key. - Plans serialized to distributed workers don't collect or use the feedback. ### Limitations: 1. Only supports fixed and contiguous types and nullable version of them. Supporting non fixed rows would make the row-major layout non-uniform between rows and output column construction loop would not be as tight anymore. Also transforming unbounded unfixed types to row major could be very heavy. 2. ColumnReplicated might get materialized. The decision is made based on the column state the join sees in the first block. If it's ColumnReplicated the column is excluded from the row store, if it's not the column is included and it's replicated in a future block it get's materialized. 3. If spilling occurs, the row stored data is split back into columns for now. In a follow up we can make the row store a column and spill it as is. ### Build overhead: | Type | Rows | Columns | avg per worker thread (ms) | |---|---|---|---| | Int64 | 2M | 8 | 28.2 | | Int64 | 1M | 16 | 31.9 | | FixedString(16) | 1M | 8 | 24.6 | | FixedString(16) | 2M | 4 | 21.5 | ### Benchmarks: #### from `04054_hash_join_with_row_store.sql`: | # | Right table | Match | Join | Before (s) | After (s) | Speedup | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 0 | `rs_right_100k` | 0.9 | INNER | 0.265 | 0.237 | 1.12× | | 1 | `rs_right_100k` | 0.3 | INNER | 0.182 | 0.178 | 1.02× | | 2 | `rs_right_10m` | 0.9 | INNER | 1.108 | 0.525 | 2.11× | | 3 | `rs_right_10m` | 0.3 | INNER | 0.532 | 0.335 | 1.59× | | 4 | `rs_right_100k_nullable` | 0.9 | INNER | 0.350 | 0.249 | 1.41× | | 5 | `rs_right_100k_nullable` | 0.3 | INNER | 0.216 | 0.183 | 1.18× | | 6 | `rs_right_10m_nullable` | 0.9 | INNER | 1.607 | 0.553 | 2.91× | | 7 | `rs_right_10m_nullable` | 0.3 | INNER | 0.698 | 0.357 | 1.95× | | 8 | `rs_right_10m` | 0.9 | FULL | 1.652 | 0.916 | 1.80× | | 9 | `rs_right_10m` | 0.3 | FULL | 1.424 | 0.861 | 1.65× | | 10 | `rs_right_1m_x10` | 0.9 | INNER | 2.239 | 1.554 | 1.44× | | 11 | `rs_right_1m_x10` | 0.3 | INNER | 0.825 | 0.641 | 1.29× | | 12 | `rs_right_1m_nullable_x10` | 0.9 | INNER | 3.771 | 1.820 | 2.07× | | 13 | `rs_right_1m_nullable_x10` | 0.3 | INNER | 1.372 | 0.771 | 1.78× | | 14 | `rs_right_mixed_10m` | 0.9 | INNER | 1.596 | 1.249 | 1.28× | | 15 | `rs_right_mixed_10m` | 0.3 | INNER | 0.759 | 0.628 | 1.21× | | 16 | `rs_right_wide_10m` | 0.9 | INNER | 6.158 | 1.979 | 3.11× | | 17 | `rs_right_wide_10m` | 0.3 | INNER | 2.563 | 1.111 | 2.31× | ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Introduce an alternative layout for hash table payload in hash joins, where qualifying columns are transformed into one row-major block of data in order to speed up join output reconstruction. Controlled by two new settings: `min_columns_for_hash_join_row_store` (default 3, the minimum number of fixed-size payload columns that triggers the row-major layout; set to 0 to disable) and `min_rows_ratio_for_hash_join_row_store` (default 2, the minimum estimated ratio of join output rows to build-side rows to enable the transformation).

signal.title: Deriving deterministic conditions from conditions involving the current time for the query condition cache
signal.text: ### Company or project name ClickHouse ### Describe the situation When a user writes ``` time >= now() - INTERVAL 10 DAY ``` it cannot be used for the query condition cache. But if we add a redundant condition: ``` time >= now() - INTERVAL 10 DAY AND time >= '2026-08-09' -- this is rounded down to the previous day ``` The condition can be used until the end of day. By persisting conditions with coarsened boundaries, we can balance between cache usefulness and invalidation. For example, the rounding can be up/down to the grid with the size of the interval multiplied by some configured constant (e.g., 1.0) and some maximum (e.g., 1 day). ### Which ClickHouse versions are affected? . ### How to reproduce . ### Expected performance _No response_ ### Related issues and pull requests _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_

signal.title: Push subcolumn reads into subqueries
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/75538 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/92455 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Read only the requested subcolumns of columns exported by subqueries, CTEs and `UNION ALL` branches instead of the whole columns. Ordinary views benefit when `analyzer_inline_views = 1`. For example, `SELECT data.a FROM (SELECT * FROM table)` with a `JSON` column `data` now reads only the subcolumn `data.a` from the table. Controlled by the new setting `optimize_push_subcolumns_into_subqueries` (enabled by default). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) --- When a subcolumn of a column exported by a subquery is requested, it is resolved into the `getSubcolumn` function over the whole column: `SELECT data.a FROM (SELECT * FROM test)` reads the whole `data` column from the table and extracts the subcolumn afterwards. The new query tree pass `PushSubcolumnsIntoSubqueries` adds the subcolumn to the subquery projection and replaces the `getSubcolumn` function with a reference to it. If the whole column is not used anywhere else, it is then removed from the subquery projection by the subsequent `RemoveUnusedProjectionColumns` pass, so only the subcolumn is read from the table. The pushdown works through several levels of subqueries, CTEs and `UNION ALL` branches, and also applies to `Tuple`, `Nullable`, `Array` and other types with subcolumns. Ordinary views benefit when `analyzer_inline_views = 1`. `UNION ALL` subqueries are supported: the subcolumn is added to every branch at the same position, all-or-nothing, and only when the branch types match exactly (the subcolumn of the least supertype is not guaranteed to be the supertype of the branch subcolumns). The `DISTINCT`, `INTERSECT` and `EXCEPT` modes deduplicate or match rows over all projection columns, so such subqueries are not rewritten (nor are recursive CTEs). The pushdown is skipped when it could change the query result: - when the subquery uses `DISTINCT`, `GROUP BY`, aggregate functions, or `ORDER BY ... WITH FILL` (an added projection column would change the result or would not be valid); - when the subquery is on a side of a `JOIN` that can be filled with default values for non-matched rows (`getSubcolumn` of a default value is not always equal to the default value of the subcolumn type, e.g. for the `null` subcolumn of `Nullable` columns); a shared subquery node (an ordinary CTE referenced several times) found in any such position is ineligible for all of its occurrences; - in the outer query with aggregation, an occurrence of `getSubcolumn` is only replaced when it is evaluated before the aggregation step (`WHERE`, `JOIN ON`, arguments of aggregate functions) or when the whole expression is an aggregation key; - when the column types diverge, e.g. under `join_use_nulls` or `group_by_use_nulls`; - when the whole column is also read in the outer query, including uses by correlated subqueries and uses under a different exported name of the same physical column (`SELECT tup AS x, tup FROM t`, or a trivial `ALIAS` storage column next to its base column), and uses of an exported column the pushed subcolumn is a part of (`SELECT x.b, tup FROM (SELECT tup.a AS x, tup FROM t)`, where the live `tup` export already reads everything `tup.a.b` reads; an export of a sibling or of a deeper subcolumn does not block the pushdown, it reads less than the whole column): the subquery would then read both the whole column and the subcolumn from the table, while extracting the subcolumn from the already read column is cheaper. For a `UNION ALL` target the alias equivalence of exported names is detected in every branch (the pushdown is applied to all branches or to none), so a single branch exporting the same physical column under another name that stays alive blocks the rewrite. The decision counts only sibling subcolumns that are validated as actually pushable into the target (in a side-effect-free dry run): when two subcolumns of the same exported column are requested and only one of them can be pushed (e.g. the other is shadowed by a same-named storage column inside the subquery), nothing is pushed, since the unpushable sibling keeps the whole column alive. - for references of a reused `MATERIALIZED` CTE (`enable_materialized_cte`): the temporary table serves all references of the CTE, so pruning the parent column there would require proving that no reference needs the whole column. Single-use materialized CTEs are inlined by the analyzer and take the ordinary subquery path (subcolumn reads over materialized CTEs are currently broken on master independently of this change, see https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113623). Subqueries spelled with an alias list, e.g. `SELECT x.a FROM (SELECT json FROM t) AS s(x)`, are supported. Trivial `ALIAS` columns (an `ALIAS` whose body is just another column of the same table, possibly chained) exported by a subquery are followed down to the underlying storage column. A subquery can also export a derived subcolumn (e.g. `SELECT json.a AS x FROM ...` over a deeper subquery keeps a `getSubcolumn(json, 'a')` projection expression); reading a subcolumn of such an export composes the paths (`a` + `b` -> `a.b`), so the pushdown continues through derived exports down to the base table. Conversely, when no name of such an alias-equivalent class of exports remains referenced in the outer queries, the never-referenced sibling exports are dead together with the replaced ones (all of them are removed by `RemoveUnusedProjectionColumns`), so they do not block the pushdown through the deeper levels of subqueries; the alias-equivalent classes are taken from every branch of a `UNION ALL` target. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112688&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112688](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112688+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix wrong count and wrong DELETE when a NULL expression sits under NOT
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112242 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112242 Requested by @ nihalzp in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112242#issuecomment-5312306258 (reported by @ zlareb1). ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results when a `WHERE` clause contained a `NULL` expression under a `NOT`, for example `SELECT count() FROM t WHERE NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL)`. Index analysis treated such a condition as provably true for the whole range, so the filter was skipped: `count()` returned rows the query rejects, and `ALTER TABLE ... DELETE` with that condition removed rows it should have kept. ### Description ```sql CREATE TABLE t (id UInt32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; INSERT INTO t SELECT number FROM numbers(40); SELECT count() FROM t WHERE NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL); -- returned 40, correct is 20 ``` Reading the rows returned 20, so `count()` and the row set disagreed on one predicate. A mutation was worse: `ALTER TABLE t DELETE WHERE NOT (id >= 38 AND NULL)` deleted all 40 rows, although the predicate is `NULL` for `id` 38 and 39, so those two had to survive. **Root cause.** `cloneDAGWithInversionPushDown` pushes `NOT` to the leaves. For `NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL)`, De Morgan turns the `and` into an `or` and pushes the inversion into both children; the all-NULL leaf is not recognized, so the tail wraps it in a literal `not()`, which `RPNBuilder` complements classically into "provably true for every row". Both steps hold only in two-valued logic: `NOT NULL` is `NULL`, which `WHERE` must reject. **The change.** Before the node dispatch, an all-NULL node absorbs the inversion instead of receiving a `not()` wrapper, the same idiom the neighbouring `materialize` and trivial-cast branches use. It still folds to "never true" downstream, correct because `NULL` is not `TRUE`, and a non-negated `x AND NULL` keeps its exact fast path. Absorbing the inversion substitutes the operand's type for the `not()` result type, so the guard is confined to `boolean_context`, the existing flag for positions where the caller discards the value. In a value position a negation would otherwise change type and drop valid rows. The all-NULL test needs both a column and a type check: `toInt64OrNull('x')` is typed `Nullable(Int64)`, while `if(id % 2, NULL, NULL)` has no constant column. <details> <summary>Validation</summary> Debug build of the base commit vs the same build with the change. | probe | base | with change | correct | |---|---|---|---| | `count() WHERE NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL)` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `toInt64OrNull('x')` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)')` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `if(id % 2, NULL, NULL)` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `materialize(NULL)` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | `numbers(100) WHERE NOT (number = 5 AND NULL) LIMIT 10` | 9 | 10 | 10 | | minmax skip index, same predicate | 40 | 20 | 20 | | `ALTER DELETE WHERE NOT (id >= 38 AND NULL)`, survivors | `[]` | `[38,39]` | `[38,39]` | | `count() WHERE id >= 20 AND NULL` | 0 | 0 | 0 | | `numbers() WHERE number > 0 AND NULL LIMIT 10` | 0 fast | 0 fast | 0 fast | | value position, `ifNull(NOT materialize(CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(Int64)')), 0)`, rows | 40 | 40 | 40 | | same with `Nullable(Float64)`, rows | 40 | 40 | 40 | The new test fails on the base build, passes with the change, and passed 50/50 randomized runs. Deleting any one of the three parts of the guard makes it fail again on exactly the arms that part covers: the column test covers `toInt64OrNull` and `CAST`, the type test covers `if(id % 2, NULL, NULL)`, the `boolean_context` test covers the two value-position arms. The unbounded `numbers()` lines pin the positive direction, which an earlier attempt at this fix turned into a hang. The projection, `KeyCondition` and minmax test families were run on both builds: the same 23 tests fail either way, all on ZooKeeper and distributed connections unavailable in this sandbox, none mentioning the exact-count projection or `KeyCondition`. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115152&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115152](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115152+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Auto-escape XML special characters in from_env config substitutions
signal.text: ### What this PR does When direct config values loaded via `from_env` contain XML special characters (`&`, `<`, `>`), the `ConfigProcessor` failed with `SAXParseException` because the raw value was concatenated directly into an XML string. Direct values are now escaped before being embedded into the XML DOM, so an environment variable can hold any XML-1.0-legal value — including one that looks like an XML fragment (taken as literal text) and one that contains the `]]>` sequence the XML grammar forbids in character data. Existing `<include from_env="..."/>` substitutions continue to interpret their value as an XML subtree. Upgrade note: a direct `from_env` value that was XML-entity-encoded for the old XML parser (for example `a&b`) now resolves to its exact literal bytes and must be set raw (`a&b`) instead. This migration is documented and covered by an integration regression. The contents of a ZooKeeper node referenced via `from_zk` may be a whole subtree. A value beginning with `<` is parsed as an XML fragment (both for a structural `<include>` and for a leaf substitution), which is kept for backward compatibility because earlier versions always interpreted a `from_zk` value as XML. An explicit `<include from_zk="..." yaml="true"/>` parses a non-`<` value as a YAML subtree. Without `yaml="true"`, the value remains literal text, so `<include>` is also the generic "replace this element with the node contents" form and may carry a leaf value such as a secret. Whitespace surrounding that `<include>` becomes part of the leaf value, so direct leaf substitutions such as `<password from_zk="..."/>` or `<some_setting from_zk="..."/>` are recommended when exact bytes matter. Those direct leaf substitutions keep a non-`<` value as literal text using its exact original bytes, so existing *plain-text* scalar substitutions and secrets keep working unchanged on upgrade. There is one deliberate behavior change on upgrade: a leaf value that was XML-entity-encoded to satisfy the old parser (which reparsed every `from_zk` value as XML and rejected a raw `&`, `<` or `>` as not well-formed) is now kept as its exact original bytes. A value stored as `a&b` used to decode to `a&b`, but now resolves to the literal `a&b`; such values must be stored raw (`a&b`) instead. This is documented in `docs/concepts/features/configuration/server-config/configuration-files.mdx` and covered by an integration regression. Upgrade note: the same literal-text behavior applies to direct ordinary-element `from_env` substitutions such as `<profiles from_env="..."/>`. Existing XML-subtree imports in that form must migrate to `<profiles><include from_env="..."/></profiles>`; this is documented and covered by an integration regression. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/78835 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry: Fixed direct config substitutions via `from_env` failing when XML-1.0-legal values contain XML special characters like `&`, `<`, `>`, or the `]]>` sequence; existing `<include from_env="..."/>` XML-subtree substitutions are unchanged. An explicit `<include from_zk="..." yaml="true"/>` substitution can read a YAML subtree wherever the generic `<include>` form is used, including inside a leaf element, so it must not be used for a literal secret or setting. Without the explicit `yaml="true"` attribute, a non-`<` value is literal text, but direct non-`<` leaf `from_zk` substitutions are recommended for exact-byte secrets/settings, because surrounding whitespace of an `<include>` becomes part of a leaf value. Values beginning with `<` continue to be interpreted as XML fragments for backward compatibility. Upgrade note: a direct `from_env` value or a non-`<` leaf `from_zk` value that was previously XML-entity-encoded (for example `a&b`) now resolves to its exact literal bytes and must be stored raw (`a&b`) instead. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=101773&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/101773](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F101773+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Reapply "Make `postgresql` and `PostgreSQL` engine work against a ClickHouse instance", with a fix for the cancel-request logical error
signal.text: Reapply #110760, reverted in #112935, together with a fix for the bug that motivated the revert. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110760 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112935 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/84085 ### Why it was reverted, and why the bug is not in the reverted change Every `Stress test` job on master started failing with ``` Logical error: 'Query context must be created after authentication' DB::Session::makeQueryContextImpl @ src/Interpreters/Session.cpp:690 DB::PostgreSQLHandler::cancelRequest @ src/Server/PostgreSQLHandler.cpp:867 DB::PostgreSQLHandler::startup @ src/Server/PostgreSQLHandler.cpp:737 ``` CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=cd6fd72e2b29fa607cffe0595e347452f8dcba9b&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_debug%29 A PostgreSQL client cancels a running statement by opening a *second* connection and sending a `CancelRequest` on it, carrying the `(process id, secret key)` pair the server handed out in `BackendKeyData`. By the protocol that connection never authenticates - the secret key is the credential - so `PostgreSQLHandler::cancelRequest` has no authenticated session, and the `session->makeQueryContext()` it called throws `LOGICAL_ERROR`. That has been true since sessions were introduced (`51ffc334573`), and it is reachable by any PostgreSQL client that cancels a statement: `psql` on Ctrl-C, or the `pgx` driver in issue #84085, which reports this very error. #110760 did not introduce it, it only made CI reach it: with ClickHouse acting as a libpq/pqxx client against itself, `PostgreSQLSource` cancels the remote statement through `PQcancel`, so a stress run that cancels a query now sends a cancel request to the server's own PostgreSQL port. ### The fix (second commit) - `cancelRequest` cancels the query through the process list directly, which needs no session, via a new `ProcessList::sendCancelToQueryOfAnyUser`. Only queries whose id has the `postgres:<connection id>:<secret key>` shape the server itself assigns can be named this way, and the secret key is what makes such an id unguessable - the same credential PostgreSQL relies on. - The raw `KILL QUERY` result the old code wrote straight into the client socket is gone with it. The protocol expects no answer at all to a cancel request, so that was protocol garbage. - The secret key never matched anything either: `BackendKeyData` was sent while `secret_key` was still zero, and every statement then re-randomized it, so the query id a cancel request resolved to was never the id of a running query - cancellation over the PostgreSQL protocol has never worked. The key now belongs to the connection, as in PostgreSQL, where it identifies the backend rather than one statement, and every statement of the connection runs under `postgres:<connection id>:<secret key>`. Statements of one connection run one after another, so reusing the id is safe. - New test `04669_postgresql_protocol_cancel_request`, which drives a real `psql` and cancels it with `SIGINT` - that is what makes `psql` send a `CancelRequest`. The `-- ping` half of issue #84085 (a comment-only statement is not recognized as an empty query) is not addressed here. ### Privileges A self-connect needs nothing beyond access to the table being read. `system.databases`, `system.tables` and `system.columns`, which the emulated `pg_namespace`, `pg_class` and `pg_attribute` are views over, are readable by every user even with `access_control_improvements.select_from_system_db_requires_grant` enabled, and their rows are filtered by the reader's own grants - so the catalog shows a user exactly the relations that user may read, as `pg_catalog` does in PostgreSQL. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The `postgresql` table function and `PostgreSQL` table engine can now be used to connect to another ClickHouse server over the PostgreSQL protocol (when a table name is used; the `query(...)` variant is not supported yet). Added the PostgreSQL-compatibility functions `format_type` and `current_setting`. Fixed cancellation over the PostgreSQL protocol: a cancel request used to log a logical error and never cancelled anything. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112940&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112940](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112940+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix 01514_parallel_formatting timeout by pinning the parse chunk size
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109369 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109369 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `01514_parallel_formatting` is too slow and too variable: it hit the 600 s per-test cap three times in 60 days, all on `Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, parallel, 1/2)`, none on master ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109369&sha=65227fe281090b5891ae106365e7540632172366&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_msan%2C%20WasmEdge%2C%20parallel%2C%201%2F2%29)), and the flaky check here put one run at 270.23 s against its own 180 s limit, median 67.30 s. First, a randomized-settings conjunction reroutes the read-back `count()`: `optimize_count_from_files = 0` makes `need_only_count` false (`StorageFile.cpp:2182`), a precondition for parallel parsing (`FormatFactory.cpp:554-556`), so it goes through `ParallelParsingInputFormat`. The segmentator cuts the file into `min_chunk_bytes_for_parallel_parsing` pieces, randomized as `max(1024, gauss(10 MiB, 5 MB))`, so the left tail collapses onto 1024 bytes against a 10 MiB default. I pin its lower bound to the default with the runner's per-setting limits mechanism, which keeps larger values randomized. Second, the pin alone was not sufficient: the failing run had parallel parsing off and the count fast path on, so that amplification never engaged. What remained is fixture size: the test inserted 3 x 10 M rows and ran `count()` after each, reading back 60 M rows, and that read side dominates at 823 ms against 108 ms of formatting per pass. So I cut the rows tenfold and `max_block_size` with them, 65505 to 1000. The test's subject is the formatter's ring of processing units, indexed `writer_unit_number % processing_units.size()` over `max_threads + 2` entries, so reuse needs the chunk count `rows / max_block_size` to exceed it. Cutting rows alone would drop chunks from 152 to 7 and stop the wrapping; cutting both raises it to 1000, wrapping 29 times on a 32-core runner instead of 4.5, and still wrapping on a 384-core machine where the old fixture never did. Coverage is verified, not assumed: the insert schedules 1005 formatter thread-pool jobs with `output_format_parallel_formatting = 1` against 3 with it off. Under the flaky check's own configuration the 50 runs pass, maximum 6.80 s. Debug build. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.767` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: geoToH3 error messages reference swapped argument positions in default lat_lon mode
signal.text: _Found via ClickGap automated review. Please close or comment if this is incorrect or needs adjustment._ _Retrospective finding from a historical scan of [PR #78852](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/78852) (merged 2025-04-15). Confirmed on current codebase — close with a note if already fixed._ ### Describe what's wrong When geoToH3 is called with Float32 arguments (accepted by type validator but rejected in execution), the error message references the wrong argument position and the wrong type. E.g., geoToH3(toFloat32(55.71), toFloat64(37.79), toUInt8(15)) reports 'Illegal type Float64 of argument 2' when the actual issue is Float32 at argument 1. **Root cause:** geoToH3.cpp:103-104: error for !col_lat always references arguments[1] and position 2, but in lat_lon mode col_lat comes from arguments[0] (position 1). Similarly line 113-114: error for !col_lon always references arguments[0] and position 1, but in lat_lon mode col_lon comes from arguments[1]. **Why we believe this is a bug:** geoToH3.cpp:88-97 assigns col_lat/col_lon from different argument indices based on geotoh3_argument_order setting, but geoToH3.cpp:99-115 hardcodes arguments[1]/position 2 for col_lat errors and arguments[0]/position 1 for col_lon errors, matching only the old lon_lat order. **Affected locations:** - `src/Functions/geoToH3.cpp:99` — Error message for col_lat null check references wrong argument index - `src/Functions/geoToH3.cpp:109` — Error message for col_lon null check references wrong argument index **Impact:** When a user passes Float32 to geoToH3 in default lat_lon mode, the error message points to the wrong argument (position and type), making debugging confusing. The error says the Float64 argument is bad and reports the wrong position. ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `f86671aa80af`). ### How to reproduce ```sql #!/usr/bin/env bash # Tags: no-fasttest # Test: geoToH3 error messages reference wrong argument position in default lat_lon mode CURDIR=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd) # shellcheck source=../shell_config.sh . Error should reference argument 2. # BUG: error references argument 1 and shows Float64 type instead of Float32. ERR2=$($CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT --query "SELECT geoToH3(toFloat64(55.71), toFloat32(37.79), toUInt8(15))" 2>&1) echo "$ERR2" | grep -oP 'argument \d' | head -1 ``` ### Expected behavior ``` argument 1 argument 2 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` argument 2 argument 1 ``` ### Additional context **Open risks:** - Similar pattern may exist in other H3 functions with setting-dependent argument ordering **Suggested fix:** Make the error message indices dynamic based on geotoh3_argument_order, or use the correct argument index for each variable: for col_lat, reference the actual source index (0 in lat_lon mode, 1 in lon_lat mode), and similarly for col_lon. **Analysis details:** Confidence HIGH | Severity P3 | Testability: `STATELESS_SQL` Found during automated review of [PR #78852](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/78852). --- _ClickGapAI · Confidence: HIGH · Severity: P3 · Finding: `h_pr78852_001`_

signal.title: Ask for continuation in single-line mode when query is incomplete
signal.text: ### What this PR does In single-line interactive mode, pressing Enter on an incomplete query (one where the parser reaches the end of input still expecting more tokens) no longer sends it and shows a syntax error. Instead, a newline is inserted into the same edit buffer, exactly like pressing Alt+Enter, so the whole query stays under a single prompt and the arrow keys can navigate and edit across all of its lines. A trailing `;` still forces submission (for example, to deliberately submit an incomplete query and see its syntax error). This replaces the earlier approach that printed a separate `:-] ` continuation prompt and read additional lines, which prevented cross-line editing and could split pasted queries. The completeness check is now passed to `ReplxxLineReader` as a callback and consulted from the `commit_action` bound to Enter. signal.title: Wrong result: optimize_trivial_count_query makes count(arrayJoin(arr)) return the table's row count instead of the number of array elements
signal.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe what's wrong - With the default `optimize_trivial_count_query = 1`, `SELECT count(arrayJoin(arr)) FROM t` returns the number of rows in the table instead of the number of array elements. - arrayJoin is a row-multiplying operator, so the aggregate must observe the post-expansion stream. The trivial-count optimization replaces the entire table read with a stored row counter and never evaluates count's argument, so the ARRAY JOIN expansion is silently dropped. No error, no warning. - The optimization rests on the premise "the number of rows the aggregate sees equals the number of rows stored in the table." That holds for `count()`, `count(1)` and `count(non_nullable_col)`, but arrayJoin breaks it, and nothing in the guard list checks for it. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? signal.title: Add only the required right keys when a join has several disjuncts
signal.text: A join with several disjuncts (`... ON a = b OR c = d`) added every right key column to its result, whether or not the query asked for it. With one disjunct the keys are split out of `sample_block_with_columns_to_add` and put back only where the query needs them, restored from the left key column - the same value, under an equality. With several disjuncts that restoration is invalid: a row matched through another clause has a right key of its own. That is a reason to *read* a key when it is asked for, not a reason to *add* it when it is not - and the plan drops those columns immediately after the join with a `ColumnPermuteTransform`. So keep the keys the query asks for and add nothing else. `TableJoin::requiredRightKeys` already tracks them and the planner fills it in `setUsedColumns`; without the analyzer nothing fills it, so there every key is kept, exactly as before. `right_table_keys` stays whole either way, so the stored right blocks - and a mixed `ON` condition evaluated against them - are untouched. For `SELECT count() FROM l ALL LEFT JOIN r ON l.a = r.a OR l.b = r.b` the join used to emit `__table2.a` and `__table2.b` for every result row, and the permutation threw them away; now it emits neither. It is not measurable on a 20M x 5M join (892 vs 903 ms with four disjuncts), so this is worth having for the work it removes and for what it unblocks, not as a speedup - no performance test is added for that reason. What it unblocks: the key-only join hash tables of https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115301 are chosen for `LEFT SEMI` only when the join produces no right value at all, which with several disjuncts could never be true. `LEFT ANTI` already qualifies there; `LEFT SEMI` starts to once this lands. A new test covers what the pruning must not change: with `ON a = a OR b = b` a row matched through the second clause has an unrelated right `a`, and that value still has to reach the result whenever it is selected - across `ALL`/`ANY`/`SEMI`/`ANTI` and `LEFT`/`INNER`/`RIGHT`/`FULL`, with a non-joined right row, a residual condition, and `join_use_nulls`. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115301 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115465&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115465](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115465+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Do not strip injective functions that hide argument nullability inside uniq
signal.text: `optimize_injective_functions_inside_uniq` stripped any injective function from a `uniq*` argument, on the grounds that an injective function preserves the number of distinct values. That holds for the values, but not for the rows the aggregate sees: `AggregateFunctionFactory::get` wraps `uniq*` in the `Null` combinator when an argument is `Nullable`, and that combinator skips the rows where the argument is NULL. An injective function whose result type cannot be `Nullable` hides the nullability of its argument, so removing it turns "count every row" into "skip the NULL rows": ```sql SELECT uniqExact(tuple(x)) FROM values('x Nullable(Int32)', 1, 2, NULL); -- 2 before this change; 3 with the optimization disabled, and 3 now ``` The pass now keeps a function whenever removing it would change the argument's nullability. The affected functions are `tuple`, `bitmaskToArray` and `bitPositionsToArray` (the injective ones whose result type cannot be `Nullable`, so `makeNullableSafe` leaves it off); the affected aggregates are `uniq`, `uniqExact`, `uniqHLL12` and `uniqTheta`. `uniqCombined` and `uniqCombined64` were already protected, because the `Null` combinator changes their result type to `Nullable(UInt64)` and the pass rejects that. This also removes a discrepancy the same rewrite caused between expressions that differ only in being constant-foldable, reported in the issue: `countDistinct(tuple(NULL))` is folded into a `ConstantNode` and so escaped the pass, while `countDistinct(tuple(arrayJoin([NULL])))` did not. All the variants return 1 now. With `enable_analyzer = 0` the same rewrite runs in `TreeOptimizer` before types are resolved, so the nullability cannot be checked there and the old results stand; the test is tagged `no-old-analyzer`. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114784 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `uniq`, `uniqExact`, `uniqHLL12` and `uniqTheta` returning a wrong result for an argument wrapped in an injective function that hides nullability, such as `uniqExact(tuple(x))` over a `Nullable` column. The `optimize_injective_functions_inside_uniq` optimization removed the wrapping function, after which NULL rows were skipped instead of counted. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115466&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115466](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115466+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Make a table read by a scalar subquery in a CONSTRAINT a loading dependency
signal.text: Attaching a table analyzes its constraints in `InterpreterCreateQuery::getConstraintsDescription`, and the analysis executes the scalar subqueries of a constraint expression. The tables such a subquery reads were not registered as loading dependencies, because `DDLLoadingDependencyVisitor` only looks at functions, dictionary sources and the storage definition. Nothing prevented dropping such a table, and the server did not start afterwards - attaching the dependent table threw `UNKNOWN_TABLE` and loading the metadata failed: ```sql CREATE TABLE t1 (id UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); CREATE TABLE t2 (conversation UInt64, CONSTRAINT c CHECK (SELECT id FROM t1 LIMIT 15) IN (conversation)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); DROP TABLE t1; -- accepted, and the server cannot start anymore ``` The referential dependency was recorded, since `DDLDependencyVisitor` visits `ASTTableExpression`, so `check_referential_table_dependencies = 1` rejected the `DROP`. But that setting is off by default, and it is the loading graph that the default `check_table_dependencies` check and the `DROP DATABASE` drop order (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/97057) use. A constraint declaration is now visited, and the tables of every subquery that the analysis executes are added to the loading dependencies. Subqueries which the analysis does not execute - the right argument of `IN` and the argument of `exists`, see `ExecuteScalarSubqueriesMatcher::visit` - are skipped, because what they read is needed only when the constraint is checked, not to attach the table. That keeps `02916_joinget_dependency`-style patterns working, in particular `02841_not_ready_set_constraints`, which drops the table read by an `x IN (SELECT ...)` constraint on purpose. Seen in CI as a `Cannot start clickhouse-server` stress failure, e.g. https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110231&sha=4de836223549fd5224ca017b8c1a28e344ce38e9&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_msan%29 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114918 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/87369 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A table read by a scalar subquery inside a `CONSTRAINT` is now a loading dependency of the table that declares the constraint. Previously such a table could be dropped, after which the server did not start, because attaching the dependent table executes the subquery. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114923&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114923](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114923+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Honour query cancellation while waiting for a cache dictionary update
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112144 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A query that misses a `cache`, `ssd_cache`, `complex_key_cache` or `complex_key_ssd_cache` dictionary and waits for the dictionary update now reacts to `KILL QUERY`, and to `max_execution_time` with the default `timeout_overflow_mode = 'throw'`, instead of staying blocked for up to `query_wait_timeout_milliseconds` (60 seconds by default) and then failing with a misleading `TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED` error blaming the source. ### Description `CacheDictionaryUpdateQueue::waitForCurrentUpdateFinish` performed a single `std::condition_variable::wait_for` whose whole budget was `query_wait_timeout_milliseconds` (default 60000), with a predicate that only tested whether the update unit had finished. Nothing on that path consulted the query's cancellation state, so a query cancelled while blocked there stayed blocked until the update finished or the budget expired, then reported `TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED "Dictionary ... source seems unavailable"` - up to 60 seconds late, and blaming the source. Reachable on a stock configuration with any slow or unresponsive source (HTTP, ODBC, executable, another instance). The wait now runs in 100 ms slices against the same total deadline, with a `CurrentThread::checkIfNotCancelled` between slices and once more before the timeout is reported. The deadline is computed once and every slice clamped to the remaining time, so the effective timeout is unchanged. Same shape as the polling waits in `DistributedPlanExecutor` and `StorageQueryRunner::PrefixLatch::waitForAllIssued`. One change covers all four cache layouts and both waiting entry points, `CacheDictionary::getColumns` and `CacheDictionary::hasKeys`. Worst case 600 extra wakeups over a 60 second wait already blocked on network I/O. `CacheDictionary::update` is deliberately untouched. An exception escaping it arms `backoff_end_time`, during which *every* other cache-missing query is refused with `CACHE_DICTIONARY_UPDATE_FAIL` - so cancelling the waiter, not the update, keeps one `KILL QUERY` from becoming a dictionary-wide outage. The abandoned update still completes and populates the cache; the async refresh path (no waiter) is unaffected. **Scope.** This covers cancellation that marks `QueryStatus` via `QueryStatus::cancelQuery`: `KILL QUERY` always does, as does `max_execution_time` with the default `timeout_overflow_mode = 'throw'`. Three cases are not: <details><summary>uncovered cases and why</summary> - `timeout_overflow_mode = 'break'`: the cancellation checker deliberately does not mark the query (it calls `checkTimeLimit`, which only returns false), so the wait still ends at its own dictionary timeout. Returning a partial result from a lookup that never produced one would be a different change. - The native-protocol `Cancel` packet and client disconnect: both set `QueryState::stop_query` in the TCP handler and cancel the pipeline without marking `QueryStatus`, so no `CurrentThread::` primitive can observe them. Pre-existing, and shared by every other `checkIfNotCancelled` call site in the tree. - The update worker's own responsiveness: it runs with no thread group, so the source call still consumes its full retry budget. Making it cancellable requires first deciding what a cancelled update means for the backoff state above. Same boundary as #112144, which covers the other half of this defect class. </details> ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes No documentation change: no setting or syntax is added or altered. An already-documented cancellation mechanism simply now takes effect on this wait.

signal.title: Fix a Keeper server never joining the cluster when background snapshot IO is enabled
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/NuRaft/pull/123 ## Problem With `nuraft_use_bg_thread_for_snapshot_io` enabled, a Keeper server added to the cluster never joins. The leader's catch-up loop waits indefinitely for a response that cannot arrive, so the configuration change is never committed. The setting is off by default, which is why this has gone unnoticed. ## Root cause `sync_log_to_new_srv` builds one of two requests for the joining server — a snapshot request when the peer is below the retained log, or a log-pack `sync_log_request` otherwise — and then dispatches on the snapshot IO mode: ```cpp if (!params->use_bg_thread_for_snapshot_io_) { srv_to_join_->send_req(srv_to_join_, req, ex_resp_handler_); } else { snapshot_io_mgr::instance().invoke(); } ``` Only the *snapshot* branch hands its work to the IO thread. Nothing ever enqueues a log pack with `snapshot_io_mgr` — `create_sync_snapshot_req` is its only producer — so with background snapshot IO on, invoking the thread does not send the log-pack request. It is dropped. Observed on the unfixed build as the new server absent from the cluster configuration and stuck at log index 1 while the leader was at 12. ## Solution Dispatch on what was actually built rather than on the IO mode. The snapshot branch leaves the request null exactly when it has queued the work with the IO thread; in every other case — including the log-pack branch in *both* IO modes — there is a request and it must be sent. Covered by `log_sync_with_async_snapshot_io_test` in NuRaft's `learner_new_joiner_test`, verified to fail against the exact pre-patch code while the four existing tests in that binary keep passing. NuRaft pull request #123 is merged, and the submodule now points at NuRaft's merge commit `2fcee8a` rather than the branch, so the Keeper integration tests, `nightly_keeper` and Jepsen exercise the merged code here. Relative to `master`'s previous pin `dd3d098`, the only NuRaft change this brings in is that fix. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a Keeper server never joining the cluster when `nuraft_use_bg_thread_for_snapshot_io` is enabled: the log batch sent to a joining server was silently dropped, so the membership change never completed. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114275&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114275](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114275+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1659` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Speed up `IN (subquery)` set building by pre-deduplicating each `MergeTree` partition independently
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108326 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105126 The set for `IN (subquery)` is built by a single `CreatingSetsTransform`: all streams of the subquery are merged into one and every row is hashed serially, no matter how many threads read the data. If the partition expression of the subquery's table is a function of the subquery's output columns (the set is keyed on all of them), the reading will now emit each partition through a single port and each stream is deduplicated independently before the filling transform. Because a key then lives in exactly one stream, per-stream deduplication is complete, and the single filling transform only hashes unique rows — the serial part of the build shrinks from all rows to distinct rows, and the deduplication itself runs in parallel. ```sql CREATE TABLE t (a UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple() PARTITION BY a % 8; INSERT INTO t SELECT number % 1000000 FROM numbers(100000000); OPTIMIZE TABLE t FINAL; EXPLAIN PIPELINE SELECT count() FROM numbers(10) WHERE number IN (SELECT a FROM t) SETTINGS allow_creating_set_partitions_independently = 1, max_threads = 8; ``` ```response (CreatingSets) DelayedPorts 9 → 8 (Expression) ExpressionTransform × 8 (Aggregating) Resize 1 → 8 AggregatingTransform (Expression) ExpressionTransform (Filter) FilterTransform (ReadFromSystemNumbers) NumbersRange 0 → 1 (CreatingSet) CreatingSetsTransform <- the single filling transform now hashes ~1M unique rows instead of 100M Resize 8 → 1 DistinctTransform × 8 <- new: parallel pre-deduplication on partition-disjoint streams (Expression) ExpressionTransform × 8 (ReadFromMergeTree) MergeTreeSelect(pool: ReadPoolInOrder, algorithm: InOrder) × 8 0 → 1 <- per-partition reading (8 partitions → 8 streams) ``` On the table above (100M rows, 1M distinct keys, 8 balanced partitions; 64-core machine, average of 3 runs after 2 warm-ups): | query | off | on | speedup | |------------------------------------------------------------|--------|--------|---------| | `SELECT count() FROM numbers(10) WHERE number IN (SELECT a FROM t)` | 0.643s | 0.113s | 5.7× | ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up set building for `IN (subquery)` on partitioned `MergeTree` tables by keeping each partition's rows within a single stream and deduplicating each stream independently, so the single set-filling transform — previously hashing every row serially — only sees unique rows. This applies when the partition expression is a deterministic function of the subquery's output columns. The optimization is not applied when the largest partition holds more than twice the rows of the average partition; the new setting `force_creating_set_partitions_independently` (disabled by default) bypasses this check. Controlled by the new setting `allow_creating_set_partitions_independently` (enabled by default). --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114645&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114645](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114645+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)]

signal.title: More settings to randomize
signal.text: Extends the stateless-test randomizers in `tests/clickhouse-test` with settings added since they were last swept, and pins the tests that were implicitly relying on the old defaults. `SettingsRandomizer`: * Broadens `query_plan_optimize_join_order_algorithm` to cover `dpsub` and `dphyp` (always with `greedy` kept in the fallback chain, since exhausting the chain throws `EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURE_ERROR`), and randomizes `query_plan_optimize_join_order_max_searched_plans`. * Adds ~35 further query-level settings (`LIMIT BY` / `FINAL` / lazy-`FINAL` / runtime-filter / text-index / statistics / regexp-compilation toggles and their numeric companions). * Adds `use_statistics_for_part_pruning` → `use_statistics` and `use_projection_index_in_read_pools` → `optimize_use_projection_filtering` to `conditional_settings`, so a child setting is not enabled while its parent is off. * Randomizes `function_implementation` over the values the server actually supports, probed at startup: it globally filters every `ImplementationSelector`-backed function and each has a different arch-tag set, so a forced value that some function lacks would raise `NO_SUITABLE_FUNCTION_IMPLEMENTATION`. * A few settings are deliberately left commented out with the reason recorded in place, e.g. `use_constant_folding_in_index_analysis` (unsafe per-part min-max prune, and the trigger for https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109893), `correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer`, `min_filtered_ratio_for_lazy_final` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112332) and `max_streams_for_union_step`. `MergeTreeSettingsRandomizer`: * Randomizes `concurrent_part_removal_threshold_for_remote_disk`. * The implicit min-max index settings (`add_minmax_index_for_block_number_column`, `add_minmax_index_for_block_offset_column`, `part_minmax_index_columns`) are explicitly kept out: they are not transparent to queries. The first two add real `MINMAX` skipping indices named `auto_minmax_index__block_number` / `auto_minmax_index__block_offset`, which surface in `SHOW INDEXES`, `system.data_skipping_indices`, part checksums and the `Skip` section of `EXPLAIN indexes = 1`; `part_minmax_index_columns = with_block_number_offset` gives every table a part-level min-max index even with no partition key, so `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` grows an extra `Min-Max / Condition: true` block everywhere. This is the same reason their siblings `add_minmax_index_for_{numeric,string,temporal}_columns` were never randomized — all five are `isReadonlySetting`, i.e. part of the table schema. The rest of the diff pins the affected settings in the stateless tests whose output depends on them. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107586 (fixes the `Invalid binary search result in MergeTreeSetIndex` logical error this randomization made much more likely to be hit; merged, so it is pulled in by the branch update) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109893 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112332 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Running CI a few times before merging. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=106734&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/106734](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F106734+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Hand the connection to the built-in web UI pages over `postMessage`
signal.text: The built-in web UI pages — `/play`, `/docs`, `/dashboard`, `/schema`, `/merges`, `/jemalloc`, `/processors-profile`, `/binary` — take their connection from their own query string, which cannot carry a password: a URL ends up in browser history, `Referer` headers, server access logs and proxy logs. Only `/webterminal` could be handed credentials by the page embedding it, in a `postMessage` message. Every page now speaks that same exchange: ``` page -> host {type: 'clickhouse-hello'} host -> page {type: 'clickhouse-credentials', url, user, password} ``` The page announces itself as soon as it can apply a connection, and the host answers. The page has to speak first because a host that opened it with `window.open` cannot observe when a cross-origin document became ready, and an embedded page would otherwise race its host's `load` handler. Having adopted a connection, each page redoes what it had already loaded with the previous one, so the handover also works when it arrives after the page started querying: `/play` re-probes the credentials, `/docs` rebuilds its cross-link name cache and re-runs the displayed search, `/dashboard` and `/processors-profile` chain their reload behind the load already in flight (two concurrent loads would otherwise duplicate charts, or let a stale failure overwrite a good listing), `/schema` and `/jemalloc` reload, and `/binary` drops its cached tiles and redraws. ## Opening `/docs` from `/play` The Documentation icon in the `/play` sidebar is the first user of the handover. A plain click opens `/docs` through `window.open` — the anchor's `rel=noopener` would sever the handle — and hands the whole connection over, so the documentation search runs against the same server as the same user without the password appearing in a URL. A middle or modifier click keeps the browser's native new-tab handling, which carries `?user=` only, since such a window has no link back to `/play`. ## Security A reply is accepted only from the one window that opened or embeds the page, and only from an exact origin: the page's own, `https://console.clickhouse.cloud`, `https://console.clickhouse-staging.com` or `https://clickhouse.com`. The list is exact rather than a domain suffix on purpose — every ClickHouse Cloud service endpoint is a `*.clickhouse.cloud` host that serves content of its owner's choosing, and a trusted host can aim a page at a server of its own through `url`, which the user may then type credentials into believing it is still their own service. `webterminal.html` gated its own exchange on such a suffix and now uses the same exact list. `url` is optional and defaults to the server the page already points at, but the credentials are replaced wholesale: a message that names only a server cannot attach credentials it did not carry to it, which is what keeps a password filled in by the browser's password manager for this page's origin from following a `url` elsewhere. Outbound, credentials are always sent with an exact target origin, never `'*'`; the readiness announcement carries no secrets, only the fact that the page exists, which its host knows already. Verified in Chromium against a mock endpoint: the `/play` → `/docs` handover, the handover into an iframe for all eight pages, rejection of a handover from an untrusted origin and from a same-origin window that is not the page's host, the wholesale credential replacement, and the exactness of the origin list for all nine pages (`https://myserviceendpoint.clickhouse.cloud`, `https://evil.clickhouse.com`, `http://console.clickhouse.cloud` and `https://console.clickhouse.cloud.evil.com` are all rejected). The committed test asserts that every served page implements both halves of the exchange and that its origin list stayed exact. The protocol is documented in `docs/concepts/features/interfaces/web-ui-embedding.mdx`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The built-in web UI pages (`/play`, `/docs`, `/dashboard`, `/schema`, `/merges`, `/jemalloc`, `/processors-profile`, `/binary`) can now be handed their connection — server URL, user and password — in a `postMessage` message by the page that opened or embedded them, instead of taking it from their own query string, where a password would be recorded in browser history, referrer headers and access logs. `/play` uses this when opening `/docs`, so the documentation search connects to the same server as the same user. A page accepts a connection only from the window that opened or embeds it, and only from an exact list of trusted origins. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115067&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115067](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115067+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Metrics for tracking insertions via materialized view
signal.text: ### Changelog category: - New Feature ### Changelog entry: Added metrics `DirectInsertedRows`, `DirectInsertedBytes`, `MaterializedViewInsertedRows`, and `MaterializedViewInsertedBytes`. ... ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes: I think there are none user-facing changes. At a minimum, the following information should be added (but add more as needed). - Motivation: Why is this function, table engine, etc. useful to ClickHouse users? Sometimes people need to track table's changes via matirialized view. - Example use: A query or command. I used this to check is materialized view metrics work: ```sql CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS test; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS test.random_events; CREATE TABLE test.random_events ( id UUID, user_id UInt64, event_type LowCardinality(String), amount Float64, is_success UInt8, event_time DateTime, payload String ) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY (event_time, user_id); INSERT INTO test.random_events SELECT generateUUIDv4(), rand64() % 1000000, arrayElement(['click', 'view', 'purchase', 'login', 'logout'], 1 + rand() % 5), round(randCanonical() * 1000, 2), rand() % 2, now() - toIntervalSecond(rand() % 86400), concat('random_payload_', toString(rand64())) FROM numbers(1000); ``` ```sql CREATE TABLE test.random_events_hourly_stats ( event_type LowCardinality(String), event_hour DateTime, total_amount Float64, success_count UInt64, fail_count UInt64, event_count UInt64 ) ENGINE = SummingMergeTree ORDER BY (event_type, event_hour); CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW test.mv_hourly_stats TO test.random_events_hourly_stats AS SELECT event_type, toStartOfHour(event_time) AS event_hour, sum(amount) AS total_amount, countIf(is_success = 1) AS success_count, countIf(is_success = 0) AS fail_count, count() AS event_count FROM test.random_events GROUP BY event_type, event_hour; -- Backfill hourly stats INSERT INTO test.random_events_hourly_stats SELECT event_type, toStartOfHour(event_time) AS event_hour, sum(amount) AS total_amount, countIf(is_success = 1) AS success_count, countIf(is_success = 0) AS fail_count, count() AS event_count FROM test.random_events GROUP BY event_type, event_hour; -- Testing results SELECT * FROM test.random_events_hourly_stats ORDER BY event_hour DESC, event_type LIMIT 20; ``` Kinda optional stage: ```sql INSERT INTO test.random_events SELECT generateUUIDv4(), rand64() % 1000000, arrayElement(['click', 'view', 'purchase', 'login', 'logout'], 1 + rand() % 5), round(randCanonical() * 1000, 2), rand() % 2, now() - toIntervalSecond(rand() % 86400), concat('random_payload_', toString(rand64())) FROM numbers(1000000); ``` Checking metrics: ```sql SELECT event, value FROM system.events WHERE (event ILIKE '%InsertedRows') OR (event ILIKE '%InsertedBytes') ORDER BY event; ``` <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110391&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110391](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110391+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Text index written by 26.6 is unreadable by older replicas in the same cluster — breaks rolling upgrades
signal.text: ### Company or project name Nebius ### Describe what's wrong Since 26.6, ClickHouse writes the `text` skip index with sparse index version 1, which no earlier version can read. An older replica that receives such a part through normal replication fails every query that uses the index: ``` Code: 246. DB::Exception: Unsupported version of sparse index (1): While reading part all_0_0_0: While executing MergeTreeSelect(pool: ReadPoolInOrder, algorithm: InOrder). (CORRUPTED_DATA) ``` **This is not a downgrade problem.** It breaks the upgrade itself. During a rolling restart of a replicated cluster, an already-upgraded replica writes parts with a v1 text index, replication delivers them to replicas that have not been restarted yet, and those replicas start failing reads — while both versions are running normally and no data directory has been touched. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes ### How to reproduce Three files and six commands. This runs **one ReplicatedMergeTree cluster with both versions live at the same time** — the state a rolling upgrade passes through. Nothing is downgraded and no data directory is moved. ```bash mkdir ch-textindex && cd ch-textindex cat > keeper.xml <<'EOF' <clickhouse> <listen_host>0.0.0.0</listen_host> <keeper_server> <tcp_port>9181</tcp_port> <server_id>1</server_id> <log_storage_path>/var/lib/clickhouse-keeper/log</log_storage_path> <snapshot_storage_path>/var/lib/clickhouse-keeper/snapshots</snapshot_storage_path> <raft_configuration> <server><id>1</id><hostname>keeper</hostname><port>9234</port></server> </raft_configuration> </keeper_server> </clickhouse> EOF cat > repl.xml <<'EOF' <clickhouse> <zookeeper><node><host>keeper</host><port>9181</port></node></zookeeper> <macros> <shard>1</shard> <replica from_env="REPLICA"/> </macros> </clickhouse> EOF cat > docker-compose.yml <<'EOF' services: keeper: image: clickhouse/clickhouse-keeper:26.6.2.160 volumes: [./keeper.xml:/etc/clickhouse-keeper/keeper_config.xml:ro] old: image: clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3.10.60 environment: {REPLICA: old} volumes: [./repl.xml:/etc/clickhouse-server/config.d/repl.xml:ro] new: image: clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.6.2.160 environment: {REPLICA: new} volumes: [./repl.xml:/etc/clickhouse-server/config.d/repl.xml:ro] EOF docker compose up -d for r in old new; do until docker compose exec -T $r clickhouse-client -q "SELECT 1" >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done; done # 1. the same replicated table on both replicas for r in old new; do docker compose exec -T $r clickhouse-client -q " CREATE TABLE t (id UInt64, s String, INDEX idx s TYPE text(tokenizer = array)) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/1/t', '{replica}') ORDER BY id"; done # 2. write on the already-upgraded replica, let replication carry the part over docker compose exec -T new clickhouse-client -q "INSERT INTO t SELECT number, hex(number) FROM numbers(20000)" docker compose exec -T old clickhouse-client -q "SYSTEM SYNC REPLICA t" # 3. the old replica only fetched that part, it never wrote one docker compose exec -T old clickhouse-client -q "SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS" docker compose exec -T old clickhouse-client -q "SELECT DISTINCT event_type FROM system.part_log WHERE table = 't'" # 4. the same query on each replica docker compose exec -T new clickhouse-client -q "SELECT count() FROM t WHERE s = '3039'" docker compose exec -T old clickhouse-client -q "SELECT count() FROM t WHERE s = '3039'" docker compose down -v ``` Output of the last three steps: ``` DownloadPart <- step 3: fetched, not written locally 1 <- step 4 on the new replica Code: 246. DB::Exception: Unsupported version of sparse index (1): While reading part all_0_0_0: While executing MergeTreeSelect(pool: ReadPoolInOrder, algorithm: InOrder). (CORRUPTED_DATA) <- step 4 on the old replica ``` No special settings are needed — the optimizer chooses the index on its own, which is how we hit it in production. `hasToken(s, '3039')` fails identically. `SELECT count() FROM t` still works, so only queries that touch the index break. [ch-textindex-repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31214857/ch-textindex-repro.zip) ### Expected behavior Either of: 1. A reader that meets a sparse index version it does not understand skips the index and reads the granules, instead of failing the query. Skip indexes are an optimisation; an unreadable one should not be fatal. 2. Failing that, the format bump is called out as backward-incompatible in the changelog with a "drop the text index before upgrading" note, as was done for the 25.12 v3 change in #91518. Currently it is neither: the query fails, and the 26.6 changelog does not mention it. Related: #91518 introduced the sparse-index version header in 25.12 and *was* flagged backward-incompatible. #111550 (open) received review feedback describing this same hazard for a later layout change — *"older binaries misparse new ones, so rolling upgrades/downgrades ... have no safe migration path"* — recommending a versioned reader that migrates or throws an explicit rebuild-required error. The 26.6 bump shipped without either. ### Error message and/or stacktrace _No response_ ### Related issues and pull requests A search for the error text (`"Unsupported version of sparse index"`, `"version of sparse index"`) returns no existing report. - **#91518** — *Inverted Text Index v3* (merged, 25.12). Introduced the version header for the text index sparse index. It was explicitly flagged backward-incompatible, with a changelog note telling users to drop the index before upgrading and rebuild it. The 26.6 bump changes the same field with no equivalent note. - **#111550** — *Text index: introduce new storage layout for positions* (open). Review feedback on it describes this exact hazard for a later layout change: *"older binaries misparse new ones, so rolling upgrades/downgrades on tables that already use `support_phrase_search` have no safe migration path"*, and recommends giving the layout a new persisted version while keeping a reader that either migrates or throws an explicit rebuild-required error. That is the same remedy this issue asks for. - **#103398** — *Upgrade from 25.x to 26.x ends with CORRUPTED_DATA* (closed). The same failure shape in a different subsystem: rolling upgrade of a replicated cluster, error 246, `Unknown version of serialization infos (1). Should be less or equal than 0`. It was resolved by manual intervention (`SYSTEM RESTORE REPLICA`) rather than by making the reader tolerant, so the pattern of a version field that older binaries reject outright is recurring. - **#94494** — *Fix text index mrk file incompatibility* (merged 26.1, backported 25.12.4.32). A different text index format problem (`.mrk` with non-adaptive `index_granularity`, triggered by merges). Listed to distinguish it: it is not this bug. - **#84606** — *Text index: remove multi format versions handling* (merged, July 2025, not-for-changelog). Consolidated `Format::v2` into `v1` and removed multi-version handling. Predates the version header, so it is not the cause, but it is context for how format-version tolerance in this index has been treated. ### Additional context **Workaround** On the not-yet-upgraded replicas, `SETTINGS use_skip_indexes = 0` makes the query succeed; `ALTER TABLE ... DROP INDEX` also works. Both give up the index for the duration. - Reproduced on `clickhouse/clickhouse-server` and `clickhouse/clickhouse-keeper` docker images, linux/aarch64. - Single shard, two replicas, one keeper. Nothing else required.

signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR in OPTIMIZE ... DRY RUN racing a concurrent merge
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107114 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114399 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a `LOGICAL_ERROR` exception (`Temporary part ... already added`) when `OPTIMIZE ... DRY RUN` runs concurrently with a real merge, or with another `DRY RUN`, on the same parts. ### Description `MergeTreeData::optimizeDryRun` executes a real `MergeTask` but, unlike the real optimize/merge paths, takes no `CurrentlyMergingPartsTagger` and no merge lock, so it never registers its source parts as "being merged". A concurrent real merge on the same parts computes the same result part name and reserves the same `tmp_merge_<result>` directory. The second reservation trips `TemporaryParts::add` -> `LOGICAL_ERROR "Temporary part ... already added"`, aborting the server on debug and sanitizer builds. Seen on 17 unrelated PRs over the 30 days to 2026-08-11 (CIDB `default.checks`, 17 rows / 17 distinct PRs), never on master. The dry-run part is throwaway, so its directory need not be named after the result part. It is now `tmp_merge_dry_run_<uuid>`, making the collision impossible on both `MergeTree` and `ReplicatedMergeTree`. A UUID rather than a counter, because the directory can live on storage shared with other servers, where a process-local counter restarts and repeats itself. Leaving the part name out also avoids a length trap: appending a token to it can exceed the 255-byte filename limit while the real merge of the same parts still succeeds. Part names are not length-capped (an all-integral partition key spells its values out, so ten `Int64` fields plus an `IPv4` reach 226 bytes) and `MergeTree` prepends `delete_tmp_` before removal, leaving 8 bytes. The new name has a fixed size. It is never parsed back into a part name and still starts with `tmp_merge_`, which the cleaner and the startup skip logic select by. Only a `dry_run_` suffix takes the new path, so top-level and projection merges keep byte-identical names. Not a duplicate of the `DRY RUN` fix linked above (rows_sources under a soft timeout). Tracking issue: #114399. Test `03823_optimize_dry_run_merge_race` races two `DRY RUN`s on the same parts via a new failpoint pausing after the directory is reserved, at part-name lengths 7, 9 and 226, asserting the real merge succeeds at 226 and each `DRY RUN` really merged. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110916&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110916](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110916+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
